articleTitle: An Efficient Data Collection using Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are an innovative technology that can be used in critical situations such as battlefields as well as commercial applications including buildings, traffic monitoring, smart homes, habitat monitoring, and more. A wireless sensor network (WSN) comprises small nodes capable of wireless sensing, processing, and communication. One of the most pressing concerns plaguing WSNs today is security. This paper suggests and investigates an energy-efficient cluster head (CH) selection approach using the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) (called WOA-Clustering (WOA-C)) and the Geographic and Energy Aware Routing Algorithm (GEAR). As a result, the suggested method simplifies the decision-making process of energy-aware CHs by utilizing the fitness function that assesses node residual energy and the total energy of neighbouring nodes. Compared to the GWO-C, GABEEC, and PSOMSB protocols, the proposed WOA-GEAR protocol consumes 28%, 22%, and 7.5% less power. The suggested algorithm's network lifetime, power efficiency, buffer occupancy, throughput, and end-to-end latency were evaluated.

Author Keywords: Geographic and Energy Aware Routing Algorithm

articleTitle: Leveraging MobileNetV2 for Accurate Detection and Classification of Orange Diseases: A Study on Blackspot, Canker, and Greening Citrus
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this article we examine three main diseases impacting oranges: citrus canker, black spot, and greening citrus. These diseases cause major losses in the citrus industry since they adversely influence the quality and output of orange harvests. Early diagnosis of these diseases is crucial to stop their spread and guarantee the health of the fruit, which is vital for both farmers and the agricultural market, so supporting food security. We addressed this issue using a classification model based on MobileNetV2 architecture with transfer learning. The collection consists in 1164 images divided into four categories: greening citrus, black spot, citrus canker, and healthy oranges. We budget eighty percent for training and twenty percent for testing. Trained and tuned specifically for this task, the MobileNetV2 model generates efficient feature extraction and classification. With a great accuracy of 95%, our model proved effective in separating healthy oranges from those affected by particular diseases. This outcome emphasizes the possibilities of employing transfer learning models for real-time, automated disease detection in orange crops, so providing a useful way to protect crop production and quality and to support sustainable agriculture, economic development, and sensible consumption patterns.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation using Parameter Analysis for massive MIMO Systems using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: mm-Wave and massive MIMO systems have emerged as feasible technologies for strengthening wireless communications performance by deploying numerous antennas at both the transmitter and receiving ends. Optimizing the performance of massive MIMO systems mandates reliable assessment of the channel characteristics. Conventional methods are not suitable for massive MIMO systems because of its complexity and dynamic nature. In this paper, analysis of important parameters for channel estimation in massive MIMO systems, such as antenna orientation and channel magnitude response for OFDM and non-OFDM systems. This paper introduces the Deep massive MIMO generator tool, and it trains the deep learning models based on the input data to estimate the channel parameters more accurately. For analysis, orientation of Base Station antenna done with different angles [(0,0, -45), (0,0, -60),) (0,0, -120)], and BS orientation is based on the signal strength and blockage are considered. And also observed the channel matrix magnitude with different OFDM parameters. The tremendous advantages of parameter analysis by using Deep mMIMO generator is expected to be implemented in intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS), and blockage prediction in massive MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Automotive Powerpoint Based on Adaptive Diversity Preservation Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Multi-objective optimization plays an important role in automotive power train, but there is the problem of inaccurate multi-objective optimization. The traditional ant colony algorithm cannot solve the multi-objective optimization problem in the automotive power train, and the optimization effect is not ideal. Therefore, a multi-objective optimization of automotive power train based on adaptive diversity preservation genetic algorithm is proposed, and the automobile power train is analyzed. Firstly, the evolutionary algorithm and multi-objective optimization theory is used to locate the influencing factors, and the indicators is divided according to the requirements of multi-objective optimization to reduce the interference factors in multi-objective optimization. Then, the evolutionary algorithm and multi-objective optimization theory is used to form an adaptive diversity genetic algorithm for automobile PowerPoint optimization, and the multi-objective optimization results is comprehensively analyzed. The MATLAB simulation results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the adaptive diversity preservation genetic algorithm is superior to the traditional ant colony algorithm in terms of multi-objective optimization accuracy and multi-objective optimization influencing factor time.

Author Keywords: Adaptive genetic algorithm to maintain diversity

articleTitle: Smart Surveillance and Lifeguard Rover with Face Recognition and IoT for Chemical Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This work aims to develop a rover for operations within a petrochemical plant environment. The rover is controlled remotely via the internet using a live video stream and the communications facilitated by the MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) protocol. To enable video streaming, an USB camera is attached to a Raspberry Pi. From the live streaming, presence of any humans inside the plant is detected using the Haar-cascade face detection algorithm running on Raspberry Pi. The Telebit and Flask are employed for displaying the video captured by the rover on a webpage. Real-time control and sensor data visualization are achieved through a secure webpage hosted on a personal server, ensuring enhanced security measures. User authentication is implemented to ensure authorized access to the webpage. The webpage, hosted on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) - Virtual Private Server (VPS), provides comprehensive control and monitoring capabilities for the rover within the petrochemical plant environment. This research addresses the need for an internet-controlled rover that can operate in hazardous environments, such as petrochemical plants, with the aim of enhancing safety and efficiency in industrial operations.

articleTitle: The Application of Image Recognition Algorithm in Intelligent Monitoring of Herringbone Gate Closure Of Ship Lock
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: During the operation of the lock, there is a relative displacement between the herringbone gate shaft and the door leaf, and the traditional manual measurement method has a large workload and low accuracy, and the problem cannot be found in time. In the process of using the traditional way of measurement, due to the influence of environment, human and other factors, it is difficult to ensure the accuracy of the measurement results, and the efficiency of manual re-inspection in the later stage is low, and a lot of manpower and material resources are required. The intelligent monitoring system for the final alignment of the herringbone gate gate gate based on computer vision realizes the rapid measurement of key parameters such as the position and angle of the door leaf through real-time image recognition and analysis of the door leaf, and compares the image recognition result with the door leaf displacement curve, so as to provide accurate and timely data support for the operation and management of the lock. Ship crossing is a complex physical process, with multiple complex factors such as ships, locks, and waterways. The alignment of the lock under the herringbone door is mainly achieved by measuring the relative position between the lock door leaf and the door leaf when the ship passes through the gate. Due to the great influence of external factors, such as the violent shaking or collision of the ship during navigation, the measurement results are prone to deviation. Therefore, it is of great significance to study the intelligent monitoring system of herringbone gate closing and final alignment of ship locks. In this paper, based on the image recognition technology, the alignment of the lock door leaves under the herringbone door is studied, and the real-time monitoring of the alignment of the lock door leaves under the herringbone door is realized by using the image recognition algorithm, and an image recognition algorithm based on multi-feature fusion is proposed.

Author Keywords: herringbone gate gate closure of ship lock

articleTitle: Leaf Detectives: A Deep Learning Approach to Grapevine Varietal Identification with DenseNet-121
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Effective viticulture depends on accurate identification of grapevine leaves, which shapes vine care and grape quality. This article presents a novel automated approach for grapevine leaf categorization utilizing DenseNet-121, a state-of-the-art convolutional neural network distinguished for image recognition performance. Essential for the wine and fruit sectors, grapevines (Vitis vinifera) show a variety of leaf traits vital for precise varietal identification. These leaves require an effective automated solution since manual classification of them is labor-intensive and prone to mistakes. In this work, we classify five different types of high-resolution grapevine leaf photos from a dataset: Ak, Ala Idris, Buzgulu, Dimnit, and Nazli. Resized to 256x256 pixels, the photos are handled to produce a batch size of 32 and a classification accuracy of 96%. There are five main parts to the approach: analysis; model architecture construction; preprocessing and dataset collecting; model training and evaluation. Resizing and normalizing photos helps the Kaggle-derived dataset to be pre-processed so standardizing inputs. DenseNet-121 is chosen for its effective feature extraction and dense connection; its design is modified for the classification purpose by changing the last layer. To improve model generalization, training comprises categorical cross-entropy loss, the Adam optimizer, and data augmentation methods. Validation and test datasets help to evaluate performance; metrics including accuracy and F1-score direct model improvement. The findings confirm that DenseNet-121 greatly increases grapevine leaf identification accuracy and efficiency, hence lowering manual labor and raising classification consistency. This work provides important new perspectives for next developments in precision agriculture and highlights the possibilities of deep learning technology in viticulture.

articleTitle: Effect of Different Oversampling Techniques to Handle Class Imbalance Challenges in Coronary Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: CHD or Coronary Heart Disease has a considerable influence on global mortality rate, hence ahead of time and precise prediction is crucial for prompt treatment and avoid patient deaths. However, predicting CHD is difficult since the dataset is skewed. To address this challenge, several oversampling techniques are proposed, including Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), random oversampling, and Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN). Incorporating these strategies lowers classifier predisposition towards the majority group while emphasizing proper knowledge of minority notions. Most algorithms perform better on balanced data rather than imbalanced data.This article tests six machine learning models using the CDG dataset. Because this is an imbalanced data problem, accuracy is not used as the primary metric. F1-score is the primary metric. The Extra Trees Classifier achieves an F1-score of 95% by employing random oversampling techniques. F1-score, accuracy, precision, Matthews Correlation Coefficient(MCC) and recall are used for measuring the performance of each algorithm.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Forecasting using Ensemble Machine Learning Models–A Case Study Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Precise load forecasting of energy demand resulting in minimal / negligible variations in real-time load curve is crucial for effective operation and planning of utility companies. The prediction further allows efficient energy storage and it could provide useful information to make decisions on energy generation and purchase. Machine learning algorithms are one of the best accurate algorithms used in prediction. In this research work we implemented the ensemble methods, which are Ada Boost Regression (AdB), Gradient Boosted Regression (GBR), and Extreme Gradient Boosting Regression (XGB) were used to predict the energy consumption. The outputs of these models were evaluated to see which one provides the best energy prediction performance. The outputs indicate that simple ensemble learning techniques such as averaging expected results could help enhance prediction models. The results of these algorithms are compared with Root mean square (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE).

articleTitle: Real-Time IoT Data Analytics Using Advanced Large Language Model Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies with advanced analytics has become critical in extracting valuable insights from continuous data streams in real-time. This paper explores the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) as a transformative approach to enhancing IoT data analytics. We present a novel framework that leverages LLMs for the real-time interpretation and processing of vast, diverse IoT data sets. Our methodology involves the adaptation of transformer-based architectures to handle structured and unstructured data from IoT sources, enabling immediate decision-making and actionable insights. Through rigorous experimentation, we demonstrate how LLMs can significantly improve the accuracy and speed of data analytics in IoT environments compared to traditional methods. The results underscore the potential of LLMs to revolutionize real-time data processing tasks across various industries, from smart cities to healthcare. Our study not only reinforces the applicability of LLMs in real-time analytics but also outlines future research directions for integrating AI with IoT infrastructure to achieve scalable and efficient solutions.

articleTitle: A Novel Hierarchical Algorithm for Securing Distributed Networks Against Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Cyber attacks are a significant threat to the security and balance of disbursed networks due to the increasing reliance on generation. Traditional safety procedures, including firewalls and intrusion detection, are now not sufficient to prevent and counter these attacks correctly. Therefore, there is a want for a novel hierarchical set of rules which can deal with the complicated and continuously evolving nature of cyber attacks. The proposed algorithm utilizes a hierarchical shape that allows efficient detection and response to a variety of assaults. At the top stage, a centralized control gadget monitors the activities and visitors of the whole network. This device then communicates with decentralized nodes on the decrease level, which are accountable for detecting and mitigating attacks in their respective regions.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach to Soil Classification: Feature Extraction with VGG16 and SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research presents an efficient soil classification approach using a hybrid model that combines the VGG16 deep learning architecture with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. The VGG16 model, pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset, is utilized for feature extraction, while the SVM classifier is employed for final classification of soil types. The dataset consists of labelled soil images categorized into different types, such as clay, alluvial, black, and red soils. To enhance model generalization and avoid overfitting, data augmentation techniques were applied during preprocessing. The hybrid model is evaluated on training and validation datasets, demonstrating strong performance with validation accuracy peaking at 97.73%. The results indicate that the VGG16+SVM model effectively leverages deep learning for feature extraction and machine learning for classification, offering a robust solution for soil classification tasks. This approach can be extended to other classification problems, providing potential applications in agriculture and environmental monitoring. Future work may explore further enhancements by fine-tuning the SVM classifier or employing advanced feature extraction methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Delta-Sigma Modulator using Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Delta sigma modulation (DSM) is a prominent technique in both analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) and digital-to-analog conversion (DAC), known for its ability to achieve high resolution and dynamic range while maintaining low power consumption. This paper introduces a novel implementation of delta sigma ADC and DAC converters aimed at enhancing high-resolution analog signal processing applications. Leveraging advanced delta sigma modulation techniques, the design and implementation of the converters are outlined, emphasizing oversampling, noise shaping, and decimation strategies to achieve superior performance. The ADC stage employs delta sigma modulation to encode analog signals into high-resolution digital format while mitigating quantization noise through noise shaping techniques. Following the ADC stage, the paper explores the reconstruction process in the DAC stage, focusing on inverse delta sigma modulation techniques to faithfully reconstruct the analog signal from digital data. Design considerations such as digital filter design, quantization error compensation, and signal-to-noise ratio optimization are addressed to ensure accurate signal reconstruction. Results highlight significant improvements in signal fidelity and noise reduction compared to conventional ADC-DAC systems. This work represents significant advancements in high-resolution analog signal processing systems, promising enhanced performance and reliability in various real-world applications including telecommunications, audio processing, and sensor interfaces.

articleTitle: FPGA Accelerated Gradient Analysis for Brain Tumours Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Real-time image processing demands rapid analysis of extensive data. This system for tumour characterisation uses high-resolution MRI datasets. The system leverages the parallel processing capabilities of FPGAs to perform real-time edge detection using a modified Sobel operator. A novel self-checking test bench was developed to validate the accuracy of FPGA results against C program results, ensuring robust performance. The proposed method was tested on a diverse set of tumour images, demonstrating enhanced edge clarity and reduced noise. This work contributes to the advancement of biomedical imaging, offering a scalable and efficient solution for real-time tumour characterization. Future work will explore the integration of machine learning techniques and adaptation to other imaging modalities.

articleTitle: Object Detection and Classification from Hyper Spectral Images Using Adaptive Gaussian and Probabilistic Based K-Nearest Neighbour Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Hyper Spectral Imagery (HSI) analysis plays a crucial role in remote sensing applications, such as object detection, identification and classification. Due to the complexity of HSI data, advanced analytical methods are required to produce accurate classification maps. A key research challenge in classification using HSI images is designing better algorithms with good efficiency capable of classifying the images captured by HSI techniques into various land cover types with precision. Processing the high dimensions of data, and class imbalance pose significant challenges. To address these issues, this research proposes a novel HSI classification model that integrates two methods – Principal Component Analysis for spectral based feature selection and a modified version of Gaussian-based method for enhancement of the features, and probabilistic model optimization for KNN classification. The main aim of the proposed method is to balance the tradeoff between accuracy and data loss in preprocessing by making use of both spatial and spectral features extraction and enhancement techniques.

articleTitle: Remote Monitoring of Live EEG of Epileptic Patients on New Radio (5G) Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Delays in diagnosing neurological disorders can seriously affect a patient’s vitals in a critical care setting. Brain electrical activity (EEG) recordings are frequently used for neurological condition monitoring and diagnosis. EEG signal analysis requires a neurologist. Nevertheless, this knowledge is frequently unavailable on-site. When offsite expert analysis is needed, a new radio (5G) based monitoring system for EEG data is presented, which can minimize delays. The system makes it possible to view EEG data while it is being acquired in real time by streaming it to a remote location. An ever-updating view of the complete EEG recording can be obtained by reviewing previously streamed data. New Radio (5G) technology is used for all communications. The only device needed to view EEG data is a 5G smartphone with the installed plugin.

articleTitle: Proactive Preterm Labor Prediction Using Ptl-Simple RNN Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Preterm labour presents a substantial obstacle in nature of obstetrics, requiring precise prediction models for prompt intervention. Utilizing deep learning, particularly simple RNN, presents encouraging opportunities for making such predictions. Simple RNN models are highly effective in capturing sequential dependencies, which is essential for studying temporal patterns in risk variables associated with premature labour. Simple RNN models may detect minor connections that indicate the start of premature labour by integrating several information sources, such as maternal health records, genetic predispositions, and environmental variables. Their ability to analyze time-series data allows for dynamic risk evaluation, resulting in improved early warning systems. In addition, Simple-RNN models can adjust to changing patient profiles, ensuring that customized risk assessment also provides higher accuracy. Simple RNN-based prediction models have great promise to reduce the effect of preterm labour by allowing preventative treatments and enhancing perinatal outcomes. This research realize this potential through ongoing improvement and integration with clinical practice.

articleTitle: Using neural networks for classification of COVID-19 cases
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Neural nets are three-dimensional meshes of neurons modeled after the brain. They are also called "connectionist" models because they are a vast collection of randomly interconnected elements. Attempts to program neural nets oftentimes yield limitless and unpredictable outcomes that seem to display intelligence. In this paper, the author use neural networks for the classification of COVID-19 cases. Neural networks are biologically inspired, with multiple layers that are densely interconnected units. The author compare COVID-19 cases by looking into CT scan reports. CT scan reports are interpreted by reading a few images and matching with the three-dimensional medical scans. Incidentally, these images have to be read with no change in the healthcare and diagnostics industries. The findings indicate that DenseNet-121 renders the best results for this classification problem.

articleTitle: Efficient Prostate Tissue Classification with MobileNetV2: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper represents a comparative analysis of the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), which is applied to the prostate tissue classification, pinpointing an overall accuracy of 71.79%. The study rigorously identifies multiple CNN architectures, with the focus on the MobileNetV2, to assess their efficacy in differentiating among the four categories: Benign, [Malignant] Pre-B, [Malignant] Pro-B, and [Malignant] early Pre-B. The results represent that while MobileNetV2 attains a balance between computational productivity and performance, it exhibits strengths in benign and early malignant tissue classification. However, the model undergoes challenges in accurately distinguishing between certain malignant stages, such as [Malignant] Pre-B and [Malignant] Pro-B. These results underscore the potential of CNNs in the classification of medical images but also point to the prerequisite for the further optimization and the enhancement. Future research should emphasize on finetuning architecture, incorporating the advanced data augmentation techniques, and analysing techniques to improve the classification accuracy and broadening in prostate tissue diagnosis.

articleTitle: Backbone PV Curve and Improved Genetic Algorithm for Energy Storage Site Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Energy storage site selection and volumetric research play an important role in energy storage system, but there is the problem of inaccurate volumetric analysis. The traditional particle swarm algorithm cannot solve the problem of site selection and capacity determination in energy storage system, and the capacity setting effect is not ideal. Therefore, this paper proposes research on energy storage site selection and capacity based on PV curve and improved genetic algorithm, and analyzes the energy storage site selection and capacity research. Firstly, natural selection and genetic theory is used to locate the influencing factors, and the indicators is divided according to the requirements of energy storage site selection and volumetric research, so as to reduce the interference factors in energy storage site selection and volumetric research. Then, natural selection and genetic theory is used to form PV curves and improve the genetic algorithm for energy storage site selection and volumetric research, and the results of energy storage site selection and volumetric determination is comprehensively analyzed. The MATLAB simulation results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the PV curve and improved genetic algorithm is superior to the traditional particle swarm algorithm in terms of the accuracy of energy storage site selection and volumetric research, and the time of influencing factors of energy storage siting and volumetric research.

articleTitle: Area-efficient Architecture of PRINCE Cipher for Resource-constrained Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The broad adoption of ubiquitous computing devices has increased security vulnerabilities in the Internet of Things (IoT) field. IoT nodes and RFID devices are secured using the lightweight cryptographic block cipher. The paper offers an area-optimized serial design for the lightweight PRINCE block cipher that makes use of the Shift Register Look-up table (SLR16) register. The proposed architecture has been accomplished or implemented using Hardware Description Language (HDL) in Verilog. The proposed design uses a 16-bit datapath to generate ciphertext in forty clock cycles. Area, throughput, efficiency, and power are among the performance metrics examined in the Virtex series, Spartan-3, and Spartan-6 Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). On Spartan-6, the suggested design used 46 slices, had a throughput of 282.94 Mbps, and an efficiency of 6.15 Mbps per slice, and can be beneficial for low-constraint applications.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-B7 for Real-Time Optical Character Recognition in Diverse Text Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) system based on the EfficientNet-B7 model, designed to improve text recognition accuracy and efficiency. Using the OCR dataset, which includes a wide variety of printed and handwritten text images with different fonts, sizes, orientations, and noise levels, the model leverages EfficientNet-B7’s compound scaling to balance computational complexity with performance. By employing transfer learning from ImageNet pre-trained weights, the system accelerates convergence while maintaining high generalization across unseen data. Advanced data augmentation techniques, such as random rotations, brightness adjustments, and cropping, are applied during preprocessing to enhance the model’s robustness. The system achieves a validation accuracy of 93.22%, significantly outperforming traditional OCR methods. Additionally, hyperparameter tuning using metaheuristic optimization further refines the model, ensuring optimal performance in terms of accuracy and loss reduction. The system’s scalability and efficiency make it suitable for real-time OCR applications in industries like healthcare, finance, and education, where precise text recognition is essential. Future research will focus on extending the model to support multi-lingual OCR and incorporating attention mechanisms to handle more complex text layouts and structures.

articleTitle: Securing Digital Images with Triple Watermarks: An Integer Wavelet Transform Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of digital media, protecting digital images through watermarking techniques is paramount. This research offers a digital image watermarking method using Integer Wavelet Transform (IWT). The host image is converted to gray scale and decomposed into subbands. Three different binarized watermark images are embedded into the horizontal subband (CH), vertical subband (CV) and diagonal subband (CD) by converting watermark bits to decimal numbers and adjusting pixel values. Inverse IWT is used to recreate the watermarked image. For watermark extraction, the reverse process is applied to retrieve the embedded information from the watermarked image. The scheme demonstrates outstanding performance when embedding a 256×256 size image, it achieves a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of around 52 dB in the CD subband, approximately 48 dB in the CH and CD subbands, and around 46 dB when embedded across the CH, CV, and CD subbands. The efficacy of the suggested technique in terms of image quality and watermark extraction accuracy is also determined by experimental findings, with comprehensive performance evaluations under various attacks. The proposed method shows potential for robust image authentication and copyright protection in digital media applications.

articleTitle: Cross-Domain Cybersecurity: Integrated Intrusion Detection Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study presents a cross-domain cybersecurity strategy that includes a sophisticated intrusion detection system (IDS) positioned strategically at the default gateway of Healthcare Systems and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) infrastructures. The suggested model combines a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architecture and incorporates a simulated XGBoost layer to improve predicting accuracy. The CNN-GRU model is designed to extract intricate spatial and temporal characteristics. The CNN component focuses on collecting local patterns, while the GRU component is responsible for addressing sequential dependencies. The outputs are merged with the original input features to create a comprehensive collection of features. This set is then passed through dense layers that simulate the capabilities of XGBoost for the final prediction. This ensemble methodology utilizes deep learning and gradient boosting to enhance accuracy and resilience in classification tasks. The framework prioritizes the processing of data in real-time, guaranteeing the integrity of the system and enabling swift detection of threats. The effectiveness of the model can be measured by its packet processing rate, which demonstrates its performance under different workloads. Our Intrusion Detection System (IDS) establishes a higher benchmark for proactive and dynamic defense, offering strong safeguarding capabilities for healthcare, IIoT, and general networks. It continuously adjusts to changing cyber threats in order to ensure the security of key infrastructure.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of the Comprehensive Evaluation Method Based on The Dtw Algorithm in the Post-Evaluation of the Power Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: There is a problem with incorrect performance placement in the application study that occurs after the power distribution network assessment, which is a vital part of the complete evaluation process. In a thorough assessment approach, the phase limit is an obstacle that the conventional Associative rule mining algorithm cannot overcome, leading to inadequate results. The outcome is an assessment of the comprehensive evaluation technique's application to the post-evaluation of distribution networks and the provision of an evaluation method based on the DTW algorithm. Starting with the application study in the post-evaluation of power distribution network's needs to decrease interference factors, the indicators are split according to the excavate theory, which is used to discover the influencing elements. Next, we use the underlying theory to develop a DTW algorithm application study for a power distribution network design that has undergone post-evaluation. We then carefully analyze the results of this research. When comparing the two algorithms for post-evaluation power distribution network accuracy and time of influencing factors, the DTW approach performs better than the conventional Associative rule mining technique, according to the MATLAB simulation findings.

articleTitle: Enhanced Blood Cell Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Accurate Diagnosis of Haematological Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Among haematological illnesses whose diagnosis and treatment depend critically on blood cell classification. Early discovery, good treatment planning, and monitoring of disease development all depend on accurate identification of blood cell types—especially malignant cells. We provide a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) model in this work to categorize blood cells into four categories: Benign, Malignant_Pre-B, Malignant_Pro-B, and Malignant_Early_Pre-B. With a 3,242-image collection taken from Kaggle, our model shows quite remarkable overall accuracy of 98%. Particularly for the Malignant_Pre-B class, the proposed CNN architecture—which comprises of well-adjusted hyper parameters and network layers—effectively captures specific features across the several cell types, so producing good precision and recall metrics. The robustness and generalizing capability of the model are confirmed by a thorough investigation covering training and validation accuracy, loss curves, and a confusion matrix. This work emphasizes how CNNs can automatically recognize blood cells, hence enhancing clinical diagnosis speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Battery Management System for Pure Electric Vehicles Based on Lin Bus
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In view of the limitations of the traditional Huffman coding algorithm in the design of battery management system for pure electric vehicles, a design scheme of battery management system based on LIN bus was proposed. Firstly, the influencing factors is accurately located through the serial communication theory, and the indicators is reasonably divided to reduce interference, and the LIN bus is used to construct the battery management system design scheme. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the proposed scheme is superior to the traditional Huffman coding algorithm in terms of battery management system design accuracy and processing time of influencing factors, and has obvious advantages. The design of battery management system plays an extremely important role in pure electric vehicles, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth characteristics and product generation of pure electric vehicles. However, the traditional Huffman coding algorithm has certain limitations in solving management system simulation problems, especially when dealing with complex problems. In this paper, a battery management system design scheme based on LIN bus is proposed to better solve this problem. In this scheme, the influencing factors is accurately located through the serial communication theory, so as to determine the division of indicators, and the LIN bus is used to construct the scheme. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the accuracy and speed of the scheme is significantly improved for different problems, and it has better performance. Therefore, the LIN bus-based simulation scheme in the design of battery management system for pure electric vehicles can better solve the limitations of the traditional Huffman coding algorithm and improve the simulation accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Novel AES Algorithm Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the digital communication era, data security is of paramount importance. To address the associated risks, various cryptographic algorithms have been developed to protect against side-channel attacks during data transmission between sender and receiver. Among these, the AES algorithm is a widely used cryptographic technique that ensures data sent from the sender is securely encrypted and processed through multiple stages, making it challenging for unauthorized users to decrypt the information intended for the receiver. This study presents a novel mixed column operation design that not only improves efficiency in terms of power, area, and timing parameters but also increases the size of the encrypted text. This enhancement reduces the decryption process to a brute-force approach, relying on trial and error for cryptanalytic attackers. The simulations were carried out using EDA Playground, with synthesis performed using the Cadence Genus Tool in a 45nm technology environment.

articleTitle: DetectBERT: Code Vulnerability Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: DetectBERT is a deep learning approach for identifying vulnerabilities in source code at the statement level. Utilizing transformer encoder models extracts features and learns complex relationships without predefined graph structures. DetectBERT addresses data distribution challenges using real-world code and normalizing user-defined names. Demonstrated effectiveness in Python using public datasets like CVEFixes and VUDENC, DetectBERT offers scalable, robust, and granular vulnerability detection.

articleTitle: MobileNetV2-SVM Hybrid Model Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy effected Human Eye
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the realm of medical diagnostics, particularly in the ophthalmology sector, Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) stands as a formidable challenge. DR, a condition that can lead to blindness if not diagnosed and treated early. Traditional approaches, heavily reliant on the meticulous examination of fundus photographs by seasoned clinicians, are not only time-intensive but are also prone to inconsistencies due to subjective interpretations. Researchers have pioneered a novel method merging MobileNetV2 and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to enhance DR severity classification. Traditional DR diagnosis methods fall short due to their heavy reliance on large datasets and substantial computational power, often unfeasible in mobile settings. The innovative approach utilizes MobileNetV2 for its compact, efficient design, optimized for mobile applications through depthwise separable convolutions, paired with the accuracy and robustness of SVM. This hybrid model, trained on the enriched APTOS 2019 dataset through data augmentation and resampling, addresses the challenges of data scarcity and computational demands. Remarkably, it achieved over 90% accuracy in classifying DR severity, marking a significant leap in ophthalmic diagnostics. This model not only streamlines DR screening but also makes it accessible and scalable, potentially reducing vision loss risk for millions, demonstrating a groundbreaking advancement in leveraging machine learning for healthcare.

articleTitle: Frameworks for Investigating the Relationship Between Traffic Control and Emission Control Using Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This Framework for Using Optimization Strategies to Look into the Connection Between Traffic Control and Emission Control There is a system that shows the groups that are part of DD and how they share information. Researchers often do systematic literature studies to find and rate all the papers that have been written on a certain subject. This study paper talks about a way to improve microgrid power supply by using swarm intelligence and mixed energy sources together. Microgrid integration is growing quickly, and so is the number of microgrids being added to the low-voltage (LV) power system. Because there are more DG sources, an islanded microgrid would run into a number of problems during the process. The idea can help with the problems of integrating green energy sources and managing microgrids. The goal of this study is to improve the performance and economy of a microgrid by adding several voltage controls. The results of these controls will be looked at and studied. MATLAB/Simulink Sim Power Systems will also be used to test the performance of the controls. There are some problems with the safety zone and working speed of the low voltage (LV) microgrid that need to be fixed before the microgrid can be used. These problems can be fixed by making a good converter that follows the future-ride-through (FRT) rules explained in the suggested study.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Wireless Power Bank
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The proposed wireless charging system functions without the need for communication wires, providing convenient charging for smart devices within a short range without cables or precise positioning. This innovative system utilizes solar cells as an alternative energy source, contributing to the prolonged lifespan of devices. The environmentally friendly and user-friendly technology incorporates a "receiver pad," ensuring wireless compatibility for all mobile devices and enabling smartphone charging anytime and anywhere. The wireless power transmission concept specifically targets the need for extended battery life, particularly in situations where power outlets are not readily available.

articleTitle: Analysis of MEMS Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor with Dual-Island Structures using Circular Silicon Diaphragm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The purpose of the work present the development and proposal of pressure sensors for microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). This work covers the design and testing of the sensor. MEMS pressure sensors are engineered to cater to a broad spectrum of pressure demands which includes high sensitivity, with the help of the theory of elasticity and circular diaphragm mechanism parameters like stress, strain and deflection are obtained, with help of the COMSOL Multiphysics software. With the help of the software, visualizing the estimated parameters in great detail is attainable and it backs up the theory used as well. A pressure sensor having a beam-membrane-dual-island with piezoresistive construction is created that fulfils the purpose of measuring micro-pressure which have high sensitivity and resistance to overload. A unique construction that blends beams with sensitive nature with a traditional bossed diagram, is used to analyse stress distribution with the help of the finite element approach (FEA). 5MPa pressure is applied to observe the outcome provided by pressure sensor when applied on island structure.

articleTitle: Power Prediction and Regulation of Photovoltaic Power Generation System Based on Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In view of the limitations of the traditional Fibonacci sequence algorithm in the power prediction and regulation of photovoltaic power generation system, a power prediction and adjustment scheme based on Kalman filter is proposed. Firstly, the influencing factors is accurately located through the linear system state theory, and the indicators is reasonably divided to reduce interference, and the power prediction and adjustment scheme is constructed by using Kalman filter. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the proposed scheme is superior to the traditional Fibonacci algorithm in terms of power prediction and adjustment accuracy, and processing time of influencing factors, and has obvious advantages. Power prediction and regulation plays an extremely important role in photovoltaic power generation systems, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth characteristics and product generation of photovoltaic power generation systems. However, the traditional Fibonacci algorithm has some limitations in solving the power simulation problem of power generation system, especially when dealing with complex problems. In this paper, a power prediction and regulation scheme based on Kalman filter is proposed to better solve this problem. In this scheme, the influencing factors is accurately located through the linear system state theory, so as to determine the division of indicators, and the scheme is constructed by using Kalman filter. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the accuracy and speed of the scheme is significantly improved for different problems, and it has better performance. Therefore, the simulation scheme based on Kalman filter in the power prediction and regulation of photovoltaic power generation system can better solve the limitations of the traditional Fibonacci sequence algorithm and improve the simulation accuracy and efficiency.

Author Keywords: Theory of state of linear systems

articleTitle: Cheque Information Processing and Validation using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Understanding document images, such as invoices, is a difficult task. It necessitates reading the text as well as comprehending the document’s general structure. Conventional techniques first extract text using Optical Character Recognition (OCR), yet this method has drawbacks. In addition to being computationally costly, OCR can have trouble converting between various languages and document formats and introduce errors that can compound throughout the analysis process.Donut is an OCR-free VDU (Visual Document Understanding) model that challenges this paradigm. It does not even bother with the text extraction stage; it analyzes the document image straight. This creative strategy produces notable advancements. Donut performs at the cutting edge, which means it is quick and precise. This is a significant development in the realm of visual document understanding since it enables Donut to handle a greater variety of languages and document types. The model has been tested using BLEU scores and ROUGE scores over 3 parameters namely – payee name, amount in words and amount in figure. The model has also been tested over variety of sample sizes ranging from 50 to 1000.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Enhanced Brain Tumor Classification Using VGG19, LSTM, and SVM Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Brain tumors are an important worldwide health issue, contributing to high rates of morbidity and mortality. Their early detection is vital for enhancing patient outcomes; yet, it remains a tough undertaking despite ongoing improvements in medical technology. This research offers a unique hybrid Deep Learning model aiming at enhancing the efficiency of brain tumor categorization. The model incorporates the characteristics of VGG19 for the feature extraction process, LSTM for understanding temporal correlations, and SVM for accurate classification. The dataset utilized for training and evaluation consists of 7023 MRI images sourced from three independent datasets: Figshare, SARTAJ, and Br35H. An important enhancement includes rectifying misclassifications in the glioma category by replacing mislabeled SARTAJ photos with appropriately classified images from Figshare. The suggested model's performance is tested using numerous measures, including Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and Accuracy. The results obtained by the model have a classification accuracy of 97%, making it highly useful for brain tumor detection and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Visualizing various Electroencephalogram signal components in case of different brain conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, renowned for their ability to unveil the dynamic workings of the human brain, serve as an invaluable resource in deciphering an array of neurological conditions. This research endeavors to conduct an exhaustive visual analysis of EEG signal components, employing advanced signal processing techniques and visualization methodologies. Our primary aim is to delineate the distinct patterns of brain wave activity associated with a spectrum of neurological conditions, encompassing ’Healthy control’, ’Depressive disorder’, ’Bipolar disorder’, ’Panic disorder’, ’Social anxiety disorder’, ’Alcohol use disorder’, ’Behavioral addiction disorder’, ’Post Ttraumatic Stress Disorder’ (PTSD), ’Acute stress disorder’(ASD), and ’Adjustment disorder’. Through meticulous examination of these visual representations, our goal is to deepen our understanding of the underlying neurophysiological mechanisms characterizing these conditions. Although it is very difficult to visualize the EEG signals, even of the already preprocessed EEG signals, but still the paper visualizes diverse brain conditions according to the lobes of the brain. Different frequency components affect the different brain lobes in different conditions. We have used Minimum Norm Estimation (MNE) library of Python, which is designed exclusively for visualizing various Magnetoencephalogram (MEG) and Electroencephalogram (EEG) Signals of the brain.

articleTitle: Passive energy-Saving Design Optimization of Buildings Based on Watershed and U-Net Model Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Building energy conservation is valued by many countries today, in the construction process, materials, planning, design, etc. should be used reasonably and maximally to improve resource utilization, among which passive building energy saving is a very important method. Traditional design methods cannot solve the complex problems of passive building energy efficiency. Therefore, this paper proposes a watershed and U-net model algorithm to analyze the energy saving of passive buildings for innovation and entrepreneurship. Firstly, the computer is used to optimize and analyze the passive energy-saving design of the building, and the indicators are divided according to the energy-saving requirements of the passive building to reduce it Interference factors in passive building energy efficiency. Then, the computer designs the passive building energy saving results to form the passive building energy saving scheme, and carries out the passive building energy saving results Comprehensive analysis. MATLAB simulation shows that under certain evaluation criteria, watershed and U-net model algorithms have an impact on building energy efficiency The feasibility of passive building energy-saving design and the rationality of passive building energy-saving are better than traditional design methods.

articleTitle: Improve The Efficiency and Code Quality Using A Framework Based On Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The primary objective of utilizing recommendation frameworks is to pick up the efficiency of the designer by prescribing documents to alter. articleTitle: Enhancing Software Fault Prediction with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study on the PC1 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Software makes the world go faster in the modern world, software is everywhere and vital to economy (and environment, education etc.) The dependency on these technology has proliferated, and software systems have become more complex. Traditional statistical approaches like Logistic Regression and Decision Tree have been utilized for RTL-based software defect prediction but they are outdated regarding the nuances of recent research demands. This work investigates whether machine learning approaches can help to advance software defect prediction by employing the PC1 dataset from PROMISE repository. The performance of Logistic regression and Decision tree is compared on MAPE, explained variance, Precision G measure F-measure AUC Accuracy. The results that can be seen in the above ROC charts suggest Logistic Regression does better on AUC and accuracy, but Decision Tree has a more balanced trade off between Recall an Precision. This research contributes to the field of software reliability engineering by applying state-fo-the-art machine learning methods in order to provide new method and insights toward improved accuracy and precision for detection / prediction of software faults.

articleTitle: Detection of Floating Waste on Water Bodies
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper outlines the general approach used for detection and monitoring of aqua-floating waste using satellite imagery and aerial photography from a drone, in-situ sensors and machine learning algorithms. Hence, by specifying the waste types and increasing the accuracy in wastes identification, the cleaner aquatic environments and the better waste management based on the system’s scalability and applicability to the global scale will be contributed.

articleTitle: Fusion of CNN and LSTM Models for Enhanced Gait Swing Phase Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a CNN-LSTM hybrid model intended for precise recognition of gait swing phases, explicitly focusing on initial swing, mid swing, and terminal swing. Gait analysis plays an important part in different fields including medical care and biomechanics, offering experiences in motion functions and supporting rehabilitation techniques. The proposed model incorporates a innovative approach of Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for feature extraction from gait successions and long short-term Memory networks (LSTMs) for catching temporal conditions inside each swing stage. After processing the sequential gait data, the CNN component extracts hierarchical features that emphasize spatial patterns important for differentiating between swing phases. These features are then used to feed into layers of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, which simulate the temporal dynamics present in human gait and allow the system to accurately identify small phase changes. Performance parameters such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to evaluate the model's performance and show how well it can categorize inclusion gait swing phases. The datasets were tested on different models CNN-LSTM, CNN-Dense-LSTM, and LSTM and the results show that CNN-LSTM achieved the highest accuracy of 98.56%.

articleTitle: Image Encryption Using Higher Dimension Chaotic Systems for Enhanced Image Security
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Encryption is the most powerful technique for securing information in communication and information technology. A high-dimensional (hyperchaotic) image encryption scheme based on dynamic DNA has been developed to provide adequate security measures for the cryptographic method and to increase the complexity of the chaotic system. The suggested work overcomes previous approach inefficiencies by featuring a cryptosystem based on zig zag scrambling, five-dimensional (5D) hyper-chaotic, six-dimensional (6D) hyperchaotic, and dynamic-DNA encoding mechanism. The proposed model generates a scrambled image using zig-zag scrambling, and a 5D hyperchaotic sequence is used to shuffle the image pixel position for increased security. The image is then diffused using a 6D hyperchaotic system with a Unix time stamp to enhance security. The diffused image is DNA encoded to generate the encrypted image. The suggested algorithm, validated with comprehensive simulation data, demonstrates its resilience to several types of attacks, thereby confirming its effectiveness and security in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Envisioning Earth: Enabling Environmental Monitoring with U-Net Segmentation of Forests and Waterbodies in Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Inspired by the pressing need for addressing environmental issues like water scarcity and deforestation, this study uses machine learning and image processing on satellite data to detect changes comprehensively. Our method focuses on precisely separating forests and water bodies using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), more especially the U-Net model. This allows for accurate tracking of environmental changes. The use of cutting-edge segmentation algorithms, dataset analysis, and literature evaluation are all components of the methodological rigor. The approved result shows how effective deep learning is at monitoring the environment and offers insightful information for sustainable management and to make informed decisions. The aim of this paper is to add a methodical methodology while highlighting deep learning's transformative potential to improve environmental conservation efforts and obtained accuracy of 0.840 and 0.880 for Forest Segmentation and Water Body Segmentation respectively

articleTitle: Based on the Application of Improved Yolov3 Intelligent Detection Algorithm in Tank Truck Loading And Unloading Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The role of safety detection in the loading and unloading of tank trucks is very important, but there is a problem that safety detection is not intelligent enough. In the past, manual inspection could not solve the intelligent detection problem in the loading and unloading operation of tank trucks, and the detection was not standardized. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv3 intelligent detection algorithm for intelligent detection and analysis. Firstly, the characteristic analysis theory is used to intelligently detect the tank truck, and the index is divided according to the intelligent detection requirements to reduce the safety operation in the interfering factor. Then, the characteristic analysis theory intelligently detects the tank truck, forms an intelligent detection scheme, and conducts the safety operation results Comprehensive analysis. MATLAB simulation shows that under the condition of certain intelligent detection standards, the YOLOv3 intelligent detection algorithm is improved for tank trucks Intelligent detection, safety operation accuracy, detection time are better than previous intelligent detection methods.

Author Keywords: Tank truck loading and unloading operations

articleTitle: Classifying Biodegradable and Non-Biodegradable Waste using a Pretrained VGG16 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research explores the development of an automated waste segregation system using the VGG16 model, aimed at accurately classifying waste into biodegradable and non-biodegradable categories. Leveraging transfer learning, the pre-trained VGG16 model was fine-tuned on a dataset of waste images, allowing it to effectively distinguish between different types of waste based on their visual features. The study involved a systematic approach to data collection, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation, ensuring robust performance. The results demonstrated a consistent improvement in both training and validation accuracy, with final accuracies exceeding 90%. Despite a brief challenge of overfitting observed during the mid-training phase, the model successfully overcame it, achieving high accuracy and low loss by the final epochs. This suggests that the VGG16-based system can reliably automate waste segregation, potentially enhancing efficiency and accuracy in waste management practices. The research highlights the model’s potential for practical application, contributing to more sustainable and effective waste management solutions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of 6T, 8T and 10T SRAM Using 180nm CMOS Technology for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: As long as the power is furnished, the Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) retains the information. SRAM does not demand continuous refreshment, which results better performance and low power usage. For wide variety of IoT applications, low power memory devices are desirable. This paper proposed 6T, 8T and 10T SRAM cells in 180nm CMOS technology, along with layout, parasitic extraction, pre and post layout also. The design of SRAM memory circuits is implemented using Cadence Virtuoso tool and Spectre simulator is used to generate waveform. This advanced SRAM model is the stand-in for IoT (Internet of Things) applications and described about the calculation of delay, noise and power. The proposed SRAM is useful for the devices like PC’s, smart phones, portable memories, embedded devices etc which require less power and high-speed operation.

articleTitle: Selling Electronic Products using Auction Mechanism in Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The emergence of the Metaverse has introduced new paradigms for commerce, including electronic product selling. This paper utilizes a game theoretic approach to analyze the dynamics of electronic product selling in the Metaverse. Through strategic interaction and decision-making among players, including consumers, sellers, and platform providers, this research explores various scenarios, equilibrium outcomes, and potential strategies for maximizing utility and profit in the virtual marketplace.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of CIGS-based Photovoltaic Cells under Varied Temperature Conditions using SCAPS Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Solar cells are constructed using semiconductors that have undergone demanding research and development. At now, the preferred material used for making photovoltaic (PV) cells is Silicon (Si), which makes up over 80% of worldwide output. Si-based compounds seem inferior to other compounds based on the CIS family due to their expensive operation and manufacturing methods. Some materials can significantly absorb the sun's light. Furthermore, CIGS has attained a heightened degree of efficiency, making it the ideal material for maximizing the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of thin-film technologies. To optimize the effectiveness of PV cells, use the SCAPS tool. This study involves the use of CIGS-based PV cells, where the temperature is systematically altered in 10 increments, ranging from 250 to 350 K. Fluctuations in temperature in controlled experiments allow for targeted examinations of the performance of materials under varying temperature circumstances. The results provide useful insights for improving the structure and efficiency of CIGS solar cells, thereby increasing the production of sustainable energy. The V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> (Open Circuit Voltage) is 0.73 V, the J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> (Short Circuit Current Density) is 42.9 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the FF (Fill Factor) is 86.11%. These values provide valuable insights for the advancement and enhancement of CIGS-based PV cells.

articleTitle: Optimization of Power Communication Signal by Signal-Wave Judgment Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: With the advancement of globalization, the rapid development of electric power communication has attracted the attention of all walks of life. Timely monitoring of the accuracy assessment in the power communication signal environment has an extremely important influence on understanding and promoting the development of the signal wave judgment method. In the process of power communication signal, because of its wide application, the signal wave judgment method becomes more convenient and quickly accepted by users. Based on this background, this study proposes an ICE-signal wave judgment method based on the signal wave judgment method, which is used for conducting the accuracy evaluation in the power communication signals. Through the method of the power communication signal evaluation, the similarity measurement of the power communication signal information detection and the accuracy distribution of the power communication generated by the modeling is conducted. This study will model the power communication signal data collected by the signal wave judgment method. In this process, this study will use the TF-IDF algorithm to extract the power communication signal in the signal wave judgment method and denoise, so as to improve the accuracy of the power communication signal of the power communication characteristics.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Advances in Autonomous Driving: A Detailed Examination of DQN and PPO
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: One of the most important subdivisions of artificial intelligence, self-driving is widely regarded as the technology that will finally change transportation for the better. This paper involves a review of the current developments in the use of reinforcement learning (RL) to enhance the autonomy of cars; this paper will consider two algorithms, the deep Q-network (DQN) and the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Both the algorithms are considerably powerful in the field of RL; wherein DQN is better suited for the problems with discrete action space, and PPO for continuous control issues. The experiments were performed in the CARLA simulator focused on driving scenes on highways, urban roads, and rural roads, and in various weather conditions and traffic intensities. The findings also show the normality of the performances across both the training and testing sets, and to validate the hypothesis that PPO performs better than DQN, important metrics are presented including the average rewards, collisions, lanes, success rate, and episode’s time steps. PPO policy optimized base technique will achieve more steady and effective learning and that’s why PPO has a high suitability for deeply complex decision-making like self-driving cars. Therefore, our work also contains a comparison with other state-of-the-art autonomous driving techniques to note the excellent position of the PPO method. Furthermore, we discussed the learning patterns and the hyperparameters’ impacts of both DQN and PPO and revealed the advantages and limitations of each. The results confirm the efficiency and flexibility of PPO enhancing its role in real-life RL applications for building future self-driving cars. Consequently, this study enriches the global knowledge on the RL of autonomous driving and provides practical suggestions to improve the learning capabilities of autonomous systems and their safety from further deterioration.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Routing Frame Work for Cloud based IoT Networks using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The explosion of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has led to an unprecedented surge in the number of devices connected. As a result, it has significantly increased energy consumption and system operation costs of the cloud environment in IoT networks. Optimal routing is critical to reduce energy consumption and improve the play of these networks. This paper proposes a novel AI-based energy-efficient routing framework for cloud-assisted IoT networks. The framework uses AI methods to determine which path the data traffic can move more efficiently, depending on how congested the network is at that moment. It includes the vs, bandwidth and energy for routing decision_TypeInfo. In addition, energy-efficient routing protocols are also integrated with the framework as part of optimization measures to conserve energy. To alleviate network congestion and improve overall efficiency, our framework ensures innovative management of resources among connected IoT devices by efficiently load balancing. It is equipped to detect & automatically rectify faulty or jammed network nodes for smooth data transmission. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduced energy consumption, delay and packet loss compared to conventional routing approaches. It helps solve the energy efficiency problem in cloud-based IoT networks and provides a scalable, immune approach that uses AI techniques. Ultimately, our framework could lead to significant performance and sustainability gains for cloud-based IoT networks.

articleTitle: ML-Based Face Recognition System for marking Attendance in organizations
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a Python-based face recognition system aimed at automating student attendance tracking. Leveraging machine learning techniques, particularly facial recognition algorithms. The system not only registers attendance but also aims to associate detected faces with corresponding student names. Our approach involves the following key steps: first, we capture facial images from the camera feed; second, we preprocess these images to enhance feature extraction and improve recognition accuracy. This feature enables the program to maintain a comprehensive record of attendance, making it invaluable for educational institutions seeking efficient attendance management solutions. By leveraging the versatility of Python and the robustness of machine learning techniques, our aim is to develop a sophisticated yet user friendly application that simplifies attendance tracking while paving the way for future enhancements and innovations in this domain.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Approach to Identify Intrusions in Edge IoT and IIoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This work presents an IDS for Internet of Things (IoT) that makes use of the ML-EdgeIIoT-dataset to safeguard critical IoT infrastructures. The proposed model integrates CNN and GRU with an XGBoost layer to enhance predictive accuracy. The CNN-GRU architecture is specifically engineered to effectively capture both spatial and temporal features. The CNN component in this design is tasked with capturing local patterns, whereas the GRU component is responsible for managing sequential dependencies. The results are combined with the initial characteristics and improved using XGBoost to generate the ultimate forecasts. The ensemble approach ensures robust real-time data processing, enabling fast and accurate risk identification. The effectiveness of the Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is evaluated using the four accuracy metrics, demonstrating its outstanding efficiency and resilience across various workloads. This comprehensive architecture prioritizes the security and dependability of the IoT system and is adaptable to evolving cyber threats. Our Intrusion Detection System (IDS) establishes a higher benchmark for taking initiative and adapting to changing circumstances in order to defend IoT networks. It offers robust safeguards to ensure the stability and security of these networks. The study emphasizes the significance of employing sophisticated machine learning methods to enhance the detection capabilities and overall robustness of IDS in Internet of Things (IoT) environments.

articleTitle: Exploring Synergistic Approaches to Enhance Predictive Modeling in Astronomical Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research article focused on testing the performance of three machine learning classification algorithms- RandomForest, XGBoost, and CatBoost for classifying stellar multiple classes allows for an evaluation of their performance metrics-accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. For all the cross-validation cases, RandomForest demonstrated constant dominance over the other algorithms, which achieved the highest accuracy of 98.29% and the best F1 scores in all classes. The ensemble approach it used to aggregate multiple decision trees considerably reduced overfitting and was capable of addressing complex feature interactions inherent in datasets of astronomy with minimal hyperparameter tuning. The recall of RandomForest was strongly concentrated on Class 1, at 99.97% which again highlighted its strength in the correct classification of positive instances. Although XGBoost and CatBoost's reported competitive performance, the strength of the system, good tradeoff between precision and recall, and interpretability provided by RandomForest are more proficient for stellar classification. Future work can be oriented towards hybrid models and feature engineering to improve classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of A*, Dijkstra’s, and Breadth-First Search Algorithms: Evaluating Complexity, Optimality, and Efficiency in Shortest Pathfinding
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of three widely used pathfinding algorithms: A*, Dijistra’s, and Breadth-First Search (BFS). We evaluate these algorithms based on their complexity, optimality, and efficiency in finding your shortest path in different scenarios. This paper compares all three algorithms looks at how fast and how well they work to find the shortest path.

articleTitle: Implementation of Various Filtering Technique for Noise Removal in Dicom Images of Colon Carcinoma
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Colorectal carcinoma in the third most affected disease worldwide. Generally, it is identified at chronic stage where the treatment options are very limited. CT, MRI, PET images are used for the assessment of the Colorectal cancer. Quality of the image is essential in order to identify abnormalities in any kind of medical images. In this study, CT dicom images are considered. During image acquisition, various noises occur in the image due to variation in radiation intensities and ambient conditions. These noises should be removed before image is being utilized. Hence, to enhance the image's quality, pre-processing is required. One of the two types of images pre-processing is noise reduction or image enhancement. By using various filtering techniques to remove noise from the images, the pre-processing step aims to enhance the user's impression of the image. Filtering techniques alter a image's texture and look by using the pixel information included in the image. In this study, noises seen in CT dicom images, including Gaussian noise, noise from salt and pepper, and passion noise, to talk about speckle noise.
