Additionally, the application of many filters for CT dicom image is discussed, including the mean, median, Gaussian, and Modified Gaussian bilateral filters.

articleTitle: A Novel Attention-Based Method for Integrating Facial and Speech Features in Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Our research introduces a novel approach for recognizing multiple emotions by leveraging perspective-based methods. This technique integrates facial features and speech characteristics obtained from different encoders to pinpoint the most significant attributes. The distinct characteristics of speech and facial expressions, along with effective size management, prove to be highly beneficial. By concentrating on specific components, the system enhances overall accuracy. Images of facial features are captured from both low and high angles to ensure a comprehensive representation. These techniques are merged through a fusion mesh, producing several feature vectors that are subsequently utilized in the classification stage for sensitivity analysis. When tested with both data sets, this algorithm surpassed existing models, achieving a weighted accuracy (WA) of 90.3%.

articleTitle: Research on Information Customer Service Data Mining and User Group Classification Based on Cluster Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Cluster analysis is an important content of information customer service data mining technology. Cluster analysis will promote the economic development of information customer service data mining, and have an important impact on the division of user groups. Nowadays, the research on information customer service data mining technology of cluster analysis focuses on the early pilot theory stage, discussing cluster analysis, information customer service data mining and other aspects, and lacks the research content of the integration of cluster analysis and user group division application. In order to further study the clustering analysis of information customer service data mining technology on the actual impact of user groups, the study through the cluster analysis method, the analysis of regression analysis of regression analysis, and depth study of various compound additives add how to affect the weightlessness characteristics, and all kinds of information on the degree of data mining. Then, based on the analysis of information customer service data mining, confirmation and latent value calculation of user group classification, standardization, weighted evaluation and user group classification load and sensitivity analysis, the final conclusion is put forward based on the regression results. The research results show that the information customer service data mining system has little negative utility value for the user group division, which is a power generation system worth promoting.

articleTitle: Elevating Deep Learning Models with Gated Recurrent Units for Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research explores emotion analysis in natural language processing (NLP) by employing bidirectional gated recurrent units (GRUs). Unlike traditional models that process data in a single direction, bidirectional GRUs can capture dependencies in both past and future sequences, making them significantly more effective for tasks like emotion analysis where context is crucial. The proposed model utilizes a sequential framework, starting with an embedding layer that converts word indices into dense vectors for text processing. To combat overfitting, a dropout layer with a 0.5 rate is incorporated. This is followed by two bidirectional GRU layers, each configured to return sequences and capture detailed temporal dependencies. A batch normalization layer is applied to stabilize and speed up training. An additional bidirectional GRU layer, consisting of six units and a softmax activation function, further refines the model’s ability to capture complex dependencies and classify emotions into six categories. The model concludes with a dense layer and uses the Adam optimizer with sparse categorical cross-entropy as the loss function. Accuracy is employed to evaluate performance, with the model achieving a 94% accuracy rate. This indicates the superior capability of bidirectional GRUs in detecting emotions by effectively identifying intricate patterns in sequential data. The model summary details the components and parameter choices that contribute to these strong results.

articleTitle: User Experience and Intelligent Algorithm Optimization of Satellite Communication Payment System in Remote Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: There have always been problems such as difficulty in electricity payment and electricity consumption in remote areas, and at present, the payment mode of satellite communication has become extremely convenient and efficient with the application of related technologies. Therefore, this paper proposes a user experience and intelligent algorithm for satellite communication payment system in remote areas, and optimizes it to a certain extent. Based on this, it will provide some help for the effective satisfaction of electricity demand in remote areas.

articleTitle: Design And Performance Analysis of Different Low-Power Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) Units
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The design of low-power Multiplier Accumulator (MAC) units has become crucial for energy-efficient computing systems. MAC units play a vital role in various applications such as digital signal processing (DSP), multimedia processing, image processing, and neural networks, where efficient multiplication and accumulation operations are required. This paper presents an overview of the key considerations and strategies involved in designing a low-power MAC unit to achieve optimal power consumption while maintaining performance. The design process starts with the selection of different energy-efficient multipliers and adder components. Power-efficient multiplier architectures such as the Carry save multiplier, Vedic multiplier, and Wallace tree multiplier are employed to minimize power consumption during multiplication operations. Similarly, low-power adders including carry-select adders, carry-skip adders, carry-save adders, and carry-lookahead adders are utilized to reduce power dissipation during addition and a low-power accumulator is designed for accumulation operations. The design of MAC units involves a trade-off between speed (propagation delay) and efficiency (power consumption) This paper compares designed MAC unit modules based on these factors. The design schematics and simulations of low-power MAC units are done using adequate libraries, with the mentor graphics Tanner EDA suit’s S-edit, T-Spice, and W-edit software using 45nm CMOS technology model files.

articleTitle: Stages of Sleep: A classification analysed from Electroencephalogram Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Investigating the various stages of sleep, an essential aspect of human health and well-being, is crucial for understanding and improving overall health. A deep and detailed analysis of sleep stages is key to identifying sleep disorders and assessing sleep quality. Traditionally, sleep stage classification has relied on polysomnography, an advanced method that tracks various physiological indicators. However, the complexity and high cost of these systems limit their accessibility for widespread use. This paper introduces an accessible alternative for sleep stage classification by applying machine learning techniques to EEG data. It highlights a novel model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to effectively interpret the intricate temporal sequences in EEG signals, which are challenging to analyze with traditional methods. The outcomes of this research are promising, demonstrating that the model can identify different sleep stages with an accuracy exceeding 85%, outperforming conventional feature-based classifiers.

articleTitle: An autoML algorithm to select suitable decision tree algorithm for classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic machine learning (autoML) algorithm to select a decision tree algorithm which is most suitable for the stated requirements by the user for classification. The user can specify requirements in terms of algorithmic characteristics such as speed, space, scalability and interpretability of the decision tree algorithms for selection. The user can also specify any missing values in the dataset and data types (numeric or categorical or mixed) in the dataset that will be used for training and testing of the selected decision tree algorithm. Based on these inputs the autoML algorithm selects one of the few best decision tree algorithms which are included for automatic selection. The decision tree algorithms available for selection include C5.0, C4.5, ID3, CART and CHAID. The autoML algorithm is tested for the selection of the suitable decision tree algorithm based on algorithmic characteristics, and data types and missing values in the dataset as fed by the user.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Digital Phase-Locked Loop (DPLL) with Vernier Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) for Dynamic Frequency Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design of a Digital Phase-Locked Loop (DPLL) that integrates a Vernier Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC), priority encoder, and multiplexer (MUX) for precise dynamic frequency selection. The design leverages an 8-bit Vernier TDC to measure time differences, which are reduced to a 3-bit code using a priority encoder. The 3-bit code is then used as select lines for an 8:1 MUX, which dynamically chooses one of eight frequencies generated by an 8-bit ring oscillator. The output is used for clock generation in high-performance digital communication systems, offering improved accuracy and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Implementing and Verifying the SPI Communication Protocol in ASICs with Cadence EDA Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The increasing complexity of electronic systems demands advanced design and verification techniques, particularly for protocols like the Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI). SPI, initially developed by Motorola, is a widely used synchronous serial communication protocol essential for connecting microcontrollers with peripheral devices. As device interconnectivity grows, ensuring fault-free operation is crucial, necessitating efficient self-test mechanisms to reduce maintenance and testing costs. This paper presents the ASIC design and verification of an 8-bit SPI module, incorporating Built-In-Self-Test (BIST) to enhance fault detection and reliability. Using Cadence EDA tools, the design flow from Register Transfer Level (RTL) coding to gate-level netlist generation is detailed. The verification process includes simulation and formal methods, followed by synthesis, with a focus on timing, power analysis, and optimization challenges.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Poisoning Attack Detection with Boosting Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: It is quite difficult to identify and counteract poisoning attempts in ML settings, especially when boosting methods are involved. The goal of this research is to investigate and improve Adaptive Gradient Boosting (AdaBoost), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting (LightGBM) ability to detect these kinds of attacks. The analysis starts with a thorough preprocessing step to guarantee data integrity and relevance, using the RT-IoT 2022 dataset as a benchmark. After that, several tests are carried out using the previously mentioned boosting methods to build reliable classification models. To maximize performance, each algorithm goes through a rigorous hyperparameter tuning process. In the experimental setting, the dataset is subjected to controlled poisoning attacks, and then boosting techniques are used to identify anomalies. Performance measures including recall, accuracy, precision, and F1-score are used to assess how effective each method is. The outcomes show clear advantages and disadvantages for each algorithm, along with particular situations in which one algorithm may perform better than the others. The trade-offs between computing effectiveness, detection accuracy, and attack vector resistance are highlighted via comparative analysis. In addition, the models’ decision-making procedures and feature importance are revealed, offering a more comprehensive comprehension and interpretability. This work provides a framework for further research in this important area and highlights the potential of boosting algorithms in strengthening the robustness of machine learning systems against poisoning attempts.

articleTitle: Application Progress and Prospect of GIS Technology in Landscape Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The intelligent landscape planning analysis based on BIM cannot solve the GIS technical problems in the application progress and prospect of landscape architecture. This paper proposes an RS-GIS technology for the analysis of G IS technology for intelligent landscape planning. Firstly, the virtual tour system of BIM+GIS is used to evaluate the type of landscape architecture, and the indicators are divided according to the GIS technical requirements to reduce the interference factors in GIS technology. Then, according to the virtual tour system of BIM+GIS, the intelligent landscape planning technology of college students was initially analyzed, and the GIS technical the fusion of vegetation rockeries was formed, and the GIS technology was formed The results were comprehensively analyzed. RS-GIS simulation shows that RS-GIS technology has a certain evaluation standard for intelligent landscape planning Both accuracy and efficiency are superior to BIM-based intelligent landscape planning.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Error Recognition of Machine English Translation Based on Multi-feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The role of automatic error recognition in machine English translation is very important, but there is a problem of low error recognition accuracy. The normal method cannot solve the problem of automatic recognition of machine English translation errors in English translation, and the recognition is incorrect. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion to carry out a comprehensive automatic error recognition analysis of machine English translation. Firstly, the computer is used to analyze and evaluate the automatic identification system, and the indicators are divided according to the automatic recognition requirements of machine English translation errors to reduce them Automatic identification of interference factors in machine English translation errors. Then, the computer evaluates the automatic recognition of machine English translation errors to form an automatic recognition scheme for machine English translation errors, and automatically identifies machine English translation errors The results were comprehensively analyzed. MATLAB simulation shows that under certain evaluation criteria, multi-feature fusion automatically identifies machine English translation errors for English translation The accuracy and automatic recognition time of machine English translation errors are better than ordinary methods.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Software Fault Diagnosis: Evaluating Decision Tree and KNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research study explores the predictive modeling of software errors by employing machine learning techniques, using the PC1 dataset extracted from PROMISE Software engineering repository. In this work, it is proposed to investigate the attributes related with dependability and quality of software that can be used for an accurate prediction model in detecting significant software problems, aiming at improvements in fault-prone detection. We evaluated two machine learning models: Decision Tree and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) using several performance indicators. The results indicate that KNN achieves higher AUC and accuracy, but Decision Tree model offers desirable balance between precision-recall trade-offs which is applicable for multiple condition-specific fault prediction scenarios. In hindsight, this work highlights the importance of selecting machine learning methodologies and evaluation metrics that are tailored to software failure prediction use-cases.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Consumption Forecasting in Smart Grids Using Quantum Boltzmann Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Smart grid systems are seen as the next big thing to energy distribution and management with more efficiency, stability, and sustainability in power distribution and energy management systems. It is challenging to predict the amount of energy consumption in smart grid system because of its randomness resulting from various factors such as consumer’s behavior, weather conditions. This is mainly because traditional forecasting techniques are usually inadequate in capturing these complexities and as a result resources are poorly allocated and organizational processes become inefficient. The work provides the energy consumption forecasting in smart grids through the application of Quantum Boltzmann Machine(QBM) in the smart grid utilizing historical data. Some of the variables incorporated in the data are reaction time, power balance, and price elasticity coefficients customized through smart meters. Once raw data is preprocessed, QBMs are developed to establish an empirical probability model that will predict actual future energy utilization characteristics. The QBM is tested against the actual consumption data and focuses on the visualization of energy profile and identification of points like local extremes.

articleTitle: Leveraging BBTS and NFTs for Ethical Ticketing in Live Events
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This research presents an innovative Blockchain-Based Ticketing System (BBTS) that leverages blockchain technology, smart contracts, and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to revolutionize the ticketing industry. The architecture comprises a User Interface, Smart Contracts Layer, Blockchain Network, Tokenization Layer, Ticketing Process, and Administrative functionalities. BBTS addresses the pervasive issue of ticket reselling, ensuring fair access to event tickets for all fans and equitable compensation for artists.Through the creation, buying, and reselling of NFT-based tickets, the platform leverages blockchain technology and smart contracts to automate ticket transactions and enhance transparency, effectively mitigating exploitative secondary markets. The system allows for the creation of NFTs associated with artists, preventing scalping and fostering a sustainable and artist-friendly ticketing ecosystem. The main aim of BBTS is to deter ticket reselling practices, ultimately benefiting both fans and artists by ensuring affordable access to events while fostering a fair compensation model. This research demonstrates the potential of blockchain-based ticketing solutions to revolutionize the event industry, establishing a foundation for fair and ethical ticket distribution.

articleTitle: A Dual-Power Approach for Skin Disease Classification Using ResNet-50 and SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this reasearch, we propose a reliable skin disease detection system by integrating a deep learning model, ResNet50, with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. Using the recommended methodology, six types of skin diseases that is Acne, Carcinoma, Eczema, Keratosis, Milia, and Rosacea should be grouped.ResNet-50 is used for feature extraction; its deep design allows it to extract fine details from pictures of skin lesions. An SVM classifier which is renowned for its effectiveness in binary classification problems is then fed the gathered information. To determine the efficacy of the model, training and assessment are conducted on a skin disease dataset that spans many epochs. The model achieves a training accuracy of 99.55% and a validation accuracy of 97.90% after 85 epochs, demonstrating high generalization and learning capacity based on experimental data.. To further support the robustness of the model, the validation loss dropped from 0.4037 at 5 epochs to 0.0865 by 85 epochs. Owing to its reliable performance in training and validation, dermatologists may utilize the model in clinical settings for the early and accurate detection of skin problems. The integration of SVM with ResNet-50 has demonstrated efficacy, yielding a scalable and dependable solution for the categorization of skin conditions.

articleTitle: Balanced Histology Dataset Analysis for Improved CNN Performance in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) performance using a confusion matrix and classification report in order to detect lung cancer and colon cancer from medical photos. Especially in differentiating between malignant and non-cancerous tissues, the CNN shows strong classification capacity. With one false positive, the algorithm shows remarkable accuracy in spotting 499 adenocarcinoma patients for colon cancer detection. But it points to a minor misclassification issue by misclassifying six benign events .CNN detects 487 adenocarcinoma cases in lung cancer with little false positives and negatives. With lung squamous cell cancer, it performs less successfully showing 14 false negatives but no false positives, suggesting space for development in this subtype. With great accuracy measures across all assessed classes, the model shows remarkable dependability and precision generally. Precision for colon adenocarcinoma is 0.99, recall 1.00, and an F1-score of 0.99, thereby implying rather few misclassifications. Likewise presenting good performance with a precision and recall of 0.97 is lung adenocarcinoma. The CNN's probable value as a diagnostic tool is highlighted by its capacity to precisely identify benign lung tissues and differentiate between malignant types. Greater datasets and iterative changes seem to help to increase dependability even further. This paper provides important information for clinical use since it shows how successfully CNN detects lung and colon tumors.

articleTitle: Exploration of Key Technology and Implementation Model of AHP Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In order to achieve zero emissions in substations and reduce their emission energy consumption, it is necessary to optimize them. Therefore, a hierarchical analysis method is proposed to optimize the energy transmission and energy regulation in substations to explore their key content and technology. The jump analysis theory is used to discover the data changes, power flow, and voltage characteristics in substations, and the key points and main factors of energy consumption are identified through step-by-step analysis. Targeted measures are taken, and the hierarchical analysis method is displayed in the simulation results. With the help of weights, subjective judgments, and experience, the energy consumption of substations can be reduced by about 10% to 15%, and the overall optimization of substations can be achieved.

articleTitle: Addressing Bone Marrow Classification Hurdles Using EfficientNetB5 Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Multi-class classification of bone marrow images faces challenges such as class imbalance, significant intra-class variability, and the need for precise and interpretable diagnostic models. These issues complicate the development of reliable automated clinical diagnostic systems. Accurate classification of bone marrow images is crucial for diagnosing a range of hematological disorders. However, difficulties arise in achieving precise and comprehensible results due to morphological variability and class imbalance. This study examines the application of EfficientNetB5, an advanced convolutional neural network, to address these issues in bone marrow image classification. By implementing customized loss functions, advanced data augmentation, and interpretability methods, our approach achieves an impressive 96% accuracy. These results highlight how EfficientNetB5 can enhance diagnostic reliability and precision in clinical settings. Our approach overcomes challenges by addressing class imbalance with tailored loss functions, increasing dataset diversity with innovative augmentation techniques, and ensuring model transparency with interpretability strategies. Leveraging EfficientNetB5's advanced architecture, we achieved a significant improvement with a 96% accuracy rate in classification.

articleTitle: Ensemble-Based Approach for Effective Detection of Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Due to the growing number of connected devices and the sophistication of attack vectors, cybersecurity experts are increasingly concerned about identifying injection attacks in Internet of Things (IoT) environments. This work focuses on exploiting the IoT-23 dataset, an exhaustive collection of IoT network traffic, to improve the detection of injection attacks through the application of ensemble learning models. the use of four cutting-edge ensemble techniques: AdaBoost, Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM). After being trained separately, the models are integrated to provide a strong detection framework. When compared to individual classifiers, the experimental findings show that the ensemble technology greatly enhances detection accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. We shed light on the traits of injection attacks and the essential features for identifying them by examining the feature importance and each model’s contribution inside the ensemble. The ensemble model improves the detection system’s robustness and generalizability in a variety of IoT environments in addition to displaying higher performance metrics. This study demonstrates how ensemble learning can strengthen IoT security and pave the way for future developments in the identification and defence against sophisticated cyber threats.

articleTitle: Optimization of Intelligent Decision-Making of Relay Protection Operation Safety Under the Multi-Scene Model Fusion Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: At present, the problem of poor accuracy is the operation safety of relay protection device, so this paper studies the intelligent decision evaluation of operation safety of relay protection device. The intelligent decision evaluation model of operation safety of relay protection device based on multi-scene model fusion framework is proposed, and the evaluation index of operation safety of relay protection device is selected. Then through the scene model fusion framework establish safety intelligent decision evaluation system, by the scene model fusion framework of input layer and hidden layer and output layer node build scene model fusion framework vector index, the connection weight and threshold output value calculation, complete the relay protection device operation safety intelligent decision evaluation. The simulation experiment results show that the proposed multi-scene model fusion framework evaluation model has the best evaluation effect on the operation safety intelligent decision evaluation of the relay protection device, and the evaluation time is short, which can effectively improve the evaluation accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Clock Tree Distributor with Systematic Scheduler for Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Clock Tree distributor (CTD) is a crucial step in the physical design of digital circuits, primarily focused on distributing the clock signal evenly across the chip. While the primary goal of CTD is to minimize skew and ensure timing accuracy, it also indirectly contributes to identifying and mitigating logic faults. The proposed approach discussed the important role of frequency synthesisers in logical fault detection during integration of low power devices. The system considers the stability level analysis of synthesizer results in terms of clock glitches, jitters, skews present in the clocks before utilizing the clocks for integrated devices. The clocks are tested with various levels of sweep stability analysis and latency of sweeping from one frequency to the next shift. The proposed system achieved ±20 ns of sweep shift latency. The sweep stability is tested with 10MHz to 10GHz frequency range with the step size of 100KHz.

articleTitle: The Designing of Carbon Nanotube FET Based Encoder Using Ternary Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel digital circuit design utilizing a Carbon Nanotube Field-Effect Transistor (CNTFET) encoder that incorporates ternary logic gates. Unlike conventional binary logic, which uses two levels, ternary logic utilizes three distinct levels, providing notable benefits in power efficiency, speed, and circuit density. We investigate the implementation and performance of ternary logic gates such as ternary NOT, NAND, and NOR in the context of a CNTFET-based encoder. This approach leverages the unique advantages of ternary logic to surpass the performance of traditional CMOS technology. Extensive simulations conducted with Electric and HSPICE tools reveal significant improvements in both propagation delay and power consumption. The findings highlight a considerable boost in speed and energy efficiency, showcasing the potential of CNTFET technology to drive advancements in digital electronics. This study underscores the promise of integrating ternary logic with CNTFETs as pivotal for the development of future electronic devices.

articleTitle: Unified CNN Approach for Fracture Detection Across All Anatomical Regions in Radiographic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Fractured bones are a serious health problem that can lead to serious consequences if not recognized and treated immediately. Early diagnosis of fractures is critical for efficient treatment and reducing long-term consequences on patient health. By incorporating AI-driven fracture detection technologies, healthcare may become more effective and efficient, supporting international efforts to provide universal access to fair and inclusive healthcare. This research employs a Bone Fracture multi-region X-ray dataset of radiographic scans to offer a complete fracture detection and categorization method utilizing a proposed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. The collection contains 10,580 X-ray scans of broken and non-fractured bones from all anatomical locations, including the lower limb, upper limb, lumbar, hips, and knees. The proposed CNN model showed exceptional results, with an overall accuracy of 97.85%, and precision and recall rates of 98%. These results illustrate the usefulness of the model in reliably identifying and categorizing fractures across diverse anatomical locations, underlining its potential for increasing early fracture detection in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Telugu Braille Character Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Braille is a tactile writing system that visually impaired individuals use for reading and writing. While Braille has been adapted for many languages around the world, including major Indian languages like Hindi, robust Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems are lacking for detecting Braille characters in Telugu, one of the classical Dravidian languages. This work presents a novel deep-learning approach for automatically recognising Telugu Braille characters from images. The proposed method involves preprocessing Braille images using techniques like principal component analysis for alignment and filtering for enhancement, followed by training a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture with an inverted residual block module on a data set of Telugu Braille images. The deep learning model achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in recognizing Telugu Braille characters while offering practical inference speed suitable for real-time applications. This work can potentially facilitate more accessible reading and writing tools for the visually impaired Telugu community.

articleTitle: Data Clustering Analysis and Application Research of New Energy Vehicles Based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Based on the calculation data clustering analysis (big data) theory, this paper using FLUENT software for NACA63 models in a kinds of new energy vehicle data condition of resistance characteristics of numerical simulation calculation, and the calculation results and the related experimental data are compared and analyzed, so this paper studies the speed vector of new energy vehicle data. The results show that under the condition of small new energy vehicle data, various clustering analysis model of large data and large data coefficient simulation results is quite accurate, and under the condition of large new energy vehicle data, shear force transmission k clustering model (also known as SSTk clustering model) large data coefficient is more accurate than the other two cluster analysis model. The large data coefficients and lift-resistance obtained from the k-kL clustering model are closer to the experimental data than the other two models. The trend of the resistance ratio and resistance coefficient with the data amount of neVs coincides with the experimental data. When the data amount of new energy vehicles is large, the boundary layer appears countercurrent and separation of the model.

articleTitle: RLWF-An Efficient Content Caching and Replacement Algorithm for ICN-IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things) generates massive amounts of data from sensor devices, where all devices are resource-constrained. Managing this huge amount of data efficiently becomes the major challenge in IoT. Existing IP-based networks are host-centric and not efficient in data management. ICN (Information Centric Network) is a content-based network that transmits content based on the content’s name rather than the content’s address. The main feature of ICN is in-network caching, which enables intermediate nodes to cache the content. This work proposed an efficient content caching technique for ICN-based IoT. The edge cluster is formed between edge devices, and the cluster head is selected based on the residual energy of the devices. When the cache is full, the unwanted content is replaced using the proposed RLWF replacement algorithm. The proposed work is simulated using ndnSIM, and results show that the proposed work achieves 5% efficiency in terms of hit ratio and reduces 8% of content retrieval delay.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Mobile Information Platform for Data Information Security
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In recent years, mobile Internet will play a more important role in people's work and life. In this context, a mobile information platform based on data information security has emerged. Based on the current actual situation of data information security and the current trend and trend of mobile information platform development, this article implements and optimizes the design of a mobile information platform for data information security. The mobile information platform based on data information security optimizes and implements two subsystems: a mobile client system and a background management system developed based on the Android platform. The background management system uses JavaEE technology and is designed according to the MVC model. It can configure and manage the front-end system; the mobile client system is developed in Java language, and the relevant functions of mobile office are designed and implemented according to the office needs of the operator company.

articleTitle: The Performance Analysis of Cyber Threat Detection Model Using AI based Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The performance analysis of cyber threat detection is crucial to ensuring data security and fewer chances for a cyber attack. This paper investigates the performance of AI-based classifiers used for cyber threat detection. Some of them are Support Vector Machines, Random Forests and Neural Networks. We gathered a large dataset of cyber threat occurrences and used different feature sets to train the classifiers. Model performance was measured with some metrics (accuracy, precision and recall). Our results demonstrate that the AI classifiers identify a significant proportion of cyber threats with very few false positives. Moreover, their capacity to learn and adapt also appeared promising against unknown threats, as suggested by the models. This research proves that AI can enhance the detection of cyber threats and prevent further online attacks.

articleTitle: Streamlining Human Resource Leave Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper developed an Online leave management system in the human resource local government unit at Magallanes Agusan Del Norte, Philippines, to easily track the online leave status, balances, and employee leave requests. In the planning phase, the developers interviewed the HRMO personnel and the head of the office. The logical model is developed in the analysis phase by designing the Context Data Flow Diagram, Use Case Diagram and System Architecture. Design phase, where the developers built the Online Leave Management System by writing codes in Visual Studio Code (VSCode) using HyperText Markup Language (HTML5), Bootsrap5, and JavaScript with jQuery as the frontend while the backend was Structured by HyperText Preprocessor (PHP) with Laravel Framework. Before the implementation phase, the functionality and security of the system were checked by evaluating the system for the endusers. The system’s overall performance in terms of Functional Suitability, Usability, Security, and User Satisfaction makes the system highly acceptable to the end-users. Index Terms—Online Leave Management System, Human Resource Local Government Unit, Leave Status.

articleTitle: Optimized Medical Recommendation System Utilizing Large Language Models for Enhanced Question Answering Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the era of fast expanding online medical filed, getting recommendations using AI technology is a challenging one. This study presents a methodology for fine-tuning GPT-3.5 Turbo-0125 model on the MedQuAD dataset, aiming to enhance performance in recommendations of medical question-answering systems. The dataset is prepared by concatenating question-answer pairs and truncating text sequences to standardized lengths. Using Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) for tokenization and optimizing hyperparameters, the model is fine-tuned to improve accuracy and contextual relevance. The evaluation, employing BLEU and ROUGE metrics, indicates substantial performance enhancements. This research underscores the potential of fine-tuning advanced language models for improved medical recommendations and personalized healthcare solutions.

articleTitle: RC Modelling and Analysis of Read Path in eFlash Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: eFlash (embedded Flash) memory is a type of nonvolatile memory integrated into semiconductor devices. The proposed work focuses on enhancing the read performance of embedded Flash (eFlash) memory through a comprehensive approach involving schematic development, RC modelling, and Monte Carlo analysis. The primary objective is to develop a detailed schematic for the read path in eFlash memory, capturing all essential components and interactions. Following this, an RC (resistor-capacitor) model will be constructed to represent the electrical characteristics of the read path, enabling precise analysis of resistive and capacitive effects. To assess the impact of process variations and other uncertainties on read performance metrics, Monte Carlo simulations will be conducted. These simulations will provide statistical insights into read speed, bit line differential voltage, and overall reliability. The outcomes of this work aim to optimize the read path design, ensuring consistent and efficient read operations in eFlash memory devices used in various applications such as microcontrollers, automotive systems, and consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Integration of Semantic Features for Short and Long Text Classification using Attention Based DL
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The categorization of text is an essential and pivotal step in the process of natural language understanding and processing. There are a lot of different approaches to solving the problem of classifying text, but very few of them leverage the semantic integration of several views to boost the classification performance. A dual-DL attention network model, referred to as DDL, is proposed in the study. In order to address the knowledge gap, this paradigm employs semantic complementarity. For more precise extraction of textual logical semantics, DDLfirst employs transductive learning and graph structure. The next step is to use logical semantics in the attention fusion layer (Channel) to train other semantics jointly, which will gradually fix the predictions produced using unlabeled test data. Important for upcoming text mining jobs, experiments show that DDL can achieve better classification across a variety of text classification datasets.

articleTitle: Feature Selection by LFPSOLF for Enhanced Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The accurate diagnosis of diseases is crucial for the treatment and life-saving of patients. Often, the curse of dimensionality in medical data causes incorrect detection of fatal diseases and thereby denies timely treatments leading to higher death tolls. Processing the relevant features alone can achieve improved accuracy at reduced computational cost. Therefore feature selection is highly significant in diagnostic systems and, in line with that, we propose a swarm intelligence-based feature selection method, Leader-follower PSO with Levy Flight (LFPSOLF), adopting the leader-follower concept. The leader performs Levy flight on a random probability basis and the followers do so when their distance from the leader exceeds a threshold, set by the user. The algorithm optimizes the feature set by minimizing the fitness function, the support vector machine (SVM) prediction weighted error. Levy flight of the leader enables the particles to explore the search space and the normal updating of particle position for exploitation. The proposed method was tested on three representative medical datasets and achieved up to 8% improvement in accuracy, while at 40-82% reduction of features. Compared to a few relevant feature selection techniques, the LFPSOLF demonstrated superior accuracy.

articleTitle: Drug Classification Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Personalized medicine is based on the categorization of medications based on each patient’s unique needs. But traditional approaches have drawbacks, especially when it comes to scaling and confidentiality. In this work, we present a new machine learning (ML) method to improve and automate processes related to medicine classification. The study’s dataset came from the open repository Kaggle. The objective point is the kind of medication, and the point settings are coitus, age, BP, cholesterol, and the ratio of sodium to potassium. As part of our process, we replace drug names with placeholders such as DrugX, DrugY, etc. to anonymize them. The patient’s age, sex, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood salt-to-potassium ratio are also considered. Our approach is evaluated on benchmark datasets to demonstrate its efficacy. Using state-of-the-art machine learning techniques like random forests and neural networks, we extract numerous features from pharmaceutical substances. The results are competitive and demonstrate improved performance over conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Towards Graph Embedding-Based Early and Reliable Network Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The stability and security of a network depends on the prompt and precise identification of intruders. Conventional machine learning and deep learning technologies are the backbone of current network intrusion detection algorithms, which categorize intrusions according to statistical characteristics of network flows. Since feature extraction is dependent on expert knowledge, it cannot be executed until network flows have concluded, postponing intrusion detection. The current approaches of graph-based intrusion detection are laborious and complicated since they rely on worldwide network traffic to build communication graphs. In addition, current intrusion detection systems that rely on graphs or deep learning need very large training sets. This study presents Graph2vec+RF, a graph embedding technology-based approach to network intrusion detection that is both early and accurate. Instead, we use graph2vec, an embedding technique, to learn the flow graph’s vector representation, form a flow graph from the first few interaction packets for every bidirectional network flow, and then use Random Forest (RF) to categorize the graph vectors. With Graph2vec+RF, you may perform early and effective network intrusion detection utilizing a small number of the first interactive packets per bidirectional system flow. It automatically extracts flow graph characteristics using subgraph structures and doesn’t need enormous training sets. Our suggested Graph CNN with SVM achieves better accuracy, recall, precision, as well as F1-score than the state-of-the-art approaches, as shown by our experimental findings on the CIC-IDS2017 as well as UNSW-NB15 datasets.

articleTitle: Using the Heterogeneous Network's Self-Adaptive Topological Structure for Drug-Protein Interaction Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The prediction of drug-protein interactions (DPIs) has been the subject of many robust computer approaches using graph neural networks (GNNs). The burden in laboratories and the costs associated with drug discovery and repurposing may be significantly decreased with its help. The unreported indications of many proteins and medications render their clinical activities unclear, nonetheless. Therefore, using the data that is currently available, it is challenging to construct a trustworthy drug-protein heterogeneous network that can characterize the interactions between medicines and proteins. We provide TAG, a DPI prediction approach that may self-adaptively alter the topological framework of the heterogeneous networks, as a solution to this challenge. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently gained a lot of interest due to their exceptional compatibility with viral proteins and pharmacological substances. Building such a model that accurately depicts the molecular structures of living molecules is, however, no easy feat. Also, newly created GNNs have been overfitting on Coronavirus datasets as they are still not widely used. Next, we propose a new model called Topology-enhanced Graph Neural Network using Multi-hop Gating Mechanism to fix those problems. Firstly, our model is able to learn more specific properties of proteins and chemicals. Conversely, we provide a novel gating approach for improving atom representation using non-neighbor data. In order to implement the drug-protein heterogeneous network, TAG sets up a representation learning module that is based on graph attention network. The network's topology may be fine-tuned in response to the training loss, and it can learn the connections between nodes using their properties. Lastly, TAG uses the embeddings of medicines and proteins to forecast the likelihood of their interactions. The experimental findings demonstrate that TAG is capable of significantly enhancing the network's topological structure. Across a range of performance criteria, TAG surpasses other state-of-the-art DPI prediction approaches. These examples demonstrate the practicality of TAG in handling partial data and unstable networks. Additional evidence that TAG is effective for finding new DPIs may be found in the case studies included at the top of the prediction results.

articleTitle: Advanced Calorie Burn Forecasting with XGBoost: A Comprehensive Predictive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Calorie burn, a measure of heat energy, is an essential indicator of the energy expenditure of the human body during physical activities. This study aims to accurately predict the number of calories burned during exercise by leveraging machine learning techniques, particularly the XGBoost regressor algorithm. The model is trained on various physiological and environmental parameters, including exercise duration, average heart rate per minute, body temperature, height, weight, gender, and age. These parameters are crucial as they directly influence the body’s energy expenditure during physical activity. The predictive model is designed to estimate the caloric expenditure based on these inputs, providing a personalized assessment of energy burn. This research contributes to the development of precise and efficient calorie estimation tools, which can be utilized in fitness tracking applications and health management systems. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the XGBoost regressor in delivering accurate calorie burn predictions, making it a valuable tool for individuals aiming to monitor and optimize their fitness routines.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wireless Sensor Networks in E-Commerce with Message Passing Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In today's e-commerce landscape, successful logistics management is essential for achieving success. In this post, we will go over how wireless sensor networks (WSNs) can help online stores streamline their logistics. Data collection and real-time monitoring made possible by wireless sensor networks (WSNs) increase supply chain visibility and control. The proposed approach includes both preprocessing and training the model. Part of the preprocessing phase is principal component analysis (PCA), which entails cleaning and transforming raw data into an appropriate format for analysis or model training. Throughout the training, CNN-BiGRU-BiLSTM was continuously utilized. With a 93.46% average accuracy, this innovative method surpasses the BiGRU and BiLSTM.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Two-Dimensional Medical Image Segmentation Using a Learned Curriculum
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Radiologists greatly benefit from medical image segmentation algorithms when determining the severity of diseases, conducting clinical evaluations, and choosing the best course of therapy. Deep learning is quickly becoming the go-to method for medical picture segmentation because to both the proliferation of big data and improvements in medical imaging methods. The medical segmentation structure encounters various obstacles, such as a lack of labelled data, complicated picture representation, low contrast variation, high structural similarity among infection as well as background, and irregularities related to texture and morphology within homogeneous infected areas. For the purpose of training convolutional neural networks to segment deformable paired 3D medical images, we investigate several curriculum learning approaches. We believe our approach to training medical image segmentation algorithms via curriculum learning, which involves beginning with a simple setup and progressively increasing its complexity, is the first of its kind to aim at improving performance. First, we take a look at two methods for learning curricula that are already out there: curriculum dropout along with curriculum through smoothing. But we provide a fresh and easy way to do curriculum: start with intentionally blurry photographs and work your way up to crisper ones throughout training. Curriculum learning can outperform traditional training methods, according to our studies using a state-of-the-art deep learning model. Among the evaluated curriculum learning methodologies, we also demonstrate that curriculum through input blur offers the highest accuracy against time trade-off.

articleTitle: Multilevel Access Control model for highly Scalable Cloud deployments with Contextual extensions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Effective access control is crucial for modern cloud deployments. Common methods like Discretionary Access Control (DAC), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Mandatory Access Control (MAC) help implement access control policies for different types of access requests. However, current models that incorporate these methods are often either too complex or provide lower Quality of Service (QoS) in large-scale deployments. Additionally, their efficiency is limited by the number of access control points, which hampers scalability under real-time loads.To address these issues, we propose a novel multilevel access control model designed for highly scalable cloud deployments with contextual extensions. This model uses MAC for each new user by redirecting requests to centrally controlled resources, thus converging all endpoints to a single entity and improving control efficiency. The MAC entity is managed via an efficient DAC model that establishes rules for RBAC requests. Additionally, RBAC is enhanced to include contextual access control features such as location-based restrictions, IP-based restrictions, and request-consistency-based restrictions.Due to these operations, the proposed model is able to improve the efficiency of access control by 9.5%, while improving the speed of access by 3.5%, and reduce computational overloads by 8.3% when compared with existing access control models on large-scale cloud deployments. This performance was also observed to be consistent even under heterogenous access-control attacks.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Assessment of IoT Networks Using the Connected Random Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In order to determine how secure an Internet of Things (IoT) network is, this article suggests a way to find all the affected devices with IP addresses at the same time. The Associated RNN (ARNN) is a recurrent structure that utilizes a particular Random Neural Network (RNN) design, which consists of two sub-networks that are mutually associated and complement each other. Two separate neurons of the ARNN support opposing opinions for every one of the n gadgets or IP addresses that exist in the IoT network: compromised or not hacked. Pairs of neurons in a fully-connected 2n ARNN structure may learn from real-world information even when power is off. A single overall attack detector is provided by the ARNN, which learns about the interdependencies among network nodes, observes the incoming traffic at each node, and formulates a recommendation for every gadget or IP address in an IoT network using the feature selection (Artificial Bee Colony Optimization) method. This eliminates the need for a separate attack detector at each network node. We go over the ARNN learning algorithm and weight initialization, and then we test it with real-world attack data and compare its results to those of other testing and learning methods. Using ground truth data offline and an improved average metric collected from entering packet traffic for online incremental learning, results are produced for both scenarios. The ARNN surpasses all prior methods by a wide margin when compared to the top state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Optimizing Data Lakes for High-Performance Analytics in Big Data Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized framework for data lakes meant to enhance parameters like data rate, response time, and capacity in big data environments. Some common issues with traditional data lakes include issues of slow data access, and basic problem of scalability that becomes an issue as data sizes increase. These challenges are however countered by the proposed method through the use of distributed data structures of data, indexing quality, concurrent processing and in memory computing. The results obtained are 40% time saving in retrieving large data set and 50% improvement in query response time for heavy data. This in-memory processed system exhibited up to 60% gain in data throughput and achieved better scalability with shorter query response time as more parallel processing nodes were added. The evidences derived from the experiment clearly explain that the proposed method not only improves the performance but also offers cost efficient solution for the organizations those are dealing with big real time data analytics. Subsequent studies may involve the exploration of higher levels of machine learning to enhance the predictability of the analytical approaches used and optimal resource allocation to improved data lake underway in the cloud.

articleTitle: Designing A Hybrid Deep Learning Methodology for Arabic Text Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The process of automatically assigning relevant labels to a corpus of text is known as text categorization. Single-label text categorization is used when there is only one label to use when sorting the content. There are challenges with the multi-label form, however. The lack of large publicly accessible Arabic rich and rational datasets complicates both of these endeavours. Therefore, we provide novel, comprehensive, and objective Arabic text categorization datasets, both multi-label (NADiA) & single-label (SANAD). Both corpora are freely available for use by researchers in the area of computational linguistics applied to the Arabic language. We provide a Hybrid Deep Learning (HDL) method for text in Arabic classification using Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) & Gated Recurrent Neural Network (GRU), which may be used to assess the efficacy of such models on SANAD and NADiA. In contrast to previous studies, our method relies only on deep learning algorithms and does not include any pre-processing. We also attempted to use word2vec embed models to enhance classification precision. The largest number of groups that attention-GRU correctly classified on NADiA's "Masrawy" database was ten, and its average overall accuracy was 88.68%.

articleTitle: Optimized Echo State Network-Based Deep Learning Model for Intrusion Detection in Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of wireless networks, the need for robust security measures is critical due to the rise in network intrusions and security threats. This paper introduces a novel intrusion detection system (IDS) based on Echo State Networks (ESNs), a type of reservoir computing model known for its training efficiency and ability to process temporal patterns. Our proposed ESN-based IDS is designed to detect and classify network intrusions with high accuracy while maintaining low computational costs. By training the model on datasets containing both normal and malicious network activity, we ensure its robustness against various attack types. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that the ESN-based IDS outperform traditional machine learning methods in terms of detection accuracy, false positives, and response time. The lightweight nature of ESNs makes them suitable for resource-constrained environments, making this approach an effective solution for securing wireless networks.

articleTitle: Serial Peripheral Interface with SOC Using Universal Verification Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The Scalability and complexity nature of the integrated circuit design makes the verification process more complicated and time-consuming. Therefore, there is a strong need for verification architecture with increased reusability and easy accessibility in today's modern day SOC. The UVM methodology -based verification architecture with reusable components is one of the widely accepted test bench architecture for carrying out such functional verification.. In addition, by using a result comparison function and limiting the frequency of accidental excitation it is possible to fully verify the SPI function at minimum percentage coverage rate. We can increase the efficiency of code coverage and functional coverage through the SPI interface. Full verification of the SPI function, with a coverage rate of 95.64 %, has been achieved through the use of a constrained random excitation and an automatic result comparison function. Lastly, a successful migration to the SOC verification environment has been achieved for the SPI module's validation environment.

articleTitle: Real-Time Text Classification Algorithm Based On Combined Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Web text categorization is a prominent area of research and a vital technology in the fields of Web information retrieval and data mining. A great deal of attention and quick progress in this field has occurred in recent years. One sort of deep learning model that has been more useful for extracting important characteristics from textual input while reducing model complexity is the convolutional neural network (CNN). In the meanwhile, a time-tested machine learning method known as support vector machine (SVM) has a stellar reputation for reliability and accuracy. By merging an improved CNN with SVM, this research suggests a new method for Web text categorization. Text characteristics are extracted using the CNN model, which has a five-layer network structure. These features are then used for classification as well as forecasting using SVM. This method presents a new approach to Web text categorization using enhanced models by combining the capabilities of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and support vector machines (SVMs). Applying this method to datasets with mixed text yields outstanding results, all things considered.

articleTitle: Video Compression System for Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: While traditional software-based solutions frequently result in excessive power consumption and limited battery life, video compression is essential for optimizing bandwidth and improving user experiences in mobile applications. To overcome these limitations, the low-power FPGA-based video compression system proposed in the study makes use of the H.265/HEVC method. The FPGA-based system uses hardware-level parallelism to provide significant energy savings and higher performance, in contrast to current approaches that rely on general-purpose CPUs and GPUs, which are inefficient for parallel processing workloads. With a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 45.2 dB and a 50:1 compression ratio, the implementation shows a 60% reduction in power consumption over software-based H.264/AVC. Furthermore, processing at 60 frames per second with a 16-millisecond latency per frame, the FPGA-based system surpasses existing methods in terms of speed and efficiency. Providing enhanced energy efficiency and real-time processing capabilities, the implementation marks a significant breakthrough in video compression technology for mobile applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Parallel Prefix Adders using 90nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of delay performance in four distinct adder architectures: Brent-Kung, Ladner-Fischer, Han-Carlson, Kogge-Stone, and Ripple Carry Adder. Adders are fundamental components in digital circuits, crucial for efficient arithmetic operations in various computational systems. Each architecture employs unique design strategies to optimize carry propagation, influencing their overall speed and efficiency. The Ripple Carry Adder, with its straightforward sequential design, serves as a baseline for comparison, while the parallel-prefix architectures of Brent-Kung, Ladner-Fischer, Han-Carlson and Kogge-Stone Adders offer advanced solutions for reducing delay and improving Power-Efficiency. Through detailed simulations and analysis using Cadence Virtuoso, the Delay, Power-Efficiency and transistor count characteristics of each adder are evaluated, highlighting their strengths and tradeoffs. This study includes the design, simulation, and performance evaluation of these adder architectures using 90 nanometer technology, aiming to provide a comprehensive comparison that guides the selection of optimal adder designs for high-performance digital applications.

articleTitle: The Impact of TikTok Shop Live Streaming on Generation Z Consumer Behavior in Purchase Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study explores the impact of TikTok Shop live streaming on the purchase decision-making processes of Generation Z consumers. Using the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research examines how perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, and the physical attractiveness of streamers influence consumer attitudes and intentions. A quantitative analysis of 255 Generation Z TikTok users from the Jabodetabek area reveals significant positive relationships between these factors and consumer attitudes, subsequently affecting their watching and purchase intentions. Specifically, the study finds that: (1) Perceived ease of use and usefulness of the TikTok Shop platform, along with the attractiveness of streamers, significantly enhance positive attitudes toward live streaming commerce. (2) These attitudes are critical in shaping both watching and purchase intentions, highlighting the importance of engaging and visually appealing content. (3) Attitudes mediate the relationship between physical attractiveness and purchase intentions, suggesting that appealing streamers can enhance product desirability, especially for visually oriented products. This study provides valuable insights for marketers and platform developers aiming to optimize live streaming shopping experiences for consumers, especially Generation Z.

articleTitle: Optimizing Task Offloading Efficiency in Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access-Enabled Edge Computing Networks Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Edge computing shows potential, in supporting applications that require computation in wireless networks. Alongside advancements in edge computing, nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has emerged as a way to improve spectrum efficiency. This study discusses an edge computing system where various edge devices utilize NOMA to coordinate their tasks with a central edge node that has computational resources for task processing. This framework involves coordinating task scheduling allocating resources and managing power distribution to minimize costs, which include delay and energy consumption. Understanding the balance between energy usage and delay is essential, in this context. It is challenging to Find the best practice for this complex combinatorial optimization problem is a real challenge. To deal with this, we offer an online knowledge-based optimization system leveraging Deep Reinforcement Learning.Our simulation results investigate and compare with the previous works on the basis of reducing the cost, resource allocation, task scheduling and proper power distribution.

articleTitle: Future Directions in Recommender System: Opportunities for Improving Recommender Systems using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Recommender systems (RS) are algorithms which provides the users with customized suggestions for the things that are most relevant to them. The vast expansion of internet content accessibility has left users with an excessive array of options. It is therefore crucial for web platforms to offer recommendations of items to each user, in order to increase user satisfaction and engagement. This paper offers a thorough overview of the main difficulties and issues encountered in the development of recommender systems, as well as a synopsis of recent research findings and solutions. Paper began with a basic overview of recommender systems, briefly outlining the many types of RSs and covered the various research projects completed to date by numerous researchers, along with their conclusions and summaries, in the related work chapter. In the next section, we conducted an exploratory analysis of the many issues and potential fixes pertaining to recommender systems. Finally, we have summed up the various metrics needed to assess recommender system quality.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Reconfiguration System-Friendly Vertical Handover Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Relaying information without accurately understanding the resource and service needs of the newly relocated node is a major obstacle to providing a smooth communication system during vertical handover in heterogeneous networks. There may be a lack of study on the topic of smooth vertical handover, according to the literature review. This research proposes a new technique for vertical handover in heterogeneous integrated networks that uses multi-attribute and neural networks. By navigating among UMTS, GPRS, WLAN, 4G, and 5G, we build the algorithm's framework according to the network environment. In order to set the input layer neurons of the BP neural network and train and learn from subsequent data, each network constructs a unique Q-Learning (Reinforcement Learning) model. Reference objects used in this process include the highest possible transmission rate, the minimum delay, SINR (signal to noise and interference ratio), bit error rate, user moving velocity, and packet loss rate, all of which can impact the wireless network's overall performance. In the end, the five wireless connections are evaluated based on the network download rate, which is used as a forecast goal. Then, the algorithm for vertical handover will choose the correct wireless network to make the choice. This research presents a vertical handover method that, according to MATLAB simulation results, enables efficient handover with seamless connection across multi-heterogeneous networks with a handover success rate of up to 90%.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-based IoT-Verifiable Query Service for Efficient and Authentic Data Retrieval in Cloud Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The integration of blockchain technology into various sectors has shown promise in enhancing security and data integrity, particularly in Internet of Things (IoT) systems. However, this amalgamation introduces challenges in data query efficiency and authenticity, especially in cloud-based settings. While blockchain offers operational streamlining and robust security, its inherent architecture involving distributed ledgers and consensus algorithms poses efficiency issues in data querying. This paper addresses the critical challenge of balancing query efficiency and data authenticity in Internet of Things (IoT)-based cloud systems. Existing solutions often lack scalability, real-time efficiency, and adaptability to the unique constraints of IoT environments. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces the IoT-Verifiable Query Service (IoT-VQS), a scalable and secure architecture optimized for real-time data querying and verification in blockchains. This architecture demonstrates high throughput and verification accuracy, desirable for real-time cloud based applications.

articleTitle: A Network for Medical Segmentation of Images with Multiple Centers That Preserves Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: An innovative system for safe medical image segmentation in multi-center collaborations, the Multi-Center Privacy-Preserving Network is introduced in this research. Reduce data transmission traffic while improving data privacy protection with our methodology’s novel method for multi-center collaborative learning. Our solution relies on a single encrypted data transfer, as opposed to federated learning’s round-by-round model data communication among the central server as well as local servers. The suggested CNN is a three-layer architecture that includes networks for encryption, segmentation, and decryption. Consequently, we provide a method for secure and adaptable cloud-based medical picture segmentation using a convolutional neural network. This research demonstrates that three cloud-based servers can train the algorithm using user-provided photos; nevertheless, they are unable to access comprehensive data on the model’s variables and user input. The experiment verifies that the technique, when put into effect, can guarantee the system’s security and efficiency while simultaneously reducing the user’s compute and storage loads. We use an encryption network to transform the raw picture data into ciphertext, and then we present a refined U-Net to separate the encrypted image data. The last step is to use a decryption network to get the segmentation mask. Computable image encryption is made possible by this design, which allows for ciphertext-based picture segmentation. We test our method on three datasets, one of which is a CTPA dataset, and two of which are cardiac MRI datasets. We show that MP-Net may safely use data from many sources to build a more accurate and comprehensive segmentation model.

articleTitle: Development and Implementation of a Secure Document Analysis and Chatbot System for Context-Aware User Interactionsr
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In an period where advanced communication and archive administration are progressively crucial, the integration of secure frameworks with progressed AI-driven advances is basic. This venture centers on the advancement and execution of a secure archive investigation and chatbot framework that leverages context-aware client intelligent. The framework is outlined to improve client encounter by guaranteeing that intelligent are both secure and profoundly significant to the user’s needs. By utilizing cutting-edge machine learning models and normal dialect preparing methods, the chatbot can get it and translate the setting of client inquiries, giving exact and context-sensitive responses. Security is a basic angle of the framework, with vigorous encryption and information security components coordinates into the record examination prepare. This guarantees that delicate data is dealt with with the most noteworthy level of privacy and judgment. The framework too highlights a energetic learning component, permitting the chatbot to adjust to advancing client necessities and developing security dangers. Through the combination of secure archive investigation and brilliantly, context-aware intuitive, this extend points to make a solid and productive apparatus for organizations that bargain with huge volumes of delicate information. The execution illustrates the potential of AI-driven chatbots in upgrading secure communication and record administration forms.

articleTitle: Communication Technologies for AMI: A Testing Analysis Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Across India, power utilities are transitioning from conventional energy meters to smart energy meters due to the numerous advantages of smart meters, including bidirectional communication, real-time energy consumption data, and accurate billing. The Government of India is actively promoting the deployment of prepaid smart meters and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) through various government-funded initiatives.
