By taking advantage of the opportunity costs associated with wiretapping and jamming, an eavesdropper may use OWJ to launch a more dangerous assault. Additionally, we provide three OWJ assault realizations, with the distance-, path-, and received-power-related cost models serving as the primary determinants. First, we provide new approximation methods to describe the uneven distributions of wiretappers, jammers, and interferers under three OWJ conclusions. This will help us understand how the new assault affects the security of mmWave networks. We illustrate the network's security effectiveness under OWJ by deriving analytical formulas for the secrecy capacity of transmission using the findings of the node distributions. Last but not least, we provide comprehensive numerical findings to show how OWJ works and how this novel attack might worsen network security performance compared to pure wiretapping or jammer attacks.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Secure Information Transmission Using Cryptography Multi layer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this proposed work, a new strategy for improving data security is presented. This approach makes use of multilayer Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) cryptographic algorithms. The purpose of this approach is to reduce the widespread risk of data hacking. The One Time Pad (OTP) algorithm, which was created within a multilayer framework, is included in the suggested system. This algorithm is responsible for regulating the transmission of signals within the mode of communication. Seed values are obtained from a Pseudorandom Noise (PN) sequence that is created by a basic polynomial. These seed values are used to initialize the functionality of the One-Time Password scheme. As an additional point of interest, this research investigates the analysis of single-layered LFSR cryptography and compares it to a cascaded LFSR encryption approach to assess the effectiveness of preserving digitized data. Within the scope of LFSR cascaded cryptography, authentication key generation circuits that cater to varied degrees of bit handling in data communication systems are designed. This makes it possible for robust encryption and decryption operations to be carried out. The cascaded multilayer cryptography system is subjected to a comprehensive analysis to determine whether or not it has the capability of enhancing data security. Evaluation parameters spanning operating frequency, power consumption, latency, and memory utilization illustrate the applicability of this technique for the creation of modern network-based applications.

articleTitle: LSTM-Based Jamming Diagnosis and Prediction Model Utilizing Transport in Wi-Fi-Enabled IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Every industry is seeing a rise in the use of the Internet of Things (IoT). Because of its widespread availability, high bandwidth, low cost, and adaptability, Wi-Fi-based communication is favored by wireless IoT devices. However, serious dangers exist due to security flaws in IoT devices, particularly in mission-critical and industrial settings. With an emphasis on industrial communication and environmental dynamics, this article introduces a new method for detecting jamming in the Internet of Things (IoT). Using production lines that include wireless IoT devices with a server-client architecture, it first focuses on collecting connection parameters and quality of service (QoS) during normal communication and jamming attacks so that it can more effectively investigate the communication conditions along with jamming in the industrial production environment. Results from experiments show that spot jamming has a devastating effect on higher-level protocol layers, showing that physical-layer jamming assaults may cause transport and application-layer failures to cascade. This research introduces a novel multi-layer jamming detection model based on stacked Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). With its strong performance in real-time applications for IoT and impressive accuracy in anticipating jamming attempts, the suggested LSTM model is a clear winner. The model undergoes testing on a real-time experimental testbed that simulates different sorts of jamming assaults after being trained on a dataset that has been meticulously selected. A 99.5% accuracy rate for jamming detection and a 99.4% precision rate were produced by the findings. This study provides new insight into the effects of jamming assaults on Internet of Things (IoT) devices and introduces a sophisticated detection model that has the potential to reduce the severity of these attacks.

articleTitle: An Internet of Things (IoT) Consumer Data Network Security Assessment that Uses Variant Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Fused CNN-Attention Bi- LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: More and more people are able to access the internet and participate in social media, leaving most companies open to a variety of threats and assaults. Consequently, intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are seen as a crucial part of network security for organizations. Their job is to detect any network breaches as soon as they occur, making them the first line of defense towards cyber-attacks. Intrusion detection systems primarily seek for harmful activity in the network by analyzing its traffic. Due to the ever-increasing demand for network services, networks nowadays are experiencing massive expansion. The created algorithms may find their application limited as a result of the different data kinds and increased network complexity caused by this growth. Also, the frequency and severity of viruses and other harmful assaults are evolving. Cybercriminals are more interested than ever before in the IoT due to its phenomenal development pace. The assertion is supported by the increasing frequency of cyberattacks targeting intermediary communication media and Internet of Things devices. Severe service disruption and financial loss may occur from attacks on the Internet of Things (IoT) that go unnoticed for a long time. Additionally, it presents a risk to one's privacy. For IoT-enabled services to be dependable, safe, and lucrative, real-time intrusion detection on IoT devices is crucial. New intrusion detection solution for Internet of Things (IoT) devices based on Deep Learning (DL) is presented in this study. To prevent assaults on linked Internet of Things (IoT) devices, this smart system employs a four-layer deep Fully Connected (FC) designing networks to identify malicious data. For easier implementation, the suggested system was built to not rely on any particular communication protocol.

articleTitle: RFID-Based Automated Bus Door System with Emergency Alert and Seat Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The main challenges of transportation include safety, efficiency and convenience in the usage of public transportation thus the need to develop the technological solutions. Presenting in this research is design and Implementation of an RFID-Based Automated Bus Door System incorporating Emergency Alert and Seat Monitoring. Incorporation of RFID technology means that bus doors will open and close automatically excluding unwanted elements from accessing the bus. Another real-time feature is integrated in the program which deals with seats to avoid overcrowding of passengers. Further, there is an added emergency alerting system that exists to quickly respond in case of an emergency thus making passenger safety better. The structure of the system is developed to feature a microcontroller as the control unit and is also responsible for handling data transfers between RFID readers, seat sensors, and alerts. The prototype model developed herein proves that, indeed these technologies can complement each other and be harnessed in a compounded manner, hence forming one interconnected system. The proposed techniques has an experimental complexity of response time with having 60 percent improvement as compared to traditional methods for response times of 210ms, 95 percent accuracy for seat occupancy detection and an energy improvement of 12 percent as compared to traditional methods. The results indicate that the RFID Based Automatic Bus Door System can provide a solid viable solution to upgrade the public transports, enhancing the organizational effectiveness and security of the passengers.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Packet Delivery Ratio Improvement Protocol Design over 5G Assisted Wireless Sensor Network Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Sensors are pervasive in modern life, and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) will play an increasingly important role in the years to come. Broadband, energy, coverage, and route optimization resource shortages are WSN's main drawbacks. Optimizing the packet delivery ratio is a crucial aspect of wireless sensor network (WSN) architecture. In order to enhance WSNs over the long term, previous approaches used a secure zone-based routing mechanism. For packet transmission, a new criterion was developed in multi-hop communication. It was built into the routing metric to protect against flooding, message manipulation, and dropping attacks. Congestion in WSN increases and reduces packet delivery ratio, even while energy conservation and attack resilience are accomplished. Our proposed solution, Advanced Path Selection with Traffic Estimation (APSTE), is a new way of routing data packets that takes flow differentiation into account. This should help increase the packet delivery ratio and solve this issue. In order to determine how effective, the suggested method is, it is cross-validated using the standard routing model known as Link Consistency with Path Evaluation (LCPE). In order to improve the WSN's QoS parameters and extend the network's lifespan, the APSTE approach reduces the energy consumption of sensor nodes while maintaining or improving their logical throughput and packet acquisition rates.

articleTitle: Innovative Techniques in the Construction of Very Large Scale Integration Circuits for Low-Power and High-Performance Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Portable electronic gadgets and high-performance computing systems have increased demand for low-power, high-performance integrated circuits (ICs). VLSI technology, which creates integrated circuits with dozens to millions of transistors on a chip, is leading these efforts. This research investigates low-power, high-performance VLSI circuit construction methods. We start with VLSI design fundamentals and power management and performance optimization concerns. The constraints of traditional VLSI design methods in satisfying current electronics' strict requirements are examined. VLSI design methodology development and evaluation are the focus of this research. Advanced power optimization methods include MTCMOS, adaptive body biasing, and power gating. We also study clock tree improvement, signal integrity enhancement, and new materials and device topologies for high performance. In addition, we study how machine learning techniques automate and optimize circuit placement, routing, and timing in VLSI design. AI handles the complexity of current VLSI designs and finds optimal design parameters for minimal power and high performance. Scaling VLSI circuits to newer technology nodes raises process variance, leakage current, and thermal management difficulties, which the research tackles. These issues can be overcome with new ways to keep VLSI circuits scaling while preserving performance and power efficiency. Finally, case studies and experimental findings show that the offered methods work in real-world applications. These findings demonstrate significant power usage and performance benefits over typical VLSI design. In conclusion, our research advances VLSI technology by developing low-power, high-performance integrated circuits. The proposed VLSI design methods and solutions could lead to more efficient and powerful electronic systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Customer Emotion Detection in Online Shopping: A CNN and BiLSTM-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Creating a mimicked environment while shopping online is becoming more common, and the majority of transactions are now conducted online. Recent innovations in e-commerce and business have made it critical to offer personalized online suggestions based on emotion prediction to users or consumers. A person's facial emotions are easy to read, but creating an algorithm that can accomplish the same thing is a huge challenge. Using facial expressions as a basis for emotion recognition, this proposed suggests a new approach for online recommendation systems. The proposed approach includes three steps: detecting faces, extracting facial features, and training the model. Because every person's face is unique, using facial detection to just identify when someone is in the room can be a challenging undertaking. In order to change the look of a person's face, whether permanent or temporary, facial feature extraction is performed. When the facial muscles are contracted, it affects the direction and amplitude of skin surface displacement. The proposed approach used CNN-BiLSTM for the model's training. This cutting-edge method outperforms BiLSTM and CNN with an average accuracy of 91.62%.

articleTitle: Scaling Intelligent Systems with Multi- Channel Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG): A robust Framework for Context Aware Knowledge Retrieval and Text Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Current intelligent systems cannot suitably preserve context accuracy, mainly at scale to complex, real-world applications though they could produce text and retrieve knowledge. In more specific terms, the common model tends to rely on single-channel retrieval approaches, and these are ineffective at taking into account a variety of heterogeneous, domain-specific sources of data that may culminate in suboptimal responses and unresponsiveness in changing contexts. Indeed, most currently existing systems cannot support real-time interaction and dynamic decision-making, which would hinder their ability to deliver the effective personalized content as well as complex question answering. In order to overcome the said limitations, this paper puts forward an effective RAG framework for Multi-Channel Retrieval Augmented Generation (MC-RAG), which enhances both context-aware knowledge retrieval and text generation. Designed with the capacity to incorporate multiple channels of retrieval from structured or unstructured data sources, the multi-channel approach allows dynamic adaptation of relevant information for evolving contexts about a query. This is most effective as generated responses are significantly more accurate and relevant while also providing more personalized interactions for end-users.The proposed Mc-RAG system is scalable and better than other solutions regarding the handling of a wide range of knowledge domains, thus being appropriate for such applications as personalized content delivery, advanced question answering, and decision support. This approach, focusing on real-time context-aware interactions and based on the given framework, offers a complete solution in terms of designing intelligent systems that can be used for navigation in complex, dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A Multi-Condition Health Prediction Model Based on Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Based on a patient's medical history and symptoms, the several Disease Prediction System using Machine Learning is an innovative healthcare application that uses machine learning algorithms to properly forecast the chance of a patient having several diseases. The system uses a large dataset of medical records and illness symptoms, which are analyzed using machine learning methods including random forests, decision trees, and support vector machines. Because of the great accuracy of the system's predictions, medical practitioners may use them to make better judgments and provide patients with better treatment regimens. Through early illness prediction and prevention, the Multiple illness Prediction System with Machine Learning has the potential to improve healthcare outcomes and reduce costs. Using machine learning methods such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, and SVM, the program aims to develop an advanced illness prediction model. This approach focuses on common illnesses including diabetes, heart disease, liver disease, and breast cancer. The system seeks to deliver precise forecasts by utilizing these algorithms' capabilities, allowing for preemptive treatments and individualized healthcare plans. The all-inclusive strategy tackles a range of medical issues, demonstrating the potential influence of machine learning on improving healthcare delivery and resource efficiency.

articleTitle: Network Intrusion Detection System for Smart Environments with High performing Novel Feature Selection Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has experienced significant growth in data traffic, resulting in increased complexity and dimensionality. Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) play a vital role in protecting against various types of cyber threats. IoT IDS systems encounter major challenges because of the varied functionality and physical diversity within IoT environments. The vast and ever-changing nature of IoT traffic makes it challenging and impractical to utilize all features and attributes for effective self-protection in IDS. To tackle these challenges, this study presents AN-SFS: A Dynamic and Adaptive Method for Optimal Feature Selection that adjusts to local data statistics. As opposed to standard approaches, AN-SFS modifies its threshold based on current feature subsets and neighboring feature statistics, enhancing its ability to capture subtle relationships and dependencies for more robust and effective selection. We assessed our model using the CSECICIDS-2018 dataset and found it to outperform traditional machine learning classifiers in detection rate, precision, and recall. It achieved an exceptional accuracy rate of 99.9% and a low false positive rate of 0.022, markedly exceeding the performance of current methods.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enhanced Data Integrity and Authentication in WSN-IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: WSNs together with IoT have become more susceptible to security threats owing to their distributed and resource constraint nature. Maintaining data consistency and strong authentication in these systems is important especially for applications that require low latency. This paper aims to evaluate how blockchain technology can be incorporated to improve security of data in WSN-IoT architecture for better data verification. We discuss existing solutions, identify emerging problems, and present a blockchain-based solution to these problems. Some of our contributions include a comprehensive discussion on the effect of blockchain technology on security parameters including latency, scalability and resource usage. The proposed approach shows that there is a notable enhancement of data quality preservation and security risks minimization in WSN-IoT.

articleTitle: LSB based Image Steganography with Password-Protected SMTP Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Picture steganography plays a crucial role in secure communication by discreetly altering images for various purposes such as data authentication, privacy protection, and watermarking. However, traditional methods often lack resistance to manipulation. To address this, we propose a solution that merges automated password generation with the Least Significant Bit (LSB) approach. This method involves embedding text within images and automatically generating an encryption password to safeguard data security. By employing Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) credentials, encrypted photos can be directly sent to recipients, significantly expediting the process. This automated approach eliminates the necessity for separate transfers of the image and decryption password, thereby enhancing simplicity and security. This new technology seamlessly integrates encryption, ensuring a trustworthy and secure communication channel. With this innovative solution, users can transmit sensitive information confidently, knowing that it is shielded from unauthorized access or manipulation. By combining the strengths of automated password generation, LSB steganography, and SMTP transmission, our approach provides a robust framework for safeguarding digital communication in various context.

articleTitle: Research on Digital Live Broadcast Recommendation System Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In view of the limitations of the traditional Depth-first search algorithm in research on digital live broadcast recommendation system, a research scheme of research on the live broadcast recommendation system based on Artificial intelligence was proposed. Firstly, the influencing factors is accurately located through computer science dispensing theories, and the indicators is reasonably divided to reduce interference, and the Artificial intelligence is used to construct a research scheme for research on the live broadcast recommendation system. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the proposed scheme is superior to the traditional Depth-first search algorithm in terms of research accuracy and processing time of influencing factors of research on the live broadcast recommendation system, and has obvious advantages. The research of research on the live broadcast recommendation system plays an extremely important role in digital live, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth characteristics and product generation of digital live. However, the traditional Depth-first search algorithm has some limitations in solving the problem of recommended system simulation, especially when dealing with complex problems. In this paper, this paper proposes a research scheme of research on the live broadcast recommendation system based on Artificial intelligence to better solve this problem. The scheme accurately locates the influencing factors through computer science dispensing theories, so as to determine the division of indicators, and uses the Artificial intelligence to construct the scheme. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the accuracy and speed of the scheme is significantly improved for different problems, and it has better performance. Therefore, the simulation scheme based on Artificial intelligence in research on digital live broadcast recommendation system can better solve the limitations of traditional Depth-first search algorithm and improve the simulation accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Improved Attack Detection and Analysis in IoT Environment Data Derived from Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The interconnection and communication capabilities of many smart gadgets are made possible by the Internet of Things. Despite the practical advantages of the Internet of Things (IoT), it is susceptible to new forms of assaults due to the introduction of new technology. Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) need a lot of resources to determine the kind of assaults due to the complicated networks and vast amounts of data generated by the Internet of Things (IoT). In contrast, most intrusion detection methods are impractical for IoT networks due to the fact that these networks need greater computational resources for attack detection, which are in short supply on IoT devices. As a result, you need an intrusion detection system (IDS) that isn't too heavy yet can still detect emerging threats. In contrast, most intrusion detection methods are impractical for IoT networks due to the fact that these networks need greater computational capacity for attack detection, which are in short supply on IoT devices. As a result, you need an intrusion detection system (IDS) that isn't too heavy yet can still detect emerging threats. This study recommends a combination of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Random Forest to optimize detection performance while simultaneously reducing network complexity via the efficient elimination of unnecessary features. Applying hold-out, Stratified k-fold cross-validation, as well as percentage split test mode on the CICIDS-2017 dataset MachineLearning CSV version, the suggested IDS is verified with testing and training data. We opted for this dataset since it contains actual data from IoT networks. The suggested hybrid IDS shows promising experimental results for performance enhancement. Recall values average out to 1.000, resulting in an accuracy rating of 99.9%.

articleTitle: Fraud Detection using Quantum Machine Learning(QML)
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Fraud detection is a Crucial aspect of securing financial systems and protecting against fraudulent activities. This paper presents a new method for Detecting fraud, combining quantum-inspired feature engineering and neural network modeling, which achieves a classification accuracy of 92%, with a precision and recall of 0.92 for non-fraudulent transactions. Utilizing QuantumCircuit from Qiskit, the approach encodes input features into quantum states through angle encoding, improving data representation and capturing complex feature interactions such as entanglement between qubits. The method employs a Quantum Neural Network (QNN) for classifying records and effectively identifying fraudulent transactions. Through real-world dataset experiments, we demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach, achieving a precision of 0.65 and recall of 0.68 for fraudulent transactions, while maintaining a false positive rate below 10%. This research leverages advanced machine learning techniques, including balanced sampling strategies to address class imbalance and hyperparameter tuning with Grid-SearchCV for optimal model performance. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the approach, highlighting its strengths in adapting to dynamic and complex environments. Quantum-inspired methods offer the potential to significantly enhance fraud detection systems. However, challenges such as computational complexity and resource requirements remain areas for further investigation. Future research will aim to scale these models for larger datasets and investigate their applicability in fields such as healthcare and e-commerce. In conclusion, our work demonstrates the promising use of quantum-enhanced machine learning for fraud detection. This innovative approach paves the way for developing advanced detection systems that can effectively respond to the evolving landscape of fraudulent activities. Future studies could concentrate on refining these techniques and exploring their potential applications in other areas to further harness the advantages of quantum computing in machine learning.

articleTitle: Analyzing Bit Error Rate Performance in Downlink Cooperative NOMA Systems with Various Modulation Techniques across Varied Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Incorporating cooperative communication into Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) networks, known as cooperative NOMA, is driven by the goal of enhancing network scalability while maintaining fair resource allocation. This approach seeks to enhance the efficiency of NOMA-based networks by leveraging cooperative strategies among users, thereby enabling fair allocation of network resources. This study investigates the performance of cooperative NOMA in comparison to alternative techniques, particularly focusing on far and near user scenarios. The research explores various nonfading and fading methods in conjunction with different modulation schemes to assess the Bit Error Rate (BER) in far and near user NOMA setups. Specifically, comparisons are made among BPSK, QPSK, and 16QAM modulation techniques, considering the impact of Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channels. Additionally, the study extends its analysis by employing BPSK and QPSK schemes across different fading channels, including Rayleigh, Rician, log-normal, and Weibull channels. The BER performance is evaluated concerning transmit power for both far and near user NOMA configurations. Using MATLAB simulations, BER performances are evaluated, and a comparative examination of BER under various environments is provided.

articleTitle: An Improved Hierarchical Control Strategy for Power Management in Islanded Hybrid Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Power management and control through a hierarchical control strategy in a Hybrid Micro Grid (HMG) consisting of multiple AC and DC small Micro Grids (MG) with different voltage ratings are focussed of this research. The ultimate aim of the proposed power management strategy is to limit the continuous operation of Interlink (IL)in different load conditions. Hence, the power loss at the IL converters are reduced, orelse it may affect the operational stability of the HMG. The hierarchical control strategy for power management and coordination for islanded mode of HMG is implemented and analysed. The designed system consists of primary and secondary control levels, that provides an accurate power transfer among the small MGs. The new methodology ensure a continuous power flow within the small MGs with minimal operation of IL converter.

articleTitle: A Voting Ensemble Learning Model for Improved Credit Default Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Credit risk prediction is one of the most rudimentary pillars for practices in financial institutions. In order to maintain sound financial health and support the long-term safety of the institution, a strong framework for credit default risk evaluation is necessary. A strong credit default risk forecasting framework ensures financial institutions expand their lending activities and explore new markets. In different cities across the world, loan defaults in financial institutions result in adverse impacts such as financial losses, reduced profitability, and capital adequacy ratios. Therefore, it is high time to overcome traditional credit evaluation methods that are being followed in several financial institutions till date. This paper thoroughly evaluates the loan default prediction methodologies or similar assessment techniques proposed till date. Exploring all the best possible machine learning (ML) techniques, this paper proposes a soft-voting ensemble model combining three different (Random Forest, XG Boost, Gradient Boosting) and high-performing models to forecast credit default risks ensuring safety and success in institutional lending activities, evaluating creditworthiness of the borrower. The dataset was acquired from Kaggle. Following data preprocessing, the processed data was trained into the proposed ensemble model, followed by hyperparameter tuning, evaluation, and deployment of the model. The evaluation metrics include the F1 score, recall rate, accuracy, AUC-ROC and model precision. The final data visualizations portray the comparisons and the benefits of using this model across different financial institutions.

articleTitle: Assessment of Photoplethysmography Signals using Customized Wavelet and Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is frequently influenced by interference, potentially resulting in inaccurate interpretation of physiological data. Hence, it is essential to conduct a quality assessment prior to extracting this information. This paper introduces a novel method for assessing PPG signal quality that combines multi-class features with multi-scale series information this approach overcomes the limitations of conventional machine learning methods, which tend to suffer from low accuracy, and deep learning methods that demand large training datasets. By extracting multi-class features, the reliance on sample size is reduced, while multi-scale series information is captured through a fusion of multi-scale wavelet transforms and deep learning techniques. The proposed method achieved the better accuracy of 98.3%, surpassing six other quality assessment methods across all metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score, based on 14,700 samples from seven experiments. This paper introduces a novel approach for quality assessment and information extraction in small PPG signal samples, showing potential for accurate monitoring and analysis of clinical and everyday PPG physiological data.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Life Expectancy Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Life expectancy, a pivotal public health measure, indicates the average lifespan based on current mortality rates and reflects societal well-being. Over the last century, it has significantly increased due to medical advancements, improved living standards, and public health initiatives. Factors like healthcare quality, lifestyle, social status, and environment have profound influence on this improvement in Life Expectancy. However, disparities persist due to uneven access to healthcare, education, and jobs. This study deploys various machine learning models, to predict life expectancy, achieving an adjusted R-squared value of 0.9729 by Extra Tree Regression, indicating exceptional model accuracy. By analyzing a comprehensive dataset, socio-economic, health, and environmental factors such as GDP per capita, composition of resources, education levels etc., were identified as key predictors of life expectancy by the model. The high R-squared value highlights the model's robustness in capturing dynamic relationships between these variables and life expectancy.

articleTitle: AI and IOT Integration for Enhanced Pesticide Detection in Organic Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Pesticide contamination in the agricultural sector is impacting public health due to its extensive use food, drinking water, and the environment has become one of the world's most serious issues for human public health. As a result, it is crucial and necessary to identify and analyze pesticides in food. This paper presents AI (Artificial Intelligence) and IOT (Internet of Things) Integration for Enhanced Pesticide Detection in Organic Agriculture. The goal of this project is to use sensors and Arduino technology to provide real-time pesticide level detection. This strategy highlights the significance of keeping an eye on food safety and gives customers useful information about the safety of the food they are consuming. Triad spectroscopy sensor, pH sensor and Gas sensors are used to detect the pesticide residue in the food. The Effective method and financially viable method of managing and gathering data from the sensors is integrating with Arduino platform. The system is a useful instrument in the continuous endeavor to guarantee the safety of agricultural products because of its embedded programming capabilities and real-time analytic capabilities.

Author Keywords: AI (Artificial Intelligence) and IOT (Internet of Things) Integration

articleTitle: High-Efficiency FPGA Implementation of Deep Learning Models for Colorectal Tumor Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: To meet the demand for real-time, energy-efficient solutions in medical diagnostics, this research offers a high-efficiency FPGA implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for colorectal tumor picture processing. Loop unrolling, pipelining, and effective memory use were among the methods used in the creation of the CNN model, which had an optimized system architecture. With a lowered latency of 10.2 milliseconds and power usage of 4.8 watts, the model achieved an accuracy of 98.5% during training and testing on the TCGA Colorectal Tumor Dataset. With a throughput of 120 frames per second, the implementation from 2021 to 2023 significantly outperformed earlier ones. These findings highlight the possibility of FPGA-based deep learning models to provide real-time, high-performance analysis at a lower energy cost. According to the results, this strategy not only improves diagnostic precision but also provides a practical, scalable solution for clinical setting deployment, opening the door for a wider use of FPGA-based systems in medical image processing.

Author Keywords: Rectified Linear Unit Digital Signal Processing

articleTitle: Twitter Sarcasm Detection using Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the last ten years, sarcasm detection has been an increasingly popular subject in natural language processing (NLP), which studies how language is used to convey meaning. Promising results have been achieved by a wide range of methods, from conventional computer learning to multifaceted deep learning techniques. Many methods have arisen that rely on context to determine whether or not a given piece of text contains sarcasm. However, sarcasm-context detection has not been the primary focus of any natural language processing studies. This research provides a method for automated sarcasm context detection with the goal of creating models that can accurately determine whether sarcasm is present or suitable. The Weighted Random Forest approach is used to train and compare many models for sarcasm-context detection utilising a widely used dataset (MUStARD). This top-notch performance is established as an F1 score of 60,1 achieving attention-based short-term and long- architecture. In addition, we evaluated the model's efficacy by testing it on the SARC database & contrasting the outcomes with those previously published in the literature. The possibility of creating a conversational AI that can recognise and react to sarcasm opens up new avenues of research.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IoT Enabled Smart Assistive Systems for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The use of IoT technology in healthcare systems has been adopted in patient monitoring because IoT technology has been adopted rapidly in the systems. This paper discusses on design and implementation of an IoT integrated smart assistive health care system to enhance the precision and speed of patient health assessment. In the proposed system, wearable sensors are used to capture respiratory rate, pulse rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and body temperature with data to be sent to the cloud server as and when it is received. Some of the features are, however, small data transmission delays, high accuracy in the physiological signals and long durations of monitoring due to the low power consumption. The simulations showed that the response time falls below 500ms, and physicians retain up to a 2 % variance to clinical grade devices, which actualized robust and effective patient care. The incorporation of predicting capacities, thus providing ways of early identification of health complications, makes the system applicable in chronic disease treatments and telemedicine.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical DAG-based Neural Network Approach to Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The DNN-BSA (DAG based Neural Networks for Sentiment Analysis) technique, which is used in the context of sentiment analysis, focuses on reliably recognizing opinion aspects and the sentiment polarity that correlate to those opinion features. Both stand-alone and integrated approaches of the past have proven unsuccessful in their attempts to accurately capture the intrinsic link that exists between these two goals. In order to overcome this issue, the study that we have conducted suggests the use of an innovative dynamic DAG graph that explicitly reflects the relationship that exists between aspect extraction and sentiment identification. The DAG network that we use comprises both regular words and emotion labels as linked nodes. This is how we tackle the problem. This approach enables interaction between aspect words and emotion information to take place in a fluid manner. During the process of real-time prediction, the graph is dynamically changed after being initialized with many distinct types of dependencies. The performance of our model is superior to that of other state-of-the-art models, as demonstrated by numerous tests conducted on benchmark datasets. In addition, in-depth examination suggests that our model exhibits considerable gains when dealing with difficult scenarios that involve multiple-opinion aspects as well as circumstances in which there is no opinion element present. This demonstrates how resilient and successful our methodology is in dealing with difficult sentiment analysis assignments.

articleTitle: Research on System for Locating Art Layout Resources Based on Interactive Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The first positioning system is an important part of art design, which has guidance for the analysis of the whole art design and art indicators. Therefore, the positioning system can enter the artistic creation more accurately. In view of the limitations of the traditional decision tree algorithm in application in art and design, a research scheme of application in design based on Interactive genetic algorithm was proposed. Firstly, the influencing factors is accurately located through Interactive evaluation theories, and the indicators is reasonably divided to reduce interference, and the Interactive genetic algorithm is used to construct a research scheme for application in design. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the proposed scheme is superior to the traditional decision tree algorithm in terms of research accuracy and processing time of influencing factors of application in design, and has obvious advantages. The research of application in design plays an extremely important role in art layout , which can accurately predict and optimize the growth characteristics and product generation of art layout . However, the traditional decision tree algorithm has some limitations in solving the problem of art layout simulation, especially when dealing with complex problems. In this paper, this paper proposes a research scheme of application in design based on Interactive genetic algorithm to better solve this problem. In the whole process of research, it was found that the art positioning system can be carried out more comprehensively. design and analysis, where intelligent algorithms can improve the accuracy of the design by between 10% and 20%. Therefore, the design of the entire resource and art system can meet the actual requirements and promote the accuracy of artistic positioning. The scheme accurately locates the influencing factors through Interactive evaluation theories, so as to determine the division of indicators, and uses the Interactive genetic algorithm to construct the scheme. Experimental results show that under certain evaluation criteria, the accuracy and speed of the scheme is significantly improved for different problems, and it has better performance. Therefore, the simulation scheme based on Interactive genetic algorithm in application in art and design can better solve the limitations of traditional decision tree algorithm and improve the simulation accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Denial-of-Service Attack Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks: A Simple Artificial Intelligence Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: When compared to more conventional networks, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) stand out. Classical networks' networking techniques, in contrast to WSN, can only regulate incoming packets according to their Internet Protocol (IP) address translation. The efficient gathering and transmission of data from such a network is an essential need for any application. A Denial of Service (DoS) assault occurs when malicious actors intentionally try to disrupt the data supply process, making the anticipated services unavailable. Because denial-of-service attacks aim to disrupt regular services, they may often severely limit the use of wireless sensor networks. When malicious nodes gain access to a network, they may launch a denial-of-service (DoS) assault. Using a trust-based method, this study aims to trace these nodes that are colluding. One component of the trust-based system is a way to quantify the level of confidence in each node. Nodes that have a low level of trust are considered to be malevolent nodes. All packets sent within the given time window are considered a measure of trust. The node that forwards the most packets while leveraging the fewest assistance will be marked as malicious. By outperforming RF, XGBoost, and KNN classifiers while using less training data, the suggested method has shown strong performance. Its accuracy rate is 99.5%. Our suggested method considerably beats these classifiers in regard to processing time, since it only uses 9.7 percent, 13.1 percent, and 2% of the time that FR, XGBoost, and KNN use, respectively. Notably, RF did yield slightly better accuracy; nevertheless, the suggested method substantially outperformed RF by requiring only 9.7 percent of RF processing time, a crucial component in fulfilling WSN restrictions. We used certain performance indicators to evaluate the results after deploying the emerging architecture in NS3. The total number of packets sent by each node during their allocated time window was used to determine trust. The most spiteful node was determined to be the one that sends out the most packets while using almost minimal resources. The NS3 program is used to explain the method and analyze the outcomes using certain metrics in this task implementation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Path Planning Strategy for Robots Based on Local Dynamic Environment Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In order to solve the challenges of real-time path planning strategies for robots, in view of the shortcomings of the existing RRT algorithms, an innovative real-time path planning strategy method based on local dynamic environment perception is introduced. This new approach uses the principles of computer vision theory to accurately identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly performs a sensible classification of indicators to reduce potential interference. At the same time, by using the unique mechanism of local dynamic environment perception, the design strategy of path planning is cleverly constructed. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows significant improvement compared with the traditional RRT algorithm in key performance indicators such as the accuracy of the real-time path planning strategy and the processing efficiency of key factors, showing its obvious strong advantages. In robots, the real-time path planning strategy plays a crucial role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the robot's real-time path planning strategy. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional RRT algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of real-time path planning strategy based on local dynamic environment perception optimization, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through computer vision theory, and uses this as the road map for index allocation, and then uses local dynamic environment perception to construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the real-time path planning strategy of the robot, the simulation scheme based on local dynamic environment perception successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional RRT algorithm and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Folk Dance Classification: An Analysis of ConvLSTM and LRCN Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study looks into the classification of various folk dances from video sequences using methods for deep learning. Knowing that Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Convolutional Network (LRCN) and Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) designs are so good at capturing temporal and spatial relationships in video data, the study focuses on using them. A diverse dataset of folk-dance videos from different geographic regions and cultural contexts was curated and preprocessed into sequential image frames for model training. The ConvLSTM and LRCN models were constructed and trained using the TensorFlow/Keras framework on GPU-accelerated hardware. In this paper, analysis revealed effective learning during training, with both models demonstrating increased training accuracy and decreased training loss. However, significant fluctuations in validation accuracy and loss indicated potential overfitting and instability in generalization to unknown data. To deal with these problems, we suggest employing regularization strategies like dropout, early stopping, and further hyperparameter tuning. Future work could explore transfer learning and more diverse validation procedures to enhance model performance. Despite the challenges, this study provides a foundational approach for improving video classification systems in the rich and varied domain of folk dances.

Author Keywords: Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Convolutional Network LRCN

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Medicine Text Mining Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The proliferation of digital devices like smartphones and the Internet of Things has resulted in a flood of data. Every second, millions of bytes of data (including text, music, images, and videos) are produced. Thus, the need for big data analytics has been sparked by the current situation. Healthcare service records are an example of the large amounts of data created every day by hospitals. Information on patient symptoms, drug use, and the discovery of new illnesses, among other things, may be gleaned from this massive dataset. In this investigation, we use text processing methodology to public hospital patient record text data from 2017–2019 to better understand how diseases manifest in their patients. Preprocessing data from medical records involves using the Nave Bayes Classifier & Random Forest algorithms to categorise illnesses. To narrow down the collection of symptom statements, a list of altered Indonesian stop words was employed. Compared to the Naive Bayes classification technique. Experiments validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our suggested technique for illness classification in medical records.

articleTitle: Novel Architecture for High-performance VLSI Interconnections: Reducing Latency and Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Traditional interconnection topologies' inadequacies typically result in latency and power consumption being the limiting factors for high-performance VLSI systems. Performance and scalability are hampered by conventional systems' excessive parasitic capacitance, inductance, and signal propagation delays. Using dynamic routing techniques and cutting-edge materials to minimize parasitic effects and maximize signal transmission, the paper proposes a revolutionary interconnection architecture that overcomes these problems. With an average delay reduction of 28% and an average power consumption reduction of 22%, the proposed method outperforms conventional methods in terms of latency and power consumption. Better thermal control and a 25% increase in throughput are also achieved with the upgraded architecture, demonstrating greater performance and scalability. The efficiency of the proposed technique to navigate around the limitations of conventional VLSI linkages is demonstrated by these results.

articleTitle: Enhanced Semantic Segmentation for Triple- Negative Breast Cancer Detection Using Modified U-Net Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an exceptionally aggressive type of breast cancer defined by the absence of estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors, and HER2 expression. Timely detection and precise diagnosis are vital for effective treatment and enhanced patient outcomes. This research introduces a new strategy for improving the semantic segmentation of TNBC cells in histological images by utilizing a modified U-Net architecture. Accurately segmenting TNBC cells in histological images poses significant challenges due to the complex and heterogeneous characteristics of breast tissue. Current techniques often fall short in capturing detailed nuances and separating cancerous cells from non-cancerous tissue. To tackle these issues, we propose a modified U-Net architecture that uses "same" padding throughout the entire network. This design choice ensures that the output segmentation mask matches the dimensions of the input image, enabling more accurate localization of cancer cells. Furthermore, the U-Net's natural ability to capture both contextual information and intricate details makes it particularly suitable for this objective. Our proposed modified U-Net architecture outperformed baseline methods, achieving superior segmentation accuracy and better capturing the intricate features of TNBC cells. The implementation of "same" padding significantly contributed to improving the localization accuracy of the segmentation masks.

articleTitle: An Extremely Scalable and Versatile Learning-Oriented Blockchain Performance Optimisation Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has recently been the subject of investigation as a potential solution to security issues plaguing IoT networks. However, when dealing with a large number of IoT gadgets and the massive amounts of data produced by these networks, the inherent scalability difficulties of blockchain-based systems become obvious. Nevertheless, there are areas where the permissioned Blockchain falls short, and these include throughput and scalability. Incorporating data science methodologies, this study proposes a way to address permissioned Blockchain's scalability problem. With a variable number of transactions, the scalability study of the suggested solution is done in the hyperledger fabric architecture, which improves scalability. Because of this, we address these issues in this research by using a lightweight consensus approach. We provide a system for handling IoT data that is scalable and built on blockchain technology. It can handle data from a large number of gadgets. To guarantee improved efficiency and effectiveness in resource-constrained IoT networks, this system employs the Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) consensus process. DPoS mitigates the performance and effectiveness deterioration in blockchain-based IoT networks by using a certain amount of elected delegates to verify and approve transactions. It is a lightweight consensus mechanism. In this article, we used Docker, the XGBoost mapping model, and the Interplanetary File System (IPFS) to assess the network's performance in relation to latency, resource consumption, and throughput. The four components of our distributed storage study were latency, throughput, resource consumption, and the duration and speed of file uploads. We found that our framework has a low latency of less than 0.976 ms in our empirical results. One state-of-the-art consensus method, Proof of Stake (PoS), is outperformed by the suggested method. We also show that the suggested method works well for Internet of Things (IoT) uses that call for minimal latency or efficient use of resources.

articleTitle: Game Theory-Based Auction Approach for Resource Allocation in Grid Computing Using Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Grid computing leverages distributed resources to achieve higher performance and scalability in computing tasks. Efficient resource allocation in such systems is crucial for optimizing performance and cost. This paper explores the application of game theory-based auction mechanisms for resource allocation in grid computing, utilizing the concept of microgrids. Microgrids, with their localized and self-sufficient resource clusters, offer an innovative framework for resource management. We propose a game-theoretical auction model to allocate resources dynamically and efficiently. The proposed approach is validated through simulations, demonstrating improved resource utilization and reduced computational costs.

articleTitle: A Siamese based Generative Adversarial Network for Separated Medical Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Due to the need for expensive and complex equipment, highly skilled personnel, and often postponed operations, obtaining high-resolution pictures in medical imaging is a difficult and expensive task. Super resolution methods based on deep learning may help us get rich information out of low-resolution images taken with current equipment. One of the major areas of focus in medical research recently has been the improvement of unpaired medical images. Medical picture improvement using deep learning has been very successful, however these systems still struggle with issues like small data sets and poor training sets quality. This article proposes a Siamese GAN with ResNet34-based dual-input mechanism image enhancement method that makes use of the target highlight structure (texture enhancement) while background balance structure (consistent background contrast) from uncoupled low-quality as well as high-quality medical images. In addition, the suggested approach incorporates the generative adversarial network methodology to accomplish structure-preserving augmentation via concurrent adversarial learning iterations. By comparing the suggested Siamese GAN plus ResNet34 to other state-of-the-art methods, experiments show how well it performs in unpaired picture improvement. Experiments are conducted using three datasets: (1) pictures from retinal fundoscopy (DRIVE and STARE), (2) brain MRI (BraTS), and (3) dermoscopy images from skin cancer (ISIC) patients.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Accurate Anomaly Detection in Multi-Cloud Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is used for identifying complicated Cloud assaults. A cooperative IDS may use an aggregation technique to decide on suspicious intrusions. Aggregation methods and IDS feedback slow the process. These restrictions make real-time cooperative IDS choices useless and unsustainable. We suggest a machine learning-based collaborative IDS that uses past feedback data to make proactive decisions to address these issues. DRL-based multi-cloud IDS was suggested. The suggested approach uses a DE noising Auto encoder (DA) to create a deep neural network. DA can rebuild IDS feedback from incomplete feedback. The DA network uses Q-learning to continuously learn features. This lets us respond on suspected incursions without IDS input. The GPU-enabled Tensor Flow model was tested on a real-world dataset. Our model achieves 95% detection accuracy in experiments.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Blast Cells in Hematological Malignancies using Inception-based Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Detection and classification of malignant leukocytes is an important step for diagnosing acute myeloid leukemia (AML) using peripheral blood smear imagery. A survey of literature on AML shows that deep learning models are introduced for detection and classification of malignant leukocytes from peripheral blood smear imagery. However, deep learning-based classification models are sensitive to handle class imbalance in classification of malignant leukocytes. This paper proposes a cost-sensitive learning with fine-tuned transfer learning methodology for detection and classification of AML. During finetuning, a transfer learning model with cost-weights are introduced for each classes of malignant leukocytes to handle the bias and inaccurate predictions. Optimal transfer learning methodology and its parameters are selected based on the hyperparameter tuning approach. Model performances are shown using a dataset of more than 18,000 leukocytes. Fine-tuned cost-sensitive InceptionResNetV2 transfer learning model showed a higher performance compared to the other models with an enhanced precision 1%, recall 3%, and f1-score 3%. The proposed model can be used by a healthcare professional to enhance the early diagnosis of AML.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fake News Detection Leveraging a Hybrid BERT-BiLSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Fake news is phenomena that deserves global attention especially with the above issues of social media being the largest source that influences people’s opinions, attitudes or decisions. Authenticating news in the upswing is energy-consuming and highly priced which is why there has been a growing focus in the field. Different means of solutions in issues related to the faking of news has been sought including: content-based classification, contexts based classification, images based classification, sentiment analysis, and mixed approaches. This work offers a method of fake news detection where news headlines are considered, which falls under the content-based classification scheme. The Architecture incorporates BERT and encompasses an LSTM layer as well. Training and evaluation were done on FakeNewsNet - PolitiFact , GossipCop datasets and ISOT dataset. The method propounded was tested against benchmark classification models while the impact of the LSTM layer on classification was tested by a BERT model that was subjected to the same conditions.

articleTitle: ADHD-Net: A Robust Deep Learning-based Framework for Detecting ADHD Patients using EEG
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental condition that affects a significant proportion of the global population. In modern civilization, many individuals, including adults and children, are diagnosed with ADHD. ADHD can substantially affect the lives of individuals in diverse domains. The condition can make it challenging for a person to maintain focus, organizational skills, and impulse control, leading to difficulties in academic, social, and professional environments. It is much better to identify ADHD during the earlier stages in order to arrange tailored treatments. The goal of this study is to design a deep learning-based framework known as ADHD-Net for the precise diagnosis of ADHD from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals of the human brain. This study utilizes a publicly available dataset consisting of EEG data from 60 healthy controls and 61 ADHD patients aged 7-12 years. First, filtering of the EEG signal is performed to remove noise and artifacts. Subsequently, Independent Component Analysis (ICA) is performed to remove the noise generated by muscle movements and eye blinking. Principal component analysis (PCA) is utilized to reduce the dimensionality of the preprocessed EEG data. A deep learning model called ‘ADHD-Net’ is designed for automated detection of ADHD patients by analyzing EEG signals. The PCA-enhanced EEG data obtained is used to train the ‘ADHD- Net’ model. The trained model can classify an EEG data sample into two classes: ‘ADHD Patient’ and ‘Healthy Person’, with a high classification accuracy of 97.96%. The novelty of this research lies in: i) designing a deep learning model named ADHD-Net for automated ADHD detection, and ii) incorporating the attention mechanism into the designed ADHD-Net model to enhance its efficacy.

articleTitle: Cricket shot classification using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Cricket is a popular sport that involves various batting techniques and shot types. Accurate and real-time detection of cricket shots can provide priceless visual images for coaches, players, and analysts. This study proposes an artificial intelligence-based approach for cricket shot detection aimed at automatically recognizing and classifying different shots played by batsmen. Images are extracted and pre-processed to enhance their quality. The pre-processed images extract key features like bat trajectory, player movement, and batsman position. A training dataset is used to enable shot classification, consisting of labeled samples of different cricket shots. Neural network models, such as a convolutional neural network, VGG16, VGG19, are trained using an image set to learn the patterns and characteristics of each shot type. The model is then employed to classify shots in real time for predicting the corresponding shot type based on the selected features. The proposed approach is evaluated on a diverse dataset of cricket match images, encompassing a broad extent of shots played by professional batsmen. Execution metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to assess the effect of the shot detection system. A VGG16 model in cricket shot prediction of the dataset yielded an impressive accuracy of 95.81%. The solution establishes the efficiency of the planned approach in accurately detecting and classifying cricket shots in real-time. The developed system has the potential to enhance cricket coaching, player performance analysis, and broadcast coverage by providing valuable insights into the shot selection and execution of batters.

articleTitle: Enhanced Yolov5 Based Approach for Effective Agricultural Pest Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Agricultural pest detection is a major challenge for farmers globally, affecting both crop health and productivity. Many current detection systems suffer from low accuracy and high false alarm rates, resulting in significant crop damage and financial losses. To address the persistent threat pests, pose to agricultural sustainability, innovative detection methods are crucial for minimizing risks and ensuring food security. The proposed system offers several improvements over existing methods, including enhanced accuracy in pest detection, fewer false alarms, and the capability to identify specific pest species and their damage. Furthermore, the use of Enhanced YOLOv5 for automated pest detection promises to increase efficiency and cost-effectiveness in managing agricultural pests.

articleTitle: Image steganography in the IoMT and telemedicine: Residual and Enhanced Discriminative Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Through the use of technology such as computers, phones, and medical equipment, telemedicine and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) enable off-site interactions between medical professionals, patients, and experts. Patient privacy or consultation outcomes might be jeopardized, leading to potentially catastrophic medical events, if the information sent in IoMT is unlawfully steganographic, altered, or leaked throughout transmission and storage. There is an immediate need to safeguard the privacy and value that is the picture data included in electronic health records (EHRs). A possible option may be image steganography. Consequently, a StegaStamp-based steganographic model for pictures from medical records is created. Medical record photos are document images, not like natural photographs, and hence they are susceptible to image cropping assaults. When it comes to detecting illicitly transmitted medical pictures in IoMT and telemedicine, steganalysis plays a crucial role. To address the challenges of picture steganalysis in IoMT and telemedicine, we provide RGAN-Net, a Residual Generative Adversarial Discriminative Network. A deep residual network, a steganographic information discriminative mechanism, and an augmentation module for steganographic information make up RGAN-Net. In order to improve the illicit steganographic signal in highly detailed medical images with complex textural qualities, the RGAN-Net utilizes a steganographic information improvement module. In order to extract and compress steganographic features, a deep residual network is used. The deep residual network uses a steganographic data discriminative technique to correct the steganographic characteristics and remove high-frequency characteristics that are erroneously classified as steganographic information. The range of RGAN-Net steganalysis error PE was found to be 0.0732-0.0010 and 0.231-0.026, respectively, in experiments carried out on public and private datasets with data concealing payloads that varied from 0.1bpp/bpnzac-0.5bpp/bpnzac in the spatial realm and the JPEG domain, respectively. Overall, the RGAN-Net beats four top-tier steganography detectors, according to both quantitative and qualitative findings on both public and private datasets.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Immunology: Predictive Models for Immune System Disorders
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The complexity of immunological illnesses makes them difficult to diagnose and treat. Conventional methods mostly concentrate on treating symptoms after these appear, depending on retrospective data and a small number of clinical indicators, which causes diagnoses to be made later and interventions to be less successful. The study presents an AI-powered predictive approach that uses machine learning and deep learning to foresee immune system problems before symptoms appear. The method improves early detection and diagnosis precision by combining large datasets, such as genomic, proteomic, and clinical data. The proposed approach surpassed conventional systems in accuracy, precision, and recall, obtaining 92.5% accuracy and 88.0% sensitivity in early detection. The results show significant improvements over current approaches. The results highlight how the system could transform immunological diagnosis and therapeutic approaches.

articleTitle: Forecasting and Analysing Cyber Threats with Graph Neural Networks and Gradient Based Explanation for Feature Impacts
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Cybersecurity is increasingly critical in today’s digital landscape, with evolving threats such as advanced persistent threats (APTs), ransomware, and phishing attacks posing significant risks to organizations and individuals alike. Traditional methods of malware detection have become insufficient as these threats grow in sophistication, highlighting the need for innovative approaches in threat management. The work addresses the gap in predictive and interpretative threat detection by focusing on AI-driven threat prediction. Graph Convolutional Network , one of the advanced Graph Neural Network (GNN) models are developed. The methodology includes building a website for file uploads, generating hash codes using Local Sensitive Hashing (LSH), training GNNs for threat detection. The gradient-based explanation method is involved from Explainable AI (XAI) that helps in interpreting the impact of individual features on a model’s predictions. This approach contributes to the field by enhancing proactive threat management and providing transparent, understandable explanations of detection results, ultimately advancing cybersecurity defences.

articleTitle: Stentrode: Pioneering Minimally Invasive Brain-Computer Interfaces – A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the field of neurointerventional electrophysiology (NeuroEP), the Stentrode emerges as a remarkable player functioning as an endovascular electrode array. The Stentrode has a unique capability to stimulate the brain without invasive means through blood vessels. This incredible technology sets the stage for Functional Neuro-intervention, a broad category covering brain computer interfaces, brain monitoring, brain mapping and deep brain stimulation. Brain Computer Interface (BCI) via Stentrode helps neurologically impaired patients to perform everyday tasks successfully.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Transformation for Enhancing Food Security through Precision Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Growing worldwide consumption of food security has laid the foundation to make farming methods more effective and sustainable. Machine learning (ML), which falls under the broader AI framework, has become an innovative enabler for precision farming—we facilitate the continuous analysis of data, the use of this data for modelling Outlooks to support farming activity, and manage resources to improve farming yields. This paper discusses the Implication of AI in precision farming as a concept that enhances crop yield forecast, resource utilisation, and the mitigations of farming hurt on the environment. The proposed AI models also use IoT sensors, remote sensing, and machine learning to decide on the use of water, fertilizers, and pesticides. The simulations reveal quite encouraging gains to the precision of yield accuracies, optimization of resources, and reduction of costs. The investigated AI applications in farming demonstrate a significant capacity to cut the farming manifold and environmental emissions, thereby indicating an ability to support the longer-term health and growth of farming and food security for the globe. However, issues like data quality, the accuracy of models used and declaration or adoption have become issues yet to settle. The study indicates that there is hope for the modern agriculture as being revolutionized by AI and points to the ways of improving the use of AI further.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Framework for Image Cyberbullying Recognition Using Transfer Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Facebook, Twitter, and other social media sites have many positive uses, but they also have many negative aspects. Cyberbullying (CB) is a problem on various social media sites. Since each individual's reaction to cyberbullying is unique, the damage it does to victims' lives is difficult to put a price on. While some may view the message as natural, victims may perceive it as bullying. Finding the bully material in cyberbullying communications is quite difficult due of their ambiguity. There has been some study on using textual posts to solve this problem. Cyberbullying detection using images, on the other hand, has gotten comparatively less focus. The overarching goal of this study is to provide a framework for addressing the problem of cyberbullying on social media sites that makes use of images. Developing models is the initial use case for the convolutional-neural-network(CNN) that is based on deep-learning (DL). In the subsequent sections, this study employs transfer-learning(TL) models. The experimental results of varying the hyper-parameters verified that the model based on TL is the superior option for this issue. With a bestcase accuracy of 95.6%, the suggested algorithm successfully identifies the vast majority of cyberbullying posts. Combining DL with TL techniques yielded better results than applying either method alone, according to experiments conducted on an image dataset.

articleTitle: Defending Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Data poisoning attacks present a significant threat to machine learning (ML) and deep learning models, compromising their reliability and effectiveness during inference. This paper draws insights from recent studies to explore various aspects, including the vulnerabilities of ML architectures, especially deep learning models, to these attacks. It introduces novel methodologies to detect and mitigate data poisoning, considering factors such as model robustness, performance degradation, and poisoning ratio thresholds. Special attention is given to backdoor attacks in multimodal learning scenarios, proposing strategies like Clean CLIP to counter spurious associations. By synthesizing findings across different attack types and defenses, the paper underscores the importance of standardized benchmarks and realistic evaluation settings in assessing countermeasures’ efficacy.
