Ultimately, this work enhances our understanding of data poisoning vulnerabilities in deep learning, offering practical strategies to bolster the resilience of ML systems against evolving adversarial threats.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fake Review Detection: A Hierarchical Graph Attention Network Approach Using Text and Ratings
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The establishment of trusting connections between buyers and sellers is essential in electronic commerce (EC) since it paves the way for mutual benefit. Users can research a business's reputation before deciding to do business with them. There are some aspects of the reputation system that are unflattering to both vendors and clients. For instance, as a consequence of their dishonesty or lack of effort while posting reviews, some users may create phantom feedback, which seems as fabricated assessments meant to boost their reputation.The proposed approach incorporates stage preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training. In order to prepare the data for the SA job, the pre-processing phase incorporates initial procedures that aid in data transformation. One way to improve the model's accuracy is to use features extraction to remove irrelevant data points. We kept using the HGAN model throughout training. This state-of-the-art method outperforms SVM and LSTM with an average accuracy of 91.26%.

articleTitle: A Lightweight & Effective Public-Key System for IoT Applications Using DL Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Online communication has grown in significance with advancements in computer network technology, and as a result, network complete solution has emerged as a means to guarantee dependable network communication. Keeping the internet secure is crucial in light of this. Most people use encryption. There are several encryption approaches that are constituted by different encryption algorithms. A novel algorithm, hyper-chaotic encryption, has evolved in the last few years. This forms the basis of an encryption system that may provide complete information security for networks and effectively thwart malicious network intrusions. Differential Privacy's main selling point is that it uses common numerical data types, which means it's compatible with the vast majority of machine learning libraries and hardware accelerators. This results in almost little overhead during implementation or runtime. Conversely, the accuracy of the model's forecasts is diminished when Differential Privacy is used. Instead of providing cryptographic assurances, Differential Privacy just provides a probability constraint on the likelihood of information leaking. The computer has become an integral part of people's daily lives, facilitating both education and daily living. Due to the multifaceted nature of the computer network environment, several variables might have an impact. Examining the safety of the computer network is the first and foremost step in making it more secure. Thus, there is a pressing need to use algorithms based on deep learning to assist programmers in developing a new system for computer internet security due to the high human and material expenses associated with maintaining this system and the inefficiency of conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Better Image Analysis, Recognition, and Interpretation in the Field of Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has brought about a significant revolution in image processing. This revolutionary technology has enabled the analysis, recognition, and interpretation of images in ways that were previously inconceivable. An investigation into the most recent developments in artificial intelligence techniques that have improved the efficiency and precision of image processing tasks is presented in this study. We survey the emergence of transformer architectures and the integration of deep learning models, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to explore how these technologies have transformed the understanding and application of images in several industries. An overview of existing image processing methods and the limits of those approaches is presented at the beginning of our research. This highlights the necessity of more advanced AI-driven solutions. After that, we examine the advancements that have been made in artificial intelligence, such as the incorporation of attention processes, the development of more effective CNN architectures, and the utilisation of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for the purpose of picture synthesis and augmentation. The purpose of this research is to investigate the impact that artificial intelligence has on particular applications of image processing, such as autonomous car navigation systems, facial recognition, medical imaging, and satellite images analysis. Specifically, we focus on the enhancements in diagnostic accuracy, environmental monitoring, security, and safety that arose as a result of the adoption of artificial intelligence in these sectors through the use of case studies. Furthermore, we discuss the issues that are associated with artificial intelligence in image processing. These challenges include the necessity for explainable AI models, the requirement for computational resources, and the protection of data privacy. A number of potential solutions to these problems are proposed by us, including federated learning and the creation of artificial intelligence systems that are more open to scrutiny. Lastly, we come to a conclusion by predicting future developments in artificial intelligence for image processing. These developments include the ability of AI to offer more personalised and adaptable image processing solutions, as well as the integration of AI with edge computing for real-time image analysis. The results of our research highlight the significant role that artificial intelligence plays in the development of image processing skills, which has far-reaching ramifications for the fields of technology, industry, and society.

articleTitle: Exploring Device Fingerprinting for Password-Less Authentication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Traditional password-based authentication systems pose security challenges due to the vulnerabilities associated with weak passwords and the storage of password representations on servers. In this paper, I investigate an alternative approach to user authentication using device fingerprinting. Device fingerprinting involves collecting information about a device’s attributes and configuration to create a unique identifier. Leveraging device fingerprints, I propose a password-less authentication system where users only need to remember their username. By comparing the computed device fingerprint with the stored identifier in the system’s database, users can gain access if the fingerprints match above a certain threshold. I discuss the origins and evolution of device fingerprinting, highlighting its use by online analytics and advertising companies for user tracking purposes. Despite privacy concerns, I argue that device fingerprinting offers advantages in authentication by eliminating the need for user input and providing enhanced security against brute-force attacks. I also examine various fingerprinting techniques and their effectiveness in identifying devices across different browsers and system configurations. Finally, I conclude by discussing the potential of device fingerprinting as a viable authentication method and suggest avenues for future research in security implementations.

articleTitle: Automated Extraction of Information from Speech Signals for Speaker Identification and Emotional State Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study, we discuss the challenging task of acquiring large human speech datasets under constrained conditions, which are typically hand-annotated for speaker recognition and emotional state analysis. We explore a novel approach to learning embedding for speech classification without using labeled audio data. Our hypothesis is that a speech signal can identify a speaker, and by observing the speaker’s facial expressions, we can determine their emotional state. We utilize the VoxCeleb dataset, which contains real-world noise and background chatter, to test our approach. For speaker identification, we apply a CNN-based architecture with the SeLU activation function and Adamax optimizer, achieving an 89.6% accuracy rate. For emotional state analysis, we use a CNN with the Adam optimizer and ReLU activation function, obtaining a 64.97% testing accuracy rate on an external benchmark dataset. Our results suggest that it is possible to infer emotional states from speech signals using facial expression analysis.

articleTitle: EfficientNet-Based Deepfake Detection: A Robust Approach for Real and Fake Media Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Deepfakes are an up-and-coming form of synthetic media-previously unrealistically realistic video, image, audio, or even live broadcast montaging faces or voices to create an impression of likeness. While opening new ways of creative expression, deepfakes create serious problems in many domains: misinformation, identity theft, defamation-the list increasingly goes on-jeopardizing the reliability of visual evidence in the modern world. As manipulations grow more and more sophisticated, the need to apply effective detection methods is critical. The present work is devoted to the application of the deep convolutional neural network EfficientNetB0 for deepfake detection. EfficientNetB0 is a scalable and computationally efficient architecture that will be applied in the differentiation of real and manipulated images by subtle irregularities in facial features and textures often invisible to the human naked eye. This model is trained on both real and deepfake images, with its optimized configuration to find these minute differences. Data augmentation techniques combined with regularization techniques, including dropout and global average pooling, enhance the capability of the model for generalization over diverse datasets. It achieved 90% on both training and validation, hence did a great job in detecting deepfakes. The confusion matrix further justifies the efficiency of the model in correctly classifying real and fake images. EfficientNetB0 has tremendous potential and can be very useful as a tool in mitigating risks due to manipulated media by helping one contribute toward preserving digital information integrity in an ever-evolving landscape.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Energy 5G IoT Devices with Updatable AI Models: A Dynamic AI-IoT Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Ultra-Low-Power (ULP) Internet of Things (IoT) devices are becoming more important in the fast developing 5G and possible 6G networks, and this study tackles the problem of incorporating dynamic AI capabilities into these devices. We present the Dynamic AI-IoT design, a new framework that aims to do away with the tedium of firmware upgrades. This design makes use of Narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) to make cloud interactions run smoothly and includes specialized firmware modifications to make dynamic interactions with TinyML models possible. Many sectors rely on deep learning that is based on massive amounts of high-quality data. The information accumulation of the framework relies on real-time acquisitions, which makes it difficult to directly implement deep learning in a real-time system. But such systems' analytical activities can't be done by collecting data for a lengthy period since they need to be executed in real time. This research presents a novel progressive deep-learning architecture and performs experiments on picture identification to address the challenges of high-quality data collection, high-timeliness data processing, and the difficulties of directly integrating deep-learning algorithms in real-time systems. The experimental findings demonstrate the efficacy, performance, and ability to get a conclusion comparable to the deep-learning architecture using large-scale data. An advanced method for managing memory is presented for the effective handling of AI tasks; it is based on memory alignment and the dynamic resolution of AI activities. Through the use of ULP IoT gadgets on a 5G testbed, empirical investigations show that the implementation of a Dynamic AI-IoT network is feasible. With an average inference duration of around 46 ms and model updates averaging less than one second, the findings are impressive.

articleTitle: A Method for the Identification of Multiple Labels in Social Media Text using CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: People are able to communicate their thoughts and perspectives with one another through various online settings, including social networks, news websites, and blogs. Because so many individuals instantaneously post their thoughts on the internet, the number of submissions that have been submitted has increased dramatically. It is critical for establishments and organizations to do an effective and speedy analysis of the massive amounts of data at their disposal in order to provide summaries that discuss the perspectives or sentiments of individuals. In this article, we offer a scalable framework that makes sentiment classification by assessing the compound probability scores of the most generally used methods in sentiment analysis using a fuzzy inference mechanism in a CNN-style way. This evaluation is carried out in order to make the framework applicable to a broad range of situations. The valance of an individual's attitude may be estimated by the designed fuzzy inference system by calculating the compound scores of the valance aware dictionary, word embedding, and count vectorization procedures. The suggested technique differs from the convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in that it permits weighting of base learners and combines the strengths of each algorithm using fuzzy rules. Another distinction is that the proposed method is more general. The process of estimating sentiment based on textual data can be handled as either a two-class (positive and negative) or a three-class (positive, neutral, and negative) problem. The former has less challenges than the latter. We carried out the experimental study on four different tagged social network data sets, and discovered that the suggested strategy delivers gains in accuracy for both 2-class and 3-class classifications.

articleTitle: Using DL Measure and Distance to Assess Text Mining Document Classification Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this study, we take an asymptotic approach to the issue of document categorization in text mining. Some intriguing aspects may be shown graphically through the formalisation of statistical hypothesis testing as a text mining task. Due to its experimental efficacy in numerous case studies, various heuristics are used to practical analysis in the text mining issue. This method will provide the necessary theoretical explanation for the efficacy of text mining approaches. Documents are sorted using a distance metric in word vector area and deep learning algorithms. The study also examines the effectiveness of distance measures from the fresh perspective of asymptotic analysis.

articleTitle: Improving 6G Network Safety, Privacy, and Resource Efficiency via the Application of Machine Learning and Network Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The 6G era of networks is tightly tied to intelligent network orchestration while administration, but the cloudification of networks using a micro-services-oriented architecture is a well-known element of 5G. It follows that the proposed 6G paradigm heavily relies on AI, ML, and DL. Proactive threat identification, smart mitigation tactics, and assurance that 6G networks would be self-sustaining are essential for future end-to-end network automation. In order to solidify and enhance AI's position in 6G network security, this article delves at potential AI applications in 6G security. To get there, our research reworked an existing 6G network anomaly detection system to make it operate with ensemble learning (EL) to communicate networks. In order to protect 6G user data from unauthorized access, resale, intoxication, and free-riding attacks, we offer a thorough framework for detecting data attacks that is optimized for secure aggregation using the Deep Reinforcement learning - PPO algorithm. To guard against data poisoning, unauthorized data sources, and mistakes in data aggregation, we use a set of encrypted data auditing tools. We have also performed analysis, evaluated many prospective security strategies, and suggested the best security measures for certain 6G situations. the Krull Herd-Advanced Encryption Standard (KH-AES) algorithm for secure data transmissions. To use IDS, this study makes use of the NSL-KDD dataset. Probing, normal, U2R, DoS, R2L, and unidentified were the six assaults used to categorize the data. Classification results are heavily affected by the weights in HCNN layers. When compared to well-known methods, the suggested system outperforms them when it comes of FS, classifications, and data sharing security.

articleTitle: A Fusion of SVR and Fully Connected Networks for Improved RUL Prediction of Lithium Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries using the Support Vector Regression (SVR) algorithm with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel and compare the outcomes with a combined model that combines SVR and Fully Connected Networks (FCN). A dataset comprising approximately 6,000 records of lithium-ion battery data were utilized, the analysis reveals significant insights into the effectiveness of SVR as a standalone predictive tool. The SVR model outcomes show that it can capture variance in the measurements, with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.2269 and a R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9531. Conversely, the FCN and SVR combined model, which employs a simple averaging technique for predictions, demonstrates marked improvements in accuracy, yielding an MSE of 0.0571,with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.9882, showcasing its superior predictive performance. These results underscore the prospect of ensemble methods in strengthening prediction accuracy, positioning the combined SVR FCN model as a more effective approach for estimating the RUL of lithium-ion batteries. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to improve predictive modeling techniques in battery life estimation, paving the path for innovations in battery management technologies and sustainability initiatives in energy storage solutions.

Author Keywords: Mean Squared Error and Coefficient of Determinant

articleTitle: Enhancing Security Mechanisms in Wireless Sensor Networks for IoT Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The incorporation of WSN-IoT is transforming multiple sectors by improving the gathering, transmission, and analysis of information. This study investigates the collaboration between WSN-IoT, examining the essential methods, uses, and factors that enhance their effectiveness. This article examines 15 pertinent studies to emphasise the technological progress, obstacles, and future potential of WSN-IoT. It offers valuable insights into the expanding importance of WSN-IoT in various industries and beyond. This research article presents a thorough analysis of the integration of Wireless Sensor Networks with the IoT. Our study entails a thorough examination of research publications, specifically concentrating on the methodologies, uses, and crucial variables that determine the effectiveness of WSN-IoT systems. In addition, we emphasise the possible advantages and obstacles of this integration across different sectors.

articleTitle: A Dynamical Combination of Multiple Features-Based Approach for Classifying Agricultural Text
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the traditional text classification technique, values are read as letters, which destroys the original semantic illustration of numerical attributes. Completely mining deeper latent semantics features in agricultural literature requires a novel text classification technique that makes use of multivariate characteristic dynamic fusion. The global principal semantic components of the text were extracted using the Bi-Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) system using an attention mechanism, and the local semantic information was extracted using the Multiple Window Convolutional Neural Network. When classifying textual content based on phenotypic quantitative categories, the deep semantic portrayal of agricultural texts may be significantly enhanced by using the attention strategy to dynamically merge the obtained various semantic features.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Music Therapy System for Regulation of Hypertension and Mental Wellness
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Music therapy is widely considered as a useful form of expression and therapy for individuals coping with chronic conditions such as high blood pressure and mental health disorders. However, traditional approaches to music therapy often lack real-time data on user’s physiological states and limited accessibility. The proposed Internet of Things (IoT)-based system integrates a wearable Pulse Rate Sensor (PRS) and Galvanic Skin Response (GSR) sensor for data collection and machine learning algorithms to offer effective music therapy interventions. By incorporating the use of the Random Forest Classifier to analyze the sensor data and detect the presence of stress and continuous passive intervention with the help of ThingSpeak, this system aims to enhance accessibility and effectiveness in managing chronic conditions. Through this innovative approach, individuals can experience reduced stress responses, decreased anxiety levels, lower blood pressure and heart rate, and improved mental well-being.

articleTitle: Automated Tuberculosis Detection from Chest X-Rays: A Deep Learning Approach with DenseNet121
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this paper presents the application of a modified DenseNet121 model for tuberculosis (TB) identification from chest X-ray images. Using 700 publicly available TB-positive images for the Tuberculosis Chest X-ray Database, 2800 more TB-positive images from the NIAID TB portal, and 3500 normal images, the model was tweaked for binary classification. Celebrated for its effective feature extraction, the DenseNet121 design was altered with sigmoid activation and a global average pooling layer. With an overall accuracy of 90%, the model was able to separate cases of normal from TB-positive. Performance criteria for normal images showed a precision of 0.90 and recall of 1.00, thereby indicating rather great accuracy in non-TB diagnosis. The recall for TB-positive cases was 0.43 even though the accuracy was exactly 1.00. Underlined the strong discriminative power of the model, the outstanding AUC of 0.976 indicated by the ROC curve analysis These results imply more work to increase TB-positive case identification and validate the promise of the DenseNet121 model in TB detection.

articleTitle: Rejection Depth Differential Dynamic Programming for Real-Time Integrated Control for Micro-Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: With the continuous addition of various heterogeneous energy sources and power users in the micro-grid, it causes different degrees of impacts on the operational stability of the grid and highlights the inadequacy of traditional control strategies in frequency control and economic scheduling of micro-grids, therefore, it is very necessary to study the economic dispatch and frequency control of multiple distributed new energy sources after they are connected to the micro-grid. Although the traditional deep learning controller can provide the output, it will lead to the deviation of the micro-grid system when the prediction probability is not high. Based on the rejection operation, this paper presents a framework for realtime generation scheduling and control of micro-grids. When the prediction probability is not high enough, the denial of knowledge deep differential dynamic programming can provide the action of analyzing the control algorithm; when the prediction probability is lower than the set probability cutoff, the exportation of the traditional proportional-integralderivative method is selected as the output of the controller. The numeric simulation results show that the proposed algorithm replaces the traditional micro-grid framework, and establishes the rejection deep differential dynamic planning method for micro-grids.

articleTitle: A Weather-Informed Traffic Forecasting System Constructed Using the SAE Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Access to accurate traffic data is critical for drivers to effectively plan routes and reduce congestion. Traffic patterns, including vehicle speeds and volumes, may be analysed with the use of monitors set up along roads. The vast majority of currently available traffic prediction systems make use of historical traffic data. But, there are two issues with people: (1) they just used traffic statistics to make forecasts, and (2) they didn't consider the volume of data or the time it would take to analyses it. Yet, the weather has a significant effect in predicting how busy the roads will be. In this research, we provide a WTPS, or weather-based traffic predictive model, which uses both traffic and weather information to make accurate predictions. The experimental findings demonstrate that WTPS beats the state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction accuracy in both dry and wet conditions. In order to handle high volumes of traffic, WTPS was developed using big data concepts.

articleTitle: Cognitive Radio-Enabled Internet of Things Communications: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Routing Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) features allow for dynamic spectrum allocation, and IoT devices are increasingly finding usage in a variety of smart applications. Achieving faster data rates and minimizing end-to-end routing latencies in CR-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) communication are our aims in this effort to optimize throughput. In an Internet of Things (IoT) setting based on cognitive radio networks (CRNs), we suggest a routing method based on reinforcement learning (RL). With the goal of reducing EED and packet collisions, the channel choice decision capacity is proposed to be included into the network layer. By modeling the cognitive radio cognitive network (CRCN) simulators as a cognitive radio-enabled Internet of Things (CR-IoT) interactions environment, we compare the network performance of our proposed RL-IoT routing mechanism to that of the recently developed AODV-IoT and ML-based routing methods. Based on our testing, the RL-IoT model outperforms the competition in terms of throughput and packet delivery ratio.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Motion Detection System for Smart Healthcare Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Humans' bad habits are a leading cause of many chronic illnesses. Preventative medicines and telemedicine courses for treating these conditions are proliferating. The availability of secure and pleasurable alternatives continues to be of paramount importance. When it comes to monitoring and studying human health, inertial measurement units (IMU) are frequently viewed as the most objective and least intrusive alternative due to their ability to identify motion patterns with relative ease. Machine learning is commonly regarded as an effective method for analysing IMU data and identifying motion patterns. As part of a smart healthcare learning tool, we describe a deep learning-based technique for detecting human movements. An innovative hybrid adjectives-based on before-classification & multi-features analysis technique is created to classify human motion for usage in healthcare e-learning. To begin, a Kalman filter is used to do preliminary processing on the raw data from the IMUs. An experiment is conducted in which minimum and average gravity reduction techniques are used to the acceleration data. Signal segmentation has been used to data from a variety of time periods to establish which kind of segmentation is most effective. Then, we identify active as well as passive motion patterns to do a preliminary categorization. Both static and dynamic motion patterns have been analysed to recover characteristics. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has been used to categorise the active and passive motion components of healthcare e-learning. We accomplished this using the wearable computing and REALDISP datasets. In experimental comparisons, our proposed method for intelligent health care learning surpassed the current state-of-the-art systems. Implementing the technique as recommended led to an accuracy of 87.35% for the REALDISP dataset & 85.18 on the wearable computers dataset. Furthermore, a smart healthcare advisor is provided with access to the classified motion sequences in order to provide immediate feedback on human health.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of SVM and Logistic Regression in Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using the WDBC Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Background Breast cancer remains a serious worldwide public health problem that requires precise diagnostic tools. We compared two machine learning algorithms, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression( LR) for the diagnostic task of breast cancer in this work. This work uses the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset, containing 569 examples split into different groups and each one identified by 30 numeric features which have already been computed regarding digital images of FNA tests. The dataset has two class of diagnostic labels: benign and malignant. Here, after putting both algorithms to the test we saw that SVM and LR had very good recall, accuracy, precision f1 score and ROC AUC Score. Especially Logistic Regression slightly performed better in a lot of important criteria. A full comparison was made to make up for what these models lacked in other measures were used. When looking at the ratio of true predictions to all predictions generated, both model experts have highest underscore for LR. The precision, that is the percentage of true positives among predicted positives) was also higher in LR. The recall measure, which denotes how many true positives are successfully identified, also showed a similar performance for both models. F1 measure which is a harmonic mean of recall and precision a little increase for LR. Finally, ROC AUC score quantified the overall discriminative capacity of classes that was slightly higher for LR.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Blockchain for User Rating in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Social networks have made a revolution in the way how people connect, communicate and share information with each other by leveraging the Internet as the platform. Social networks are open platforms where users can enjoy their freedom of expression to the maximum for posting anything online. Except for a few occasions, censorship play minimum or no role in the social media networks. Hence, it is the responsibility of the reader to identify and choose the content that is suitable for him to read or repost. Some researchers have created mechanisms for evaluating the contents posted. But, presently there is no mechanism for rating users based on the type of material they post online. In this research, a blockchain powered mechanism is proposed for rating users based on the comments received for their posts. The proposed mechanism leverages the advantages of blockchain including transparency, immutability, traceability and security. The proposed mechanism rewards users for their good behavior using non-fungible tokens and revoking them for misbehavior. The proposed mechanism has been tested using publicly available data and a set of students in a simulated environment. The evaluation results are promising as it can identify users who continuously post good or malicious contents online and rank them accordingly.

articleTitle: Integrating Feature Selection with Deep Learning for Enhanced Obesity Prediction Accuracy in Adults
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Existing obesity prediction algorithms generally rely on conventional machine learning approaches such as decision trees and support vector machines, which struggle with large datasets and complex, nonlinear relationships, resulting in overfitting and poor accuracy. To overcome these limitations, the proposed approach integrates deep learning models with two complex feature selection techniques, recursive feature elimination (RFE) and L1 regularization. The combination increases the model's capacity to detect complicated patterns while effectively lowering the complexity of the input. Prediction accuracy is greatly increased by the system, and performance measures demonstrate notable improvements over conventional models. To be more precise, the proposed system outperformed the existing systems with an accuracy of 85.7%, precision of 84.5%, recall of 86.3%, and F1-score of 88.8%. Healthcare workers can gain useful insights into predicting and controlling adult obesity with the strong and accurate model.

articleTitle: Synergistic CNN-Random Forest Model for Signature Recognition and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The abstract performance characteristics of a signature classifying hypothesis, including precision, recall, F1-Score, encouragement, support percentage, and accuracy for two different signature classification levels. To take a Signature Classification stage one, the proposed approach achieves remarkable accuracy, recall, and F1-Score ratings of 99.87%, 99.50%, & 99.68%, accordingly. These metrics show how amazingly well the algorithm can classify situations in this category. The robustness of the model is demonstrated by the support column, which has 4020 instances classified as Signature Classification Stage 1. With a significant value of 0.47, the support percentage indicates the class's contribution to the entire dataset. In a similar vein, Signature Classification Stage 2 exhibits excellent performance characteristics, with 99.77 percent accuracy, recall, and F1-Score. There is a greater support rate in this class since 4510 instances give 0.52 to the total dataset. The model demonstrates its ability to identify signals with a stunning 99.64% Small Average accuracy, which is the average precision over all cases. Both signature levels performed in balance, as indicated by the weighted average & macro average metrics, which are predicted to be 99.73% for F1-Score, 99.82% for accuracy, & 99.64% for recall. This demonstrates how the model succeeds in maintaining a high level of accuracy throughout the entire dataset in addition to predicting specific classes. With a 99.6483% overall accuracy, it is shown that the notion of signature classification helps classify signatures at different levels.

articleTitle: Combination of Machine Learning Approach for Classifying Important Medicinal Crops
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this study, we use image processing & machine learning approaches to the problem of medicinal plant categorization based on leaf attributes. Medicinal herbs have critical roles in many different medical traditions, and this research emphasises how important it is to accurately identify them. The suggested method begins with image preprocessing to improve the quality of the leaf pictures, followed by image segmentation to extract the leaf features. After the leaves have been subdivided, feature extraction methods are used to record additional information about them, such as their colour, texture, and shape. Using the collected characteristics, the leaf samples are categorised into distinct groups using machine learning methods like Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) & Decision Tree. The automated leaf categorization system has the potential to improve medicinal plant industries' quality control, authentication, & inventory management. Correctly identifying medicinal plants is an important step towards guaranteeing the efficacy and safety of herbal remedies. Herbal medicine practitioners and manufacturers alike may reap the benefits of improved efficiency and accuracy in medicinal plant identification thanks to the use of image processing & machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Leveraging Logistic Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors for Accurate Detection of Multiple Sclerosis from MRI and Clinical Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS), a common demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, produces a spectrum of symptoms including visual loss, muscle weakness, and coordination difficulties. Good control and treatment depend on correct and quick diagnosis. This paper evaluates Logistic Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) classifiers for MS identification using a dataset comprising several clinical and MRI features. The dataset offers a complete basis for classification including age, gender, early symptoms, and MRI findings. For both groups, logistic regression exceeded KNN in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. Logistic Regression specifically attained a precision of 0.75 and recall of 0.88 for Class 1 and a precision of 0.89 and recall of 0.77 for Class 2, therefore producing greater F1-scores and total accuracy of 0.82. With an overall accuracy of 0.78, KNN displayed lesser performance with respect to precision, recall, and F1-scores for Class 1 and Class 2 being 0.71, 0.83, 0.77, and 0.85, respectively, with an overall accuracy of 0.74, These results emphasise Logistic Regression as a more efficient model for MS identification, thereby offering a strong instrument for early diagnosis and maybe enhancing patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Effectual LDA Approach for Optimal Topic Modelling from Social Network Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Methods like document clustering & topic modelling in OSNs allow for the classification, annotation, and analysis of massive volumes of user-generated content. Using these methods, you may finally comprehend the material. Among the various approaches that have been developed throughout time are text mining and clustering techniques. Other techniques, such as hidden subject models & neural embedding approaches, have also been developed. Prior Inference for the Use of Latent Dirichlet Allocation is included as a comparison to our other topic models. Given the many accessible methods of assessment, we review the research to determine which extrinsic measures will provide the best results and then provide guidance on how to use them. Furthermore, we demonstrate the efficacy of the methods on data sets consisting of documents of varied lengths. Our study found that, when using appropriate extrinsic evaluation measures, the best results were obtained across all data sets by using clustering techniques to neural embedding versions of features. Using tf-idf weights & embedding distance measurements, we also provide a top-words based approach to make sense of the clusters. This strategy is predicated on the notion that a sentence's most important words are also the ones that occur most often in it.

articleTitle: Harnessing Machine Learning for Enhanced Diagnosis and Treatment of Brain Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Detecting brain cancer is a crucial aspect of medical imaging, where the accuracy and timeliness of diagnosis can profoundly affect patient outcomes. This study introduces a deep learning (DL) approach, utilizing the VGG16 architecture, to identify brain tumors. The model was developed and tested using a dataset of MRI images, with the primary focus on distinguishing between malignant and benign tissues. The model’s training was optimized using Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), which played a key role in achieving efficient learning and model convergence. Over the course of 30 training epochs, the model showed consistent improvements in accuracy, ultimately reaching a peak validation accuracy of 98%. The confusion matrix provided further validation of the model’s performance, reflecting a well-balanced classification with minimal occurrences of false positives and false negatives. This study underscores the effectiveness of combining VGG16 with SGD in brain tumor detection. The model’s high accuracy and low error rates highlight its robustness, suggesting strong potential for practical use in clinical settings. Such a model could be highly beneficial for radiologists, offering an automated tool that supports early and precise brain cancer diagnosis, thereby contributing to enhanced patient care.

articleTitle: A Novel Framework for the Development of Quality-Aware Autonomic IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: A tremendous quantity of data is being generated via the Internet of Things (IoT). While our knowledge of how to assess the quality of this data at the network and device levels is expanding, there are still significant obstacles to overcome when it comes to interpreting and assessing the quality at the informational and application levels. If you want to know what aspects impact the overall system quality, this post will go over some of the problems with IoT systems and how to fix them at various OSI levels. Using two digital health apps made possible by the internet of things (IoT), the authors look at how semantics may be used to measure the system’s data quality and how to integrate multimodal information to clinical decision support. Important data quality issues arise from the fact that the Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem generates massive amounts of data collected from a variety of heterogeneous sources. The reason for this is that the whole operation of the internet of things system is badly affected by low data quality standards. Data quality has been the subject of much research outside of the Internet of Things (IoT) domain, and the idea is backed by massive standardization efforts. However, data quality management inside the IoT has received little attention. An essential idea with many existing applications for issue solving, data quality (DQ) is used in the creation and execution of information, handling data, decision making, as well as engineering systems. But the ways DQ is now integrated into data management pipelines aren’t flexible enough to accommodate all kinds of uses, which limits its use in the IoT space. A generic framework is introduced in this research that allows for the implementation of DQ assessment in a wide range of Internet of Things applications. A knowledge graph serves as the foundation of the framework, making it easy to incorporate into new uses. The study’s findings highlight many gaps in the current state of IoT quality assurance research. A better comprehension of the investigation’s gaps may be aided by the study’s findings. On top of that, the findings point the way for potential areas of future study.

articleTitle: Optimizing Thyroid Disorder Diagnosis: An ensemble Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Thyroid disorders, including hormonal abnormalities, have a profound effect on human health by affecting metabolism and physiological processes in general This work equips a complex learning algorithm combining decision trees, XGBoost, and logistic regression to overcome the challenges of reliably diagnosing these diseases under different experimental conditions Research also ensures that they can be used reliable: average, worst, and best. The ensemble method performs exceptionally well, with an outstanding diagnostic accuracy of 0.94 across data sets. This model raises the accuracy of medical diagnosis by using different algorithms and reducing their errors. The results show significant progress in integrating machine learning into healthcare systems to improve patient outcomes, highlighting the potential of sophisticated computational techniques to improve clinical processes.

articleTitle: Converter Networks for Multi-Scale Tokens-Aware Multi-Region and Multi-Sequence MR-to-CT Synthesis in a Single Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Synthetic computed tomography (sCT) based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) streamlines the planning of radiation therapy treatments by doing away with CT simulation and error-prone picture registration, which in turn reduces radiation dosage for patients and setup uncertainty. To create sCT images that matched the MRI anatomy, an optimally trained MultiHead Attention was used in conjunction with the reverse diffusion process. We generated sCT using MRI on two datasets—one for the brain and one for the prostate—to test the suggested strategy. The following metrics were used for qualitative evaluation: ground truth CTs and sCTs normalized cross correlation (NCC) indices, multi-scale Structure Similarity index (MS-SSIM), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and mean absolute error (MAE) of Hounsfield unit (HU). A new method for creating CT images from standard MRIs utilizing a transformer-based convolutional neural network (CNN) has been designed and verified by us. Synthetic CT (sCT) pictures of excellent quality and robustness may be produced in a few minutes using this model, which successfully depicts the intricate interaction among CT and MRI images. By cutting down on patient time spent on treatment planning, improving accuracy of treatment delivery, and doing away with the necessity for extra CT scans, this method may considerably streamline radiation treatment planning.

articleTitle: Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for the Traffic Accidents Duration Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Traffic management and disaster response rely heavily on accident duration anticipation on expressways. There is no way around the fact that data pertaining to traffic accidents is multi-mode data. Nevertheless, the vast majority of research has been on single-mode data, and there has been surprisingly little quantitative examination of how multi-mode data affects model prediction abilities. In response to these shortcomings, the current study suggests a heterogeneous deep learning architecture that makes use of multi-modal characteristics to enhance the precision of motorway traffic accident length prediction models. To begin, by combining structured and textual data, six distinct data modes are produced. Second, to construct classification models with less prediction error, a hybrid deep learning method is used. In the end, we use a number of deep learning models to thoroughly examine how multi-mode data affects the accuracy of accident length predictions. The survey data obtained from an expressway observing system of China, is utilized to gauge the proposed method. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that Word2Vec-BiGRU-CNN—with an F1-score of 0.3648—is the most appropriate and superior for anticipating the duration of traffic accidents using text features. The results of this study show that deep learning algorithms’ prediction abilities are much improved by using newly-established structured features retrieved from text data.

articleTitle: Photogrammetry: Insights on 3D Model Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This paper delves into the core principles of photogrammetry, exploring the concepts that enable the creation of 3D object models from photographs. We provide a detailed examination of the photogrammetry workflow, with a particular focus on key stages such as data capture, point cloud generation, polygon mesh creation, and triangulation. An experimental analysis is also conducted using a real example of the lion statue in Mahabalipuram, applying the concepts that have been explored in this paper.

articleTitle: Temporal Evolution of Color Variations in Land Lotus Using CNN-LSTM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: A full review of standard performance measures that differed between groups at different times is provided in the abstract. After careful analysis, we found that the classification system showed differences in accuracy, recall, and F1 scores over different periods. It is important to note that the model achieves a certainty rate of 72.00% at 6:00 AM, a recall of 69.44%, and an F1-Score of 70.69%, indicating a balanced prediction power during the early morning hours. Time travel continues and reveals the mystery of different times such as 10:00, 15:00, and 18:00; characterized by more decisions and return values and the highest score F1. When viewed in the context of the macro average, the decision of 73.56%, a return rate of 73.24%, and an F1 score of 73.26% provide the all-time outlook. Considering the impact of the outcome in the classroom, the weighted average shows that the decision, recovery rate, and F1 score are higher at 74%, 72%, and 72% respectively. This demonstrates the model's poor performance in classifying events across a wide range of physical conditions when accounting for class differences. Finally, micro averaging provides a composite measure across all scenarios, yielding a precision, recall, and F1 score of 74.20%. This consensus provides further evidence that the model successfully reflects the physical complexity of the data set at a holistic level. These key points include performance measurements of historical classification models. It provides information about the model's predictive capabilities at different times and forms the basis for subsequent adjustments and improvements.

articleTitle: Design of Trading Mechanism and Blockchain-Based Spectrum Administration System for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Complete connectivity and high-quality service are provided via a space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN). Because it brings together devices from several untrusted authorities, an integrated network like this raises security risks. While blockchain's decentralized ledger features promise to address SAGIN's security flaws, they also pose the risk of incurring intolerable latency due to sequential request validation and consuming vast amounts of storage space required to maintain a full copy of the chain on each node in a large-scale networks. In order to facilitate the required inter-segment cooperation, it becomes conceivable to use several parallel blockchains for the effective management of various SAGIN with blockchain collaboration technology segments. To that aim, we present SAGIN's collaborative blockchain architecture as a means to an end—the efficient and safe administration of varied resources. While blockchain cooperation is possible, each section of SAGIN—the air, ground, and space networks—maintains its own specifically constructed blockchain. In SAGIN, spectrum management has become crucial as the number of wireless gadgets and services continues to skyrocket. Reliable spectrum sensing under lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is still a major barrier for spectrum management, despite the fact that efforts to provide dynamic spectrum access are showing promise in promoting more spectrum sharing. To enhance the performance of spectrum sensing, a deep neural network-based detection structure is constructed to extract features data-drivenly from the received signal's covariance matrix. This approach is based on the idea that artificial intelligence (AI) can provide intelligence to wireless networks through learning and data mining. A method for blindly defining thresholds without using the system's past knowledge is suggested in order to eradicate the effect of noise uncertainty. The suggested scheme's detection effectiveness is enhanced in a low SNR domain, according to numerical evaluations conducted on both real-world and simulated signals.Next, we use relay chain technology to build a collaborative blockchain that uses incentives to govern space-air-ground mobility. This will make sure that diverse parts of the network participate and that cooperation is secure. The suggested framework is effective, as shown by numerical findings.

articleTitle: Enhancing Predictive Analytics in Big Data through Feature Selection and Dimensionality Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The rising sophistication of Big Data has been marked by high dimensionality that poses numerous challenges when predicting analytics computations and model performance. This paper tries to adopt an integrated features selection and dimensionality reduction based on Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) respectively. The removal of those features and the use of principal components analysis lead to a more accurate predictive model while reducing the need for computation time. Furthermore, experimental results indicate that the level of accurate prediction in the model is enhanced from 75% to 85% in addition to the decrease of computation time by 20%. The approach successfully overcomes the obstacles of overfitting and increased computational costs associated with processing big data. This method is particularly applicable for call centers, hospitals, banks, credit cards, insurance, or any other domains, where large data volumes are dealt with frequently and where large volumes of data can be a key differentiator.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi Lockdown: Ensuring Rock-Solid Security in Wireless Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The dynamic cyber threat landscape requires a robust Wi-Fi security framework. The paper identifies shortcomings in existing systems, such as vulnerabilities in WPA2 encryption, limited network segmentation, irregular firmware updates, susceptibility to MAC address spoofing, potential VPN weaknesses, single-factor authentication reliance, insufficient security audits, ineffective firewall configurations, and inadequate user education. The proposed Wi-Fi security system addresses these issues with enhanced WPA3 encryption, robust network segmentation, automatic firmware upgrades, improved MAC address filtering, enhanced VPN protocols, two-factor authentication, regular security audits, optimized firewall setup, and comprehensive user education. Results demonstrate significant improvements in data transmission, reduced network downtime, and enhanced security. Comparison metrics demonstrate the proposed system's superiority in preventing unauthorized access attempts. With a quarterly network downtime frequency, 1.5 seconds user authentication speed, and a firewall reaction time of 5 ms, the proposed system provides a more efficient, dependable, and secure wireless network environment. The complete strategy establishes a solid foundation for Wi-Fi security, reducing the risks associated with cyber threats in modern wireless environments.

articleTitle: Text Mining for the Detection and Categorization of Cyberbullying in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The goal of this research is to classify the tweets and other social media posts on bullying using a text-mining approach. The study resulted in the development of a method for the detection and categorization of cyberbullying across many media types. This approach integrates textual and metadata data to identify cyberbullying resources within the context of social networks. Finally, cyberbullying samples from the research are classified using a decision tree classifier; once classified, these features are combined with text examples to determine the proposed model's performance. The simulation is conducted to evaluate the classifier's detection performance against state-of-the-art methods. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the current methods in terms of classification and id. Accurateness.

articleTitle: Broadcast Tree Construction for Secure and Shortest Path Finding Techniques in WSN for Smart Farming Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: A wireless sensor network (WSN) consists of a large number of distributed sensing devices that use little power and processing capabilities. Data packet switching in sensing devices is often achieved by using multi-hop transmission due to the limited range of connection and the dense distribution of sensor nodes. Dynamic routing in wireless sensor networks (WSN) has been more popular in recent years. In modern times, sensor networks often use the multipath data transmitting approach to optimize system performance by using the available bandwidth. The main objective of this paper is to elucidate the concept of multipath routing, along with its inherent challenges and fundamental justifications for using this approach in sensor networks. This study presents a method for determining the shortest route using the Broadcast Tree Construction (BTC) algorithm, which incorporates data aggregation methods to reduce network overhead during communication. This method is suitable for both cluster networks and Wireless Sensor networks. We conducted a comprehensive experimental study to assess the performance of our proposed system in the NS2 environment. We tested the system using four distinct protocols and examined its efficiency. The system conserves 15% of the energy of internal nodes and improves network life by 7% when it operates with SAODV.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of CNN and SVM for Sleep Apnea Classification: Evaluating Performance and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Inadequate oxygen levels can happen when a person with sleep apnea has periods of paused breathing and then resumes breathing during the night. If the signal is not received, the individual's airway will close and they will cease to breathe. These interruptions can occur occasionally but frequently during sleep. When they start breathing again, they could snort, inhale deeply, or wake up feeling as though they are choking, gasping, or suffocating. This study introduces a classification model to identify different types of sleep apnea using polysomnographic data, with a focus on Normal (No Apnea), Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA), Central Sleep Apnea (CSA), Mixed Sleep Apnea (MSA), and Hypopnea (Reduced Breathing). The model showed excellent accuracy levels, with precision and recall measurements demonstrating strong performance, especially in Normal and Hypopnea categorizations. Although effective, the model encountered difficulties in correctly differentiating between CSA and MSA, as shown by higher rates of false negatives in these groups. the model achieves an impressive accuracy of 99% for Normal and OSA, and 97% for CSA and MSA, demonstrating its efficacy in classifying sleep apnea types and underscoring its potential for clinical application in diagnosing sleep disorders.

articleTitle: Mitigating Rogue Switch Attacks in Software-Defined Networking: Techniques and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) introduces innovative network management and flexibility but also exposes new vulnerabilities. This paper investigates the impact of rogue switches on SDN controllers, detailing various attack methodologies, including Denial-of-Service (DoS), traffic diversion, rule modification, and false reporting. Through experimentation with both basic and optimized Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks on Pox and Ryu controllers, I demonstrate significant degradation in network performance. The study also explores advanced rogue switch behaviors, such as cloning and diverting traffic, selective rule manipulation, and information extraction about the controller’s state. I propose several countermeasures, emphasizing the necessity of SSL/TLS implementation and additional verification mechanisms to protect controllers. Our findings underline the critical need to integrate security as a fundamental priority in future SDN specifications to safeguard against these threats.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Improved Quantum Evolution Algorithm in Computer Network Routing Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In order to meet the challenges of applied research in computer network routing, in view of the shortcomings of the existing D-P algorithms, this study proposes an innovative application research method based on improved quantum evolution algorithms. The new solution leverages the principles of QEA theory to accurately identify and locate key influencing factors, and accordingly to classify indicators wisely to reduce potential interference. At the same time, by using the unique mechanism of improving the quantum evolution algorithm, the design strategy of the application in the selection is cleverly constructed. The empirical results show that the proposed scheme shows a significant improvement compared with the traditional D-P algorithm in the key performance indicators such as the accuracy of the application research and the processing efficiency of key factors in routing selection, showing its obvious strong advantages. In computer networks, the applied research in routing plays a vital role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of the applied research in computer network routing. However, in the face of complex simulation tasks, traditional D-P algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of applied research in the routing selection of improved quantum evolution algorithm optimization, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the QEA theory, and uses this as the road map for index allocation, and then uses the improved quantum evolution algorithm to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the application research of computer network routing, the simulation scheme based on the improved quantum evolution algorithm successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional D-P algorithm and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Multilingual Translation System Based on Machine Translation and Algorithm Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In order to solve the challenges of multilingual translation system design and implementation, this study proposes an innovative translation system design and implementation method based on machine translation and algorithm learning in view of the shortcomings of the existing AES algorithms. This new scheme uses the principle of convex optimization theory to accurately identify and locate the key influencing factors, and accordingly carries out a wise index classification work to reduce possible interference. At the same time, by using the unique mechanism of machine translation and algorithm learning, the scheme cleverly constructs the design strategy of the system. The empirical results show that this scheme shows a significant improvement over the traditional AES algorithm in terms of the accuracy of the design and implementation of the translation system, the processing efficiency of key factors, and other key performance indicators, showing its obvious strong advantages. In multilingual translation, the design and implementation of translation systems plays a crucial role, which can accurately predict and optimize the growth trend and output results of multilingual translation system design and implementation. However, when faced with complex simulation tasks, traditional AES algorithms show some inherent shortcomings, especially when dealing with multi-level challenges, their performance is often unsatisfactory. To overcome this problem, this study introduces a new idea of translation system design and implementation based on machine translation and algorithm learning optimization, and accurately controls the influencing parameters through the convex optimization theory, and uses this as a road map for index allocation, and then uses machine translation and algorithm learning to innovate and construct a system scheme. The test results clearly point out that in the context of the evaluation criteria, the new scheme has been significantly optimized in terms of accuracy and processing speed for a variety of challenges, showing stronger performance superiority. Therefore, in the design and implementation of the multilingual translation system, the simulation scheme based on machine translation and algorithm learning successfully overcomes the shortcomings of the traditional AES algorithm and significantly improves the accuracy and operation efficiency of the simulation.

articleTitle: Integrating Edge Computing with Big Data for Efficient IoT Data Processing and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: IoT ecosystem is now generating more data due to the changes in the usage of IoT systems worldwide, real-time processing and large scale analytics have been a challenge. Many IoT applications are not suitable for traditional cloud solutions because of the issues, such as high latency, consumed bandwidth, and lack of scalability. To address these challenges this work puts forward a novel architecture that incorporates Edge Computing along with Big Data systems for efficient IoT data processing. Through partitioning of computations between the edge and clouds, the system eliminates bottlenecks, optimizes bandwidth usage, and ultimately boosts system performance. Thus, when comparing the results, the presented system achieves 66% of lower latency, 50% less bandwidth usage, 97% of processing efficiency as a result of surpassing traditional cloud based systems. Real-time analysis happens locally at edge nodes while the aggregated, big data and complex analysis is done with the help of cloud using tools like Hadoop and Spark. This implies that the proposed approach is well suited to the contemporary demand of IoT systems by providing both interactivity and advanced processing abilities.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Model With Hybrid Feature Learning For Sematic Text Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this article, we present a generic inference hybrid structure for Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (conv-RNN) text semantic modelling, combining the strengths of convolutional and recurrent neural network structures in extracting distinct linguistic features. In addition to the conv-RNN-based sentence matching as well as classification models, we also offer a new sentence classification model as well as an attention-based response selection model with improved performance. Two difficult answer selection (AS) tasks & five standard datasets for sentence classification (SC) are used to verify the suggested models. As far as we are aware, these are the most comprehensive comparison findings in AS and SC to date. We demonstrate the superiority of conv-RNN over other state-of-the-art methods experimentally on a variety of hard tasks and benchmark datasets. Deep training-based architectures outperform ensemble learning methods and supervised training approaches for the sentiment analysis issue in educational data mining. Overall classification accuracy was 95.80% for long-term short-term memory networks using representations built upon the GloVe word-embedding method, making them the most efficient prediction arrangement.

articleTitle: Design and Implement Opinion Mining Approach: Using Deep Learning for Large Scale Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Sentiment Analysis (SA), commonly known as opinion mining, constitutes a segment of machine learning tasked with discerning the overall sentiment conveyed in a word, text, phrase, paragraph, or even an entire document. Leveraging machine learning algorithms and natural language processing methods, SA extracts subjectivity-related information from documents and categorizes them based on polarity, such as positive, negative, or neutral sentiments. SA proves invaluable for businesses seeking to analyze various texts or reviews to glean opinions about their brands, as well as for stock markets aiming to forecast stock trends.More recently, Deep Learning Techniques have gained traction in this field due to their promising ability to accurately decipher emotions from videos, audios, and textual data found on the internet. This paper presents experiments conducted using various deep learning techniques to enhance the extraction of opinions and emotions from audio databases like UrbanSound8k, RAVDESS, and others alike.

articleTitle: Active Filter Design - Second Order Low Pass And High Pass
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of a biquad active low-pass and high-pass filter employing a two-stage differential amplifier topology with a custom-designed operational amplifier. The proposed design utilizes switched capacitor circuits instead of traditional resistors, leveraging the advantages of switched capacitor technology, such as high precision and low sensitivity to process variations.The active filter architecture is implemented using Cadence Virtuoso in a 180nm technology node. Simulation results demonstrate the functionality and performance of the designed biquad active low-pass and high-pass filters. The filters exhibit desirable frequency response characteristics, including cutoff frequencies, passband gain, and stopband attenuation, meeting the specifications outlined for the project. The use of switched capacitor circuits enhances the filter’s performance, providing improved linearity and noise rejection compared to conventional resistor-based designs.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning for the Detection of Audio Deep Fake
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Strong detection procedures are crucial for preserving digital safety and reliability in light of the rapid development of deepfaketechnology, especially in the audio domain. Presenting a "Improved Deepfake Audio Detection using Spectro-Temporal Deep Learning Approach," our study attempts to tackle the growing problem of differentiating real audio from advanced deepfake alterations. In order to train and test a new deep learning model, our approach makes use of the extensive ADD2022 dataset. At its heart, our method is based on a painstaking data preparation step that involves resampling, normalizing, and silence removal of audio samples to make them consistent and improve the quality of the model input. An novel combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for spectral feature extraction and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) or Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for temporal dynamics analysis is used in our deep learning model architecture. The complex irregularities seen in deepfake audios may be easily detected by this hybrid model. This research presents a method for detecting speech spoofing using Convolutional neural networks. The system uses many audio properties to distinguish between human and synthetic voices. In the worst-case scenario, unethical applications of deepfake audios meant to harm third parties might do widespread damage to national assets and reputations. An assailant may create convincing voiceovers by using a tiny audio sample of a real person. A 2D graph may be created using mathematical formulas to represent any audio stream. Converting audio files to pictures of audio features (Spectrogram, MFCC, FFT, STFT) before logging obtaining the array values in a numerical format that is best for feeding into a convolutional neural network (CNN) reduces the amount of computation needed to build a system that can detect deepfake voices. Predictions are made using both standalone and combined methods of entering data into the model.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach to License Plate Recognition: YOLO-v9 and Quantum-Enhanced CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The integration of quantum machine learning with Convolutional Neural Networks presents a groundbreaking approach to Automatic License Plate Recognition. While traditional CNNs require extensive datasets for high accuracy, this hybrid model leverages quantum computing’s unique capabilities to achieve superior results with limited data. The proposed system combines YOLO v9 for license plate detection with a quantum-optimized CNN for character recognition. The quantum component enhances the model’s pattern recognition and generalization abilities, enabling it to extract more meaningful features from smaller datasets. This quantum advantage results in over 95% accuracy in character recognition, surpassing traditional CNN performance. The hybrid approach not only improves accuracy but also addresses the challenge of limited data availability, paving the way for more efficient and robust AI systems in the quantum era.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Forecasting Model with Deep Learning Capabilities for Unbalanced Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: During the last several years, deep learning capabilities have surpassed those of more conventional models on a wide variety of machine learning-related tasks. Neural networks with deep layers have indeed been effectively used to time series forecasting issues, which are crucial to the field of data mining. Their ability to instantly understand the temporal connections contained in time series has made them a viable option. Yet, deciding on a deep neural network architecture and then optimizing its parameters calls for a high level of skill. Thus, it is essential to conduct comprehensive studies of the predictive capacities of all current architectural frameworks. The completion of this work is hampered by two primary factors: (1) a complete examination of the most recent research on depth learning's application to time series forecasting, and (2) an empirical inquiry analysing the effectiveness of the most commonly used architectures. Seven distinct deep learning models are evaluated and compared for their efficiency and accuracy. We present scores and distributions based on our analysis of the suggested models trained with various architectures and hyperparameter settings. The 50,000 time series in the databases are used to solve 12 unique forecasting issues. Using this data to train approximately 38,000 models, we present the largest deep learning research to date for forecasting time series. While LSTMs were shown to be the most significantly predictive, both LSTMs & CNNs showed promise in this research. Comparable performance is attained by CNNs, but with less variance in results as well as a more based on the best available overall.

articleTitle: A Robust and Energy Efficient Opportunistic Routing Protocol Design over Wireless Sensor Network to Enhance Communication Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) play a crucial role in monitoring and transmitting data in environments where traditional networks are impractical. This paper explores the essential principles that underpin the efficient operation of WSNs, focusing on energy efficiency, reliability, and adaptability. Energy efficiency is achieved through techniques such as duty cycling, low-power communication modes, and dynamic sleep scheduling, which collectively reduce energy consumption and extend battery life. Reliability is enhanced through robust error detection and correction mechanisms, as well as route redundancy strategies, resulting in improved packet delivery ratios: 95% with error detection, 97% with error correction, and 99% with route redundancy.
