Adaptability is ensured by opportunistic and topology-aware routing strategies that dynamically adjust to real-time network conditions. These advancements in energy harvesting, cross-layer optimization, and the integration of machine learning for smarter decision-making processes.

articleTitle: SafeComm: An IOT-based System for enhancing rural child safety using LoRa Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The safety of kids who play outside while travelling in rural areas is a big concern. Safecomm’s new technical fix combines LoRa, NFC, as well as UVC cam systems. Thereby, the gadget has been engineered by merging LoRa modules, NFC tags, GSM module and ESP cams for real-time tracking of where their children are and instant alerting their parents or schools. Besides, when there is an emergency, the wearer can choose to press the emergency button for the SOS family contacts and the emergency services organisations to be alerted in case the battery level is still good. If required, images can also be captured and saved on the cloud storage. This IoT product leverages LoRa, NFC, and an UVC cam to cater for safety issues relating to modes of transport for rural schools. Every day when children mobile around, this machine secures them. The attendance is made easy and quick response in cases of emergency is also possible through this technology so the risks are averted. This device ensures that children are safe when they move about every day. These technologies make keeping track of attendance easier and being able to quickly respond during emergencies so that dangers are mitigated, therefore parents as well as teachers can be less worried. This undertaking is seen as one important stride toward using internet of things (IoT) technology for ensuring children from outside urban areas are safe and boosting safety inside schools or while commuting using linked transportation means.

Author Keywords: Rural child safety monitoring and alert system

articleTitle: Quantum Randomness and Key Hashing in SSH Authentication Across Asymmetric Cryptographic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In the ever-evolving field of cybersecurity, randomness plays a critical role in cryptographic systems. Traditional pseudo-random number generators, while widely used, can be vulnerable to attacks due to their deterministic nature. This paper explores the integration of quantum randomness into SSH authentication by utilizing a Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) to enhance key generation across various asymmetric cryptographic algorithms, specifically RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA. Quantum-generated randomness offers a higher level of unpredictability, strengthening the security of cryptographic keys. We propose a method to generate keys using quantum random bits, hash them using SHA-256, and secure them for SSH authentication. The generated keys are evaluated for security improvements over conventional methods, and the performance of SSH authentication is analyzed. The results demonstrate that incorporating quantum randomness into key generation increases the cryptographic strength of the keys, offering a more robust defense against potential cryptanalytic attacks, while maintaining compatibility with existing SSH protocols. This approach signifies a step forward in leveraging quantum technologies to enhance network communication security.

articleTitle: Application of Machine Learning for the Detection of Secure Cyber Fraud
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Identifying fraudulent transactions is of utmost importance in the cybersecurity business, since the volume of valid transactions far exceeds the fraudulent ones. There has to be a concerted effort to improve cybersecurity in a practical manner because cybercriminals are becoming smarter and more aggressive, and they're getting better at hiding their traces. Cybercrime has become more prevalent because to the COVID-19 epidemic. Every nation that falls victim to cybercrime sees a significant dent in its GDP. Hacking, phishing, online fraud, cyberbullying, cyber espionage, and most significantly, botnet-orchestrated assaults are all part of this wide-ranging category of cybercrimes. For the purpose of early botnet attack detection and identification, this paper presents a novel collaborative deep learning method based on supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithms and unsupervised long short-term memory (LSTM) models. We test the suggested approach on the IoT-23 and CTU-13 datasets. With an impressively high success rate (around 98.7%) and a very low false positive rate (0.04%), the trial findings show that the suggested strategy performs better than the competition. The research helps us better comprehend cyber threat intelligence, finds new kinds of botnet assaults, and makes forensic investigation processes better.

articleTitle: Distributed Blockchain Technology Combined With Deep Learning for Big Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: This study presented a big data a security framework to address the current state of affairs in cloud-based big data privacy and security protection. Dig The safety and confidentiality of information in the cloud is achieved through the use of blockchain technology and a trusted data cloud centre, with the help of ideas like trusted authorization, intrusion detection, data categorization, as well as decentralised storage, as well as services like Amazon's Web Services log processing service, the Pair Hand authentication of users protocol, as well as the Hadoop data analysis framework. In this work, we implement system startup and user authentication, as well as decentralised and hierarchical data storage and secure user access. The primary contribution of this article is the integration of two cutting-edge tools, namely Blockchain and deep learning, for the protection of large datasets. The results of the experiments show that the system design can guarantee data safety and information access speed, which may serve as a useful reference for cloud security.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Data Forecasting Methodology for Smart Transportation System
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Since traffic patterns alter over time and have complicated spatial connections owing to road systems, traffic forecasting provides unique problems for spatiotemporal forecasting. To address this challenge, we introduce the Graph-based Gated Recurrent Neural Network (G2RNN), a novel deep learning framework that uses graphs to learn the interactions between roads and make network-wide traffic predictions. Our concept of the flow graph inversion is based on the physical network architecture. We also elaborate on the connection between our proposed traffic graph convolution and the spectral graph convolution. G2RNN features are added to a loss function to increase the model's interpretability. Experimental findings show that the suggested approach outperforms baseline techniques on two traffic in the real world state datasets. Graph convolution weights visualisation demonstrates the proposed system's ability to pinpoint critical nodes in actual traffic networks.

Author Keywords: Data Forecasting Model and Graph based Gated Recurrent Neural Networks

articleTitle: Investigating Cybersecurity Dynamics in SDN Controller Buildings: The Danger Environment and Consequences
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: A novel way of constructing networks is the software-defined network, or SDN. New network security dangers exist, yet it can better enable dynamic traffic management than the conventional network. It is crucial to use several controllers to promptly identify suspicious SDN devices in order to enhance SDN security and alleviate the burden on a single controller, utilizing analytical modeling of cyber assaults utilizing the concept of topological change in stochastic networks, the paper presents a way to assuring the functionality of Software-Defined Networks (SDN) in cyber attack situations. In contrast to previous popular methods, the suggested technique integrates analytical modeling-based SDN resilience evaluation with neural network-based SDN status monitoring. Analytical expressions may be used to determine the robustness indicators of SDN, which are made feasible by considering the mathematical basis of this evaluation. The suggested major metric for SDN resilience is the right operation coefficient. This study presents an enhanced anomaly detection approach for SDN multi-controller based on the XGBoost mechanism. The system is fault-tolerant, meaning it can withstand aberrant or erroneous instructions and guarantees the right issuance of the flow table. One relatively new machine learning approach that has been gaining a lot of traction is XGBoost. IIt is essential for SDN controllers to have high accuracy in attack detection, low false positive rates, and fast processing speeds. As a detection approach in SDN-based clouds, we use extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) in this study. Furthermore, we use the POX as the SDN controller, construct the SDN topology using Mininet, and mimic a real-life DDoS assault scenario with the help of the attack tool Hyenae. The XGBoost classifier compares itself to other classifiers using the flow packet data set obtained from TcpDump for DDoS detection. The detection findings show that our technique is faster, more accurate, more scalable. It also has a decreased false positive rate.Both theoretical research and practical simulations confirmed that this approach might significantly fortify SDN network defenses.

articleTitle: Optimizing Threat Mitigation in Critical Infrastructure through AI-Driven Cybersecurity Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: In this paper, the author proposes a novel AI-based cybersecurity model meant for improving threat identification and response in critical infrastructure contexts. Using highly developed methods of artificial neural networks, the system adapts to network flows, logs and system outages and identifies and counteracts increasingly complex cyber threats. The product was developed and validated through exercise scenarios in order to evaluate the impact on sectors of critical infrastructure such as energy, transport, healthcare and others. The outcomes show that the system has received substantial enhancements in threat detection of multiple classes, with classification level of 94% and the false positive levels of 4%. The large-scale AI system was shown to be able to attain better scalability than the model trained on the local set without decreased performance during the high network utilization. Moreover, time responses for threat counteraction reduced dramatically as the system developed through iterations, demonstrating its real-time learning ability. It also describes difficulties which appear when applying the solution, for example, when it comes to data variety and integration of AI models with existing systems. Nonetheless, the solution that is proposed herein has the potential for achieving a scalable and adaptive security in key sectors.

articleTitle: Implementation and Performance Analysis of Optimization based GMPP Tracking Algorithms for a PV Array under Various Shading Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems is largely affected under partial shading conditions (PSCs), which create multiple maximum power peaks while tracking output power. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an adapted grey-wolf optimization (AGO) algorithm for efficient power extraction from a PV system under various PSCs without requiring any sensing components. It utilizes simplified computational blocks and a constant value for the convergence factor to explicit the convergence towards global maximum power point (GMPP). The proposed GMPP tracking algorithm is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and validated through comparative study with a fast converging technique such as APO-MPC. Results confirm that the proposed approach offers higher tracking speed and faster convergence toward the GMPP.

articleTitle: Flask-Powered Machine Learning Model for Accurate Real Estate Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Real estate price prediction is a critical task for various stakeholders, including buyers, sellers, and investors. Existing methods often face challenges such as limited data availability, inadequate feature engineering, and the inability to adapt to dynamic market conditions. This research proposes a novel approach to address these limitations by leveraging machine learning and a Flask-based web application. The proposed system utilizes a comprehensive dataset encompassing various property attributes, including area type, location, total square footage, number of bathrooms, and balconies. A machine learning model is trained on this data to accurately predict real estate prices. The user-friendly web interface allows users to input property details and obtain real-time price estimates. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through rigorous evaluation, showcasing its ability to provide reliable predictions and assist users in making informed decisions. The integration of machine learning and web technology offers a valuable tool for the real estate industry.

articleTitle: Churn Rate Prediction System using Logistic Regression, SVM, and Random Forest Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: Customers are the life blood of any business, and their importance cannot be overstated. Customers are a business’s primary source of revenue. Retaining and gaining new clients is crucial to profitability. Over time, repeat customers typically spend more, and gaining new customers is frequently more expensive than keeping current ones. Consequently, establishing a foundation of devoted clients might boost revenue. Without customers purchasing products or services, there would be no income to sustain the business operations or drive growth. It might have several detrimental implications, such as a decline in market share, loss of revenue, bad impact on staff morale, etc. To tackle this problem supervised learning algorithms are trained on historical data, where the input features and corresponding churn labels are known. The goal is to learn patterns from the data that can help and predict churn accurately for newly unseen data. These algorithms guarantee a high degree of accuracy when forecasting customer attrition, allowing businesses to precisely identify consumers who pose a danger. Businesses frequently use focused tactics, such as re-engagement campaigns with discounts or offers that are specifically catered to the requirements and interests of each churned consumer, to entice and re-engage these customers through individualized communication.

articleTitle: Real-Time Threat Detection and Response Using AI for Securing Critical Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: The main aim of this paper is to discuss the conceptualisation and application of an Artificial Intelligence-based Real-Time Threat Detection and Response system (RTT-DS) for CIS. The system currently applied the best of machine learning as well as deep learning for perfect identification of an anomalous point as well as threat identification. The operation of the system is enhanced with the aspects of both cloud and edge computing, thereby handling big data and offering low latency. In simulation, the proposed system’s accuracy of the proposed system was found to be 95% in threat classification and also in response time; high level threats was taken within a maximum of 2 seconds. The real-time monitors of the system allow one to promptly address the risks before they aggravate. The effectiveness of the proposed system in dynamic and large-scale environments was confirmed through studying of the performance indicators such as precision, recall and resources used. Based on the experimental findings, the authors argue that the proposed system based on artificial intelligence can be effective for addressing intricate security threats in the critical infrastructure areas, and is versatile.

articleTitle: Identification of Proactive Cyber Threats in Cloud-Managed Internet of Things Systems Utilizing Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Global Conference on Communications and Information Technologies (GCCIT)
abstract: IoT gadgets and cloud computing have revolutionized how we utilize technology. Increasing connectivity and dependence on cloud-managed IoT technology has raised cyber threat attack surfaces. Reactive security methods often fail against increasingly complex cyber threats. Thus, proactive threat identification systems must detect cyber dangers before they occur. ML is used to provide a new paradigm for proactive cyber threat assessment in cloud-managed IoT systems. Data from telemetry devices, user behaviors, and network traffic is analyzed using ML algorithms to identify cyberattack tendencies. The approach proactively identifies IoT security issues to reduce data breaches and service outages. First, the paper examines IoT cyber threats and insufficient security protocols. It then examines how ML methods including supervised and unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, predictive modeling, and threat identification are used. The study evaluates decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks, and ensemble techniques for proactive cyber threat detection. The research uses real-world and simulated IoT data to test the methods. The results show that ML can detect malware infections, unlawful access attempts, and DDoS attacks. The framework's performance is measured by detection accuracy, false positive rate, and reaction time to balance security and usability. In addition, the research covers using cloud-managed IoT security protocols with ML-based threat identification. It addresses data privacy, generalizing models, and ML algorithm scalability in big IoT rollouts. ML techniques can transform cloud-based IoT security, the study concludes. It emphasizes ML models that learn and adapt to stay up with new cyber threats. Further research should investigate advanced ML methods like deep learning and reinforcement learning and create AI models that are easy to comprehend and utilize for open threat identification. ML-based proactive threat identification is proposed in this paper, which adds to Internet of Things security literature. The process it outlines to make cloud-managed IoT systems more cyber-resistant ensures the security and reliability of all linked devices in the digital ecosystem.
